requirements.title: Bitmap-Based Enablement Check
requirements.statement:
fun {N} C ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (bits : N → Bool), C.presence t bits = true ↔ MaskCheck t bits
requirements.scope: all executors (the mask test of the bitmap executor; the precompiled executor's sparse form is PERF-042)
reading: For every transition t and every bitmap (one bit per place), the presence check of t passes exactly when every input place and every read place of t has its bit set and no inhibitor place of t has its bit set.
quotes: The presence check of a transition *shall* pass on a bitmap exactly when every bit of its needs-mask is set in the bitmap and no bit of its inhibitor-mask is set.
assumes: A bitmap is read as one bit per place (N → Bool) and a mask as the set of places whose bit is set; the needs-mask is the input places and the read places, the inhibitor-mask the inhibitor places (glossary: Needs-mask, Inhibitor-mask, Presence check). Place numbering, word layout and when the masks are computed are CONC-007's and PERF-042's subject. The presence check is a function of the transition and the bitmap only (the type of EnableCheck.presence): it reads no token count, which is what 'bitmap-based' adds to the glossary's Enabled.

The line ranges over every bitmap, not only the presence bitmap of a marking, and says nothing about what a bit means. The parentheses '(all must have tokens)' and '(none may have tokens)' and the operand 'marking' of the formula, which tie a bit to a marked place, are carried by CONC-008, whose lines apply the presence check to the presence bitmap of the marking (glossary: Presence bitmap). Which bitmap the executor passes (the live presence bitmap, or the snapshot of a firing pass, EXEC-003) is not this ID's subject.

This line constrains the presence phase of the check, not the decision the executor makes with it: read alone, it accepts a check whose presence phase is the formula but whose whole check runs a second needs-mask without the read places (a sparse mask out of step with the full-width one). CONC-008 ties the whole check to the presence phase and kills that check (CONC_008_forbids_driftedMask); the two blocks together fix the whole check of every transition that builds (conc004_008_pins_check).

Reset arcs and output arcs set no bit of either mask: a reset arc never gates its transition (CORE-034, second line). The mutant that puts the reset places in the needs-mask is killed (CONC_004_forbids_withResets).

The inhibitor test fails when any inhibitor place has its bit set, not only when all of them have (`(marking & inhibitor-mask) == 0`); the reading that blocks only when every inhibitor place is marked is killed (CONC_004_forbids_inhAll).

The body calls the mask test the 'Enablement check'; CONC-008 makes it phase 1 of the enablement check, followed by the cardinality check and the ν-match check (clash conc-a#10). This block reads the formula as the presence check, the glossary's name for phase 1, and the inserted sentence says so; no existing sentence is reworded. The reading in which the mask test is the whole enablement check is CONC-008's mutant CONC_008_mutant_maskOnly, killed there by AC2.

'The primary executor' is read as every executor (scope): the bitmap executor's mask test is this line, and the precompiled executor's sparse mask test answers what the full-width test answers (PERF-042).

'uses precomputed bitmasks' and 'Each transition has precomputed masks' say how and when the masks are held, not what the check returns, and are not encoded: the line fixes the content of the masks as a function of the transition, and when they are computed is CONC-007's and PERF-042's subject. The reference check refEnableCheck walks the arc lists; it is a witness of what the check returns, not of how it is computed.
Kind F: the formula line is the one functional sentence of the body; the acceptance criteria and the test derivation are all cost criteria, listed below as not encoded.

The body sentence on the cost ('O(1) enablement checking per transition (proportional to the number of machine words needed to represent all places)') is a quality property and is not encoded: the parenthesis reads 'O(1)' as O(W), constant for a fixed place count (clash conc-a#4, D20). It is PERF-002's subject; CONC_004_reference cites PERF-002 for what the O(W) check returns.

AC1 (enablement checked by bitwise operations, not by iterating over arcs) is a quality property of how the check is computed and is not encoded; what the bitwise check returns is the line. The word check of PERF-042 is the bitwise form, and that block proves it answers what the full-width check answers.

AC2 (a transition with 3 inputs and 2 reads needs only 1-2 bitwise operations) is a quality property and is not encoded; the operation count holds for one word (W = 1, clash conc-a#4). The answer of the check for such a transition is the line at CONC_004_nonvacuous, whose transition has 3 input places, 2 read places and 1 inhibitor place.
AC3 (the check is O(W), W = ceil(numPlaces / word_size)) is a quality property, PERF-002's subject, and is not encoded.
The test derivation (constant check time per transition on a 100-place net) is a performance test, PERF-002's, and is not encoded.

requirements.title: Dirty Set Optimization
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (X : TimedNet N),
    (∀ (l : TLbl N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
        InNet X u →
          on fun s s' ↦ R X s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
            ¬Armed s u →
              Armed s' u →
                ∃ t d,
                  l = TLbl.fire t d ∧
                    (t.core.name = u.core.name ∨ ∃ p, ArcPlace u p ∧ Writes t d p)) ∧
      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
          InNet X u →
            on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.fire t d) s', shall fun x s' ↦
              (∃ p, ArcPlace u p ∧ Writes t d p) → Enabled u s'.m → Armed s' u) ∧
        (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
            on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.fire t d) s', shall fun s s' ↦
              (∀ (p : N), ArcPlace u p → ¬Writes t d p) →
                (Enabled u s'.m ↔ Enabled u s.m)) ∧
          ∀ (l : TLbl N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
            InNet X u →
              (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N),
                  l = TLbl.fire t d →
                    u.core.name ≠ t.core.name ∧ ∀ (p : N), ArcPlace u p → ¬Writes t d p) →
                (∀ (v : Reference.Trans N), l = TLbl.reap v → v.core.name ≠ u.core.name) →
                  on fun s s' ↦ R X s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
                    Armed s u → Armed s' u ∧ s'.stamp u.core.name = s.stamp u.core.name
reading: For every timed net X:
a transition of the net that is not armed before a step and is armed after it was armed by a firing, either of a transition of its own name or one that writes one of its arc places;
a firing that writes an arc place of the net's transition u leaves u armed if u is enabled after it, whether or not u was armed before it;
a firing that writes none of u's arc places leaves u enabled after it exactly when u was enabled before it;

a step that is not a firing of a transition of u's name, not a firing that writes one of u's arc places, and not the reap of a transition of u's name leaves the net's transition u, if it was armed before the step, armed after it with the stamp it held.
quotes: *When* a firing or an injected token writes one of a transition's arc places, the executor *shall* re-run the transition's enablement check.
The executor *shall* re-run a transition's enablement check only when a firing or an injected token writes one of its arc places, or when the transition itself fires.

*If* the consumption of a firing, the deposit of a firing or an injected token writes none of a transition's arc places, *then* the transition's enablement check *shall* pass after it exactly when it passed before it.
assumes: A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic: the step that starts a firing completes it, so no transition is in flight. Arc place, Write, Enabled and Armed are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean).

The quoted sentences speak of the enablement check (glossary: Enablement check); a re-evaluation is a run of it, and the lines read its verdict as Enabled: for a transition that has no match specification the enablement check passes exactly when the transition is enabled (CONC-008, its fourth shall sentence), and the transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every transition of the net is such a transition (ruling D30). The ν-match check of a transition with a match specification (NU-020) reads only the tokens of its correlated inputs, which are arc places, so line 3 holds of it as well; it is not encoded here.

A re-evaluation is read through what it decides. The enablement update that re-evaluates a transition leaves it armed when it is enabled and not armed when it is not enabled (TIME-010, TIME-011); a transition it does not re-evaluate keeps the state it had, its stamp included. The step relation shows a re-evaluation only through Armed and the stamp, so the lines speak of those: the runtimes' per-transition enabled flag is the glossary's Armed (a reaped transition has it cleared, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap_backend.rs enforce_deadlines). With reaping the skip is behaviour, not only cost (ruling D6, clash conc-a#6): re-evaluating a reaped transition none of whose arc places was written would arm it again (TIME-013 line 6, Libpetri.deadline_reap_dirty_diverges), which line 1 forbids (CONC_005_forbids_rearmAny).

Line 2 is the first quoted sentence: every transition one of whose arc places the firing writes is re-evaluated, armed before or not, so it is armed after the firing exactly when it is enabled after it (Armed implies Enabled gives the other direction). An enablement update that disarms a written transition that stays enabled, by arming only the transitions that were not armed, breaks it (CONC_005_forbids_armedLost). The reverse index is complete: an arc place is an input, read, inhibitor or reset place (glossary: Arc place, ruling D6), and a reverse index that holds input places only misses a transition whose inhibitor place is drained (CONC_005_forbids_inputOnly). The stamp a re-evaluation gives a transition it arms, and whether a firing restarts the clock of a written transition that stays enabled, are TIME-010 and TIME-012.

Lines 1 and 4 are the second quoted sentence. Line 1 is its half for a transition that is not armed: only a firing that writes one of its arc places, or a firing of the transition itself, arms it; a delay or a reap arms nothing. Line 4 is its half for a transition that is armed: a step that does not re-evaluate it, which is every delay, every reap of another name and every firing of another name that writes none of its arc places, leaves it armed with its stamp. A reap that disarms the transitions sharing an arc place with the reaped one (CONC_005_forbids_reapDisarms), a firing that drops the clock of every transition it does not re-evaluate (CONC_005_forbids_dropClean) and one that restarts the clock of every armed transition (CONC_005_forbids_restartAll) break line 4. Line 4 states only the step from armed to armed: that such a step arms no transition that was not armed is line 1.

The exception 'or when the transition itself fires' is in lines 1 and 4 by name: the transition whose firing it is may be re-evaluated whatever its firing writes (Rust marks it dirty when its firing starts, bitmap_backend.rs post_fire; Java and TypeScript when its completion is processed, BitmapNetExecutor.java). That a transition does not fire from a state in which it is not armed is TIME-010 line 5, and what its own firing does to its clock is [TIME-012]; the reap of the transition itself is TIME-013.

Line 3 is the third quoted sentence, the section's 'only transitions affected by that place need re-evaluation' made a requirement: skipping a transition is correct only if a firing that writes none of its arc places leaves its enablement as it was. A write is the glossary's Write (ruling D6): consuming, depositing, and draining through a reset arc, a reset place that is already empty included; reading through a read arc and testing through an inhibitor arc never write. The section's 'tokens are added or removed from a place' is read as a write: an input arc counts even where nothing would be consumed, and draining an empty reset place counts although no token moves. Line 3 follows from the marking update of a firing ([CORE-022]); it excludes a step whose firing changes a place it does not write, for instance one that consumes the token of a read arc (CONC_005_forbids_readConsumes), under which skipping a transition would leave a stale enablement. Like the sentence, it has no exception: it speaks of the fired transition and of transitions outside the net too.

The third quoted sentence is stated per change of the marking (the consumption of a firing, the deposit of a firing, an injected token), because in all three runtimes an asynchronous action's deposit is made when its completion is processed, in a later cycle than its consumption, with other firings and injected tokens between. One step of R is an atomic firing: its consumption followed by its deposit with nothing between, and a place it writes is a place its consumption or its deposit writes (glossary: Write). So line 3 is the sentence applied to the two halves in turn; the interleaved case is the companion of the executor model (RefExec, W5) named below.
Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10): a stamp is kept per name, and lines 1, 2 and 4 speak of the transition the net holds under the name (InNet).

Injected tokens are not steps of the Phase 1 relation, which has no environment places, and the glossary's Writes leaves its injection clause out: the injection half of each quoted sentence is not encoded by this block. It is encoded with [ENV-003] over the cycle relation of Phase 2 (RefExec), in a companion block of this ID (ruling D33, open). The same companion carries the transition in flight: in Java and TypeScript an enablement update skips a transition whose firing is in flight although a firing wrote one of its arc places, and re-evaluates it when its completion is processed; whether a transition may start again while a firing of it is in flight is ruling D8 (open). Which enablement update performs a re-evaluation (the one of the cycle that takes the write in) is Phase 2 as well.

The evaluation of every transition at the start of a run, in the initial marking, is not a re-evaluation: it is the initial state (TSt.init, [TIME-010]); the runtimes mark every transition dirty once, when the marking is initialised.

The reverse index 'maps each place to the set of transitions that reference it': a transition references a place when the place is one of its arc places; a transition that only deposits into the place does not (glossary: Arc place, ruling D6, clash conc-a#7). The reverse index as a data structure is [CONC-007]; this block states its behaviour: complete (line 2), and sound because unwritten arc places keep their counts (line 3).

The second paragraph (the dirty set is a bitmap, the executor sets the bits of the affected transitions, only dirty transitions are re-evaluated each cycle) is the representation of the quoted sentences (kind Q): no step relation observes a bit or a cycle. 'When a place changes' is read as a write.

AC1 (adding a token to place P only marks transitions connected to P as dirty): 'marks as dirty' is the representation of 'will be re-evaluated', and 'connected to P' is 'P is one of its arc places'; its behaviour is lines 1, 2 and 4, exercised by CONC_005_nonvacuous and CONC_005_nonvacuous_kept: a firing that deposits into place 0 arms the transition with an input arc on 0 and keeps an armed one armed, a firing that writes no place leaves the reaped transition reaped and an armed one armed with its stamp, and a reap leaves an armed competitor armed. AC2 (transitions not connected to P are not re-evaluated) is lines 1 and 4, with the mutants CONC_005_forbids_rearmAny, CONC_005_forbids_dropClean, CONC_005_forbids_restartAll and CONC_005_forbids_reapDisarms. AC3 (dirty bits are cleared after re-evaluation) is representation (kind Q) and is not encoded. The test derivation (50 transitions, exactly 3 re-evaluated) counts re-evaluations, a cost ([PERF-003]), and is not encoded.

requirements.title: Multi-Phase Enablement
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] C ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
    Builds t →
      ∀ (m : CountMarking N),
        (¬OnlyOneInputs t →
            C.presence t (presenceOf m) = true →
              (C.cardinality t m = true ↔ CardinalityOk t m)) ∧
          (¬OnlyOneInputs t →
              C.check t m = (C.presence t (presenceOf m) && C.cardinality t m)) ∧
            (OnlyOneInputs t → C.check t m = C.presence t (presenceOf m)) ∧
              (C.check t m = true ↔ Enabled t m)
requirements.scope: all executors, transitions that build and have no match specification
reading: For every transition t that builds (Builds t: distinct input places, every input arc requiring at least one token, no place with both an input arc and a read arc, a well-formed output spec; no transition has a match specification here) and every count marking m:

if t has an input that is not `One` and the presence check of t passes on the presence bitmap of m, the cardinality check of t passes on m exactly when every input place of t holds at least its required count;
if t has an input that is not `One`, the enablement check of t on m passes exactly when the presence check of t passes on the presence bitmap of m and the cardinality check of t passes on m;
if t has no input that is not `One` (a transition with no input arc included), the enablement check of t on m passes exactly when the presence check of t passes on the presence bitmap of m;
the enablement check of t on m passes exactly when t is enabled in m.
quotes: *When* a transition that builds has no match specification and has an `Exactly(n)`, `All` or `AtLeast(m)` input, and its presence check passes on the presence bitmap of the marking, its cardinality check *shall* pass exactly when every input place holds at least its required count.

*When* a transition that builds has no match specification and has an `Exactly(n)`, `All` or `AtLeast(m)` input, its enablement check *shall* pass exactly when the presence check passes on the presence bitmap of the marking and the cardinality check passes.

*When* a transition that builds has no match specification and no `Exactly(n)`, `All` or `AtLeast(m)` input, its enablement check *shall* pass exactly when the presence check passes on the presence bitmap of the marking.
*When* a transition that builds has no match specification, its enablement check *shall* pass exactly when the transition is enabled ([CORE-022]).
assumes: A marking is read as its token counts (CountMarking) and its presence bitmap as one bit per place, set exactly when the place is marked (glossary: Presence bitmap). The check is the abstract EnableCheck of CONC-004: its presence phase on a bitmap, its cardinality phase on counts, and the whole check on a marking.

'The presence check' in the quoted sentences is the glossary term that CONC-004 pins, so the sentences mean this block and CONC-004 together; the presence phase is constrained there, not here. Read alone, this block accepts a presence phase that ignores the input bits of a transition with an input that is not `One`, since its cardinality phase covers those places (conc008_dropInputs_ok); CONC-004 kills that check (CONC_004_forbids_dropInputs). The two blocks hold together of one check (CONC_004_008_consistent), and together they fix the whole check of every transition that builds to the reference check (conc004_008_pins_check).

Every line speaks of transitions that build (glossary: Builds), as CORE-022 does: a definition that building rejects is held by no executor, so no check is asked of it. Two build checks matter here. IO-002 and IO-004 reject an `Exactly(0)` or `AtLeast(0)` input, which is enabled on an empty place but fails the presence check: without them the fourth line contradicts the second line together with CONC-004 (conc008_unscoped_conflict). CORE-030 rejects two input arcs on one place, which have no coherent consumption semantics: a cardinality phase that adds up the required counts of all arcs on one place answers what the reference answers on every transition that builds, and the block allows it (CONC_008_allows_sumDup).

Phase 3 and AC3 (a transition with a match specification needs the ν-match check, which scans its correlated inputs for a shared name, [NU-020]) are not encoded: the count-level transition has no match specification, and the ν line waits for the ν model (RefNu, wave W9). Every quoted sentence is stated for transitions without a match specification; the lines for a transition with one, and the body item 'This is the only per-token phase; there is no value-predicate phase (guards were removed, [IO-006])', wait for the same line. At the count level no check sees token values, so a value-predicate phase cannot be expressed; the fourth line already forbids any extra phase that rejects an enabled transition.

A transition with no `Exactly(n)`, `All` or `AtLeast(m)` input, including one with no input arc at all (a read-only, inhibitor-only or source transition), is checked by phase 1 alone (third line, AC1). 'Fully checked in Phase 1' is read as 'the answer of the check is the answer of phase 1': computing phase 2 anyway is not forbidden, and its cardinality phase is not constrained. Rust and TypeScript skip phase 2 for it (they build no cardinality check unless some input is not `One`); Java also skips it for an `Exactly(1)` input (it builds one only for a required count above 1, `All` or `AtLeast`); the reference runs phase 2 for every transition, where it passes whenever phase 1 does. All three satisfy the block (CONC_008_reference, CONC_008_allows_skipOneOnly, CONC_008_allows_skipJava). For a transition with an input that is not `One`, phase 2 checks every input place, `One` inputs included, as the runtimes do.

'Phases 2 and 3 are only reached if Phase 1 passes, minimizing work for most transitions' is not encoded as an order of evaluation. The second line is an equation of Boolean values, whose answer does not depend on the order its parts are evaluated in, so a check that evaluates phase 2 first, or always, satisfies it (CONC_008_allows_cardFirst). What the sentence implies for the answer is encoded: the whole check passes only if phase 1 does (second and third lines), and where phase 1 fails phase 2 is not constrained (the first line is stated only at a marking where phase 1 passes; there a skipped phase 2 passes trivially, and that is the right answer because every input place is marked). The order and the saving of work are quality properties. Phase 1's 'O(W) bitwise check' and 'fast reject for most transitions' are CONC-004's and PERF-002's quality properties.

Which marking the phases read is not this ID's subject: in the enablement update the presence phase reads the bitmap snapshot and the cardinality phase the live counts, taken at the same instant; in the recheck of a firing pass (EXEC-003) the cardinality phase discounts same-pass deposits. This block is the function of one marking; the pass recheck is EXEC-003's.

The body names the mask test of CONC-004 the 'Enablement check' and this ID makes it phase 1 (clash conc-a#10). The reading in which CONC-004's formula is the whole enablement check is the mutant CONC_008_mutant_maskOnly, killed by AC2.

With CONC-004 in force, the fourth line follows from the first three; it is kept because this block alone needs it: it makes phase 1 on the presence bitmap agree with enablement for a transition with only `One` inputs, and CONC_008_forbids_cardOnly uses it.
AC1 (a transition with only One inputs and no match specification is fully checked in phase 1) is the third line (CONC_008_mutant_noPhase1Only_killed, CONC_008_nonvacuous).

AC2 (a transition with an Exactly(5) input needs phase 2 to verify the token count) is the first and second lines: with three tokens the presence check passes, the cardinality check fails and so does the enablement check (CONC_008_mutant_maskOnly_killed, CONC_008_nonvacuous). CONC_008_nonvacuous also runs an `All` input and an `AtLeast(3)` input through both phases.
AC3 is not encoded here: it is the ν line of wave W9 (see above).
The test derivation's 'correct enablement' is the fourth line; its 'minimal re-evaluation' is CONC-005's subject.

requirements.title: Opcode-Based Consume Operations
requirements.statement:
fun S X ↦
  ∀ (s : S.σ) (t : Transition),
    (∀ (p : PlaceId), touches t p → S.ok s p) →
      DistinctInputPlaces t →
        bbCanEnable (S.view s) t = true →
          (X s t).inputs = bbInputsBag (S.view s) t ∧
            (X s t).reads = bbReadsBag (bbPostInput (S.view s) t) t.reads ∧
              ∀ (q : PlaceId),
                (S.ok (X s t).store q ↔ S.ok s q) ∧
                  (S.ok s q → S.view (X s t).store q = bbConsumeMarking (S.view s) t q)
requirements.scope: the precompiled executor, transitions without a match specification
reading: For a token store S by place id and a consume program X over it, for every store state s and compiled transition t such that S holds a queue for every place t has an arc on, t has no two input arcs on one place, and t is enabled on the queues of s by the reference enablement:

the inputs X hands the action are the reference's: from each input place the first tokens of its queue, in queue order, as many as the consumption count of the arc on the queue's length (One 1, Exactly n, All and AtLeast every token), and nothing from any other place;
the read tokens X hands the action are the reference's: for each read arc, in arc order, the head of the read place's queue after the input consumption;

after X, S holds a queue for exactly the places it held one for in s, and at each of them the queue is the reference's: empty at a reset place, the queue without its consumed prefix at any other input place, unchanged at every other place.
quotes: *When* the precompiled executor fires a transition that has no match specification ([NU-020]), its consume operations *shall* hand the action from each input place the oldest tokens the place holds, as many as the consumption count of the input arc ([IO-007]) for the number of tokens the firing may drain ([EXEC-003] AC5), in queue order, and nothing from any other place.

*When* the precompiled executor fires a transition that has no match specification ([NU-020]), its consume operations *shall* hand the action for each read arc the head of the read place's queue as it is after the input operations and before the reset operations.

*When* the precompiled executor fires a transition that has no match specification ([NU-020]), its consume operations *shall* remove from each reset place every token the firing may drain ([EXEC-003] AC5), leave each other input place its queue without the tokens handed to the action, leave the queue of every other place unchanged, and hold a queue for every place the token storage held and for no other place.
assumes: The model is a token store S (glossary: MarkingOps, at place ids PlaceId and token values Colour), CONC-022's interface: view s p is the queue place p holds in s, oldest first (glossary: Queue order), and S.ok s p says that s is a well-formed store holding a queue for p. The consume program X maps a store state and a compiled transition (Libpetri.Transition of Basic.lean: input arcs with their cardinality, inhibitor, read and reset places, by place id) to a ConsumeOut: the store after the consume phase and the input and read tokens the action receives, by place id. The tokens a reset destroys are not handed to the action, so they are not a field; that they are reported to the event store is EVT's subject. The right-hand sides are the Bitmap reference executor's consume (Refinement/Model.lean: bbInputsBag, bbReadsBag over bbPostInput, bbConsumeMarking), applied to the store's view, and the enablement premise is the reference enablement bbCanEnable on the view, not the program's own enablement check.

Scope: transitions without a match specification (ruling D30, the consequence of D16 for EXEC-010). A transition with a match specification consumes its correlated inputs by name ([NU-020]) and does not run the input opcodes (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:1146, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:2332-2335, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:1085-1088). The compiled Transition has no match specification, so every transition the statement quantifies over is one the EARS sentences speak of; the ν consume path is NU-020's subject. Each quoted sentence carries the scope in its trigger, and the prose sentence on iterating the opcode array states it as its exception.

The premises are the build-time guarantees under which the precompiled executor fires: every place a transition has an arc on is a compiled place id (the store holds a queue for it; CompiledNet::compile interns every referenced place), no two input arcs of a transition are on one place (DistinctInputPlaces, CORE-030 AC3, rejected at build time; with duplicate inputs the opcode interpreter is not total, canEnable_insufficient_for_totality in RetrodictExec.lean), and the transition is enabled ('fires' presupposes it). Guards are not modelled: input guards were removed from the spec (IO-006), and the guard field of the Lean InSpec is ignored by both the reference and the interpreter.

The statement does not assume ruling D15 (no input arc and read arc on one place, EXEC-012): the reference peeks the reads after input consumption whatever the arcs, and so does the precompiled executor. Under D15, which the build enforces, a read place is never an input place, so 'after the input operations' is not observable on a transition that builds: CONC_021_forbids_readsBeforeInputs kills a peek before the input opcodes only on a transition with an input arc and a read arc on one place, so on buildable nets that half of line 2 is stricter than the build needs. 'Before the reset operations' is observable, for a place that is both a read place and a reset place, which EXEC-013 allows and which CONC_021_forbids_readsAfterReset tests.

Draining opcodes are modelled with no same-pass deposit outstanding (clash conc-b#10, ruling D20). The opcode table and the first and third EARS sentences say 'the tokens the firing may drain ([EXEC-003] AC5)': a draining arc or reset that fires later in a firing pass takes only the tokens present when the pass began, and tokens a same-pass synchronous action deposited survive it (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:1276-1279 and :1300, drainable at :690-695; java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:791). A consume program here sees one firing and no pass, so every token is one the firing may drain, the available count of line 1 is the queue's length, line 1 reads 'every token' for All and AtLeast, and line 3 reads 'empty' at a reset place (the module header of Conservation.lean states the same limit). The deposited case is the Phase 2 executor model's (RefExec, W5) and EXEC-003's. For the same reason a program that also drains the inhibitor places with the RESET tail meets the lines: an enabled transition's inhibitor places are empty, and only a same-pass deposit between the enablement check and the consume could tell the two apart, which is for that model's mutant list.

Line 1 is the first EARS sentence. 'The oldest tokens the place holds, as many as the consumption count of the input arc ([IO-007]) for the number of tokens the firing may drain' is the queue's prefix of length consumptionCount(available), with available the queue's length (consumeCountAt). 'Nothing from any other place' is the bag equality off the input places: a reset place that is not an input place hands the action nothing. CONSUME_ATLEAST taking only its minimum is killed (CONC_021_forbids_atLeastMin), the RESET tail run before the input opcodes, which hands an input place that is also a reset place nothing, is killed (CONC_021_forbids_resetFirst), a RESET tail that hands the tokens it drains to the action is killed at the reset-only place 1 (CONC_021_forbids_resetHandsTokens, 'nothing from any other place'), and CONSUME_N taking the newest tokens of its place is killed (CONC_021_forbids_newestFirst, 'the oldest tokens ... in queue order').

Line 2 is the second EARS sentence: per read arc the head of the read place's queue after the input consumption and before the drain, by bbReadsBag, which adds one head per read arc in arc order. A peek after the RESET tail, the order the Rust precompiled executor had before fix (b) (preFixReads, read_reset_order_diverges in RetrodictExec.lean), hands a read place that is also a reset place nothing and is killed (CONC_021_forbids_readsAfterReset); a peek before the input opcodes is killed as the D15 paragraph says. The sentence presupposes the read place's queue is not empty after the input operations; bbReadsBag hands nothing when it is, which only a read place that is also a draining input place can reach, and D15 rejects that transition at build time.

Line 3 is the third EARS sentence. Its view half is bbConsumeMarking: a reset place ends empty, any other input place keeps its queue without the consumed prefix, in order, every other place (read places and inhibitor places included) keeps its queue. A read compiled as a consuming opcode (AC2: reads do not consume) removes the read token and is killed (CONC_021_forbids_readConsumes), so is a program without the RESET tail (CONC_021_forbids_noReset), and so is one that hands the right tokens but shrinks the ring from its tail, leaving the input place its newest tokens removed instead of its oldest (CONC_021_forbids_tailShrink, 'its queue without the tokens handed to the action'). Its S.ok half is 'hold a queue for every place the token storage held and for no other place', both directions of the frame condition that lets one firing's store be the next firing's: a program that hands back a store with the right queues but no places is killed (CONC_021_forbids_forgetPlaces), and so is one that hands back a store holding places, with tokens, that the store before did not hold (CONC_021_forbids_seedPlaces, a lazily allocated pool reseeded from a cached template). Token conservation (the queue before is the delivered tokens, then the reset-destroyed tokens, then the queue after) is a consequence on the places the store holds, token_conservation in Conservation.lean.

Not quoted: the prose sentences 'Each transition's input and reset arcs are compiled into a flat integer array of opcodes.', 'During firing, the executor iterates the opcode array instead of pattern-matching on sealed arc types, except for a transition with a match specification, whose inputs are consumed through the match path (its correlated inputs by name, [NU-020]).' and 'Read arcs are compiled into a separate place-ID array.', and the opcode table. They describe the compiled representation and how firing walks it, which a consume program's observable behaviour does not show: a program that dispatches on arc types and one that runs an opcode array satisfy the lines alike. Only the by-name exception of the second sentence is used, as the scope above. The witness has the structure (compileConsumeOps: the input opcodes in declaration order, then the RESET tail; reads outside it, consumeForFiring_eq_program, cited by conc021_program). The u32 encoding and the pc walk are not modelled (Compile.lean header).

The witness is the Rust ring pool. The Java precompiled executor keeps rings too; the TypeScript one keeps a plain array per place (clash conc-b#5, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:179). The statement is over CONC-022's store interface and reads the store through its view, so a consume program over an array store is in its domain alike. CONC_021_ringMarking shows the reference over core070_ringMarking, the store of the consistency theorem spec_consistent_queue.

AC1 (each transition has a precompiled consume operation array) and AC2's first half (read arcs compiled into a separate place-ID array) are the compiled representation, kind Q, not lines; the witness's compileConsumeOps has that shape (conc021_program). AC2's second half (reads do not consume) is line 3 at a read place (CONC_021_forbids_readConsumes).

AC3 (firing iterates the opcode array without type dispatch, except for a transition with a match specification, whose inputs are consumed through the match path, its correlated inputs by name) is a cost and structure criterion, kind Q, not a line; its by-name exception is the scope assumption above.

AC4 (all five opcodes produce the same observable behaviour as the corresponding arc types) is the three lines: the right-hand sides are the reference arc semantics, and CONC_021_nonvacuous runs one transition with all five opcodes (One, Exactly 2, All, AtLeast 2, two resets), two read arcs and an inhibitor arc. The test derivation (compile a net with all arc types, fire, compare with the bitmap executor) is the same example; over whole runs on the untimed immediate synchronous fragment the comparison is precompiled_refines_bitmap_immediate (Refinement.lean), which cites CONC-021.
The Kind line is F, the kind of its one block (ruling D21: one letter); the structure sentences are Q content without a line.

requirements.title: Flat-Array Token Storage
requirements.statement:
fun S ↦
  (∀ (n : PlaceId), ∃ s, ∀ p < n, S.ok s p) ∧
    (∀ (s : S.σ) (p : PlaceId) (x : Colour),
        S.ok s p →
          S.view (S.add s p x) p = S.view s p ++ [x] ∧
            ∀ (q : PlaceId),
              S.ok s q →
                S.ok (S.add s p x) q ∧ (q ≠ p → S.view (S.add s p x) q = S.view s q)) ∧
      (∀ (s : S.σ) (p : PlaceId),
          S.ok s p →
            Marked (Counts (S.view s)) p →
              (S.removeFirst s p).1 = Head (S.view s) p ∧
                S.view (S.removeFirst s p).2 p = (S.view s p).tail ∧
                  ∀ (q : PlaceId),
                    S.ok s q →
                      S.ok (S.removeFirst s p).2 q ∧
                        (q ≠ p → S.view (S.removeFirst s p).2 q = S.view s q)) ∧
        (∀ (s : S.σ) (p : PlaceId), S.ok s p → S.peek s p = Head (S.view s) p) ∧
          ∀ (s : S.σ) (p : PlaceId), S.ok s p → S.count s p = Counts (S.view s) p
reading: For a token store S by place id:
for every number n, some state of S holds a queue for each of the place ids below n;
and for every state s of S and place p for which s is a well-formed store holding a queue for p (S.ok s p):
adding a token x to p appends x at the tail of p's queue; every place q the store held a queue for still has one, and every such q other than p keeps its queue;

if p is marked, removing the first token of p returns the head of p's queue and leaves p its queue without the head, in order; every place q the store held a queue for still has one, and every such q other than p keeps its queue;
peeking p returns the head of p's queue, which is nothing when p's queue is empty;
the count of p is the length of p's queue.
quotes: The precompiled executor's token storage *shall* hold a dedicated queue for each place of the net it is built for.

*When* a token is added to a place the token storage holds a queue for, the token storage *shall* append it at the tail of the place's queue whatever the capacity of the place's storage, *shall* keep holding a queue for every place it held, and *shall* leave the queue of every other place unchanged.

*When* the first token of a marked place the token storage holds a queue for is removed, the token storage *shall* return the head of the place's queue, keep the rest of that queue in queue order, keep holding a queue for every place it held, and leave the queue of every other place unchanged.

*When* the first token of a place the token storage holds a queue for is read without removing it, the token storage *shall* return the head of the place's queue, or nothing when the place is not marked.
The token storage *shall* report as the token count of a place it holds a queue for the length of the place's queue.
assumes: The model is a token store by place id (glossary: MarkingOps, at place ids PlaceId and token values Colour). Its state type is σ; view s p is the queue place p holds in s, oldest token first (glossary: Queue order); ok s p says that s is a well-formed store that holds a queue for p. A store whose places are fixed when the net is compiled (the ring pool sized per place id) holds queues for those places only, so lines 2 to 5 are stated at the places the store holds, as the quoted sentences are ('a place the token storage holds a queue for').

Line 1 is the first quoted sentence. The interface has no net, so 'each place of the net it is built for' is read on place ids: a compiled net of n places numbers them 0 to n - 1 (CONC-020; which name gets which id, and where tokens on a place outside the net go, are CONC-020's and CORE-072's subject), and line 1 asks for a state holding a queue for each of them, for every n. It rules out a store with no well-formed state (CONC_022_forbids_noPlace) and a store that holds a queue for one place only, which satisfies lines 2 to 5 with their frame halves empty (CONC_022_mutant_heldFree_killed). It does not say that the state is empty, nor that it is the state an executor starts from: the interface has no constructor for the store of a net, so neither can be stated (see the ok assumption below).

The scope is the precompiled executor's token storage: the section stands under the heading 'Precompiled Flat-Array Executor', and the first quoted sentence names it; the later sentences say 'the token storage' for the same storage. The Bitmap reference executor's marking is CORE-070's subject, over the same interface.

Which states are ok is the implementation's choice, made by its refinement to its runtime, and the statement only constrains ok states. A store can therefore hide a fault by leaving out of ok every state it fails on, provided the states it keeps are closed under the operations: a ring pool whose growth (new capacity cap + cap / 2) leaves a ring of capacity 1 at capacity 1, with ok asking every ring to have capacity 2 or more, satisfies the block (CONC_022_allows_noGrowCap1) although it loses a token on the capacity-1 ring that the reference grows (conc022_noGrowCap1_wrong). The reference's ok (Pool.WF and a place id below nplaces) is the widest one: it holds every well-formed pool, capacity-1 rings included, and conc022_fullPool shows such a ring grow. The Rust runtime starts every ring at capacity 4 and doubles it (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:34, 162, grow_ring_static at :1412). Closing the gap needs the store an executor starts from in the interface (a constructor of MarkingOps, a glossary change) or in the executor model (CONC-025's Materialiser, RefExec in W5); neither is in this block.
Token values are Colour (a natural number). No line inspects a value, so the choice of value type does not matter; it is fixed because the witness, the ring pool, stores Colour.

The two prose sentences of the section ('Token storage uses ring buffers indexed by place ID for O(1) access.' and 'Each place has a dedicated ring buffer that preserves FIFO ordering [CORE-013] and grows dynamically when capacity is exceeded.') are not quoted. Their behaviour is the five shall sentences: 'indexed by place ID' is the store being addressed by place id, 'each place has a dedicated' buffer is line 1 with the frame halves of lines 2 and 3, 'preserves FIFO ordering' is lines 3 and 4 (AC2), 'grows dynamically when capacity is exceeded' is line 2 whatever the capacity. 'Ring buffer', 'grows dynamically' as a mechanism, and 'O(1)' are data structure and cost (kind Q): any unbounded store meets line 2 without growing, and the TypeScript precompiled executor keeps a plain array per place (typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:179) and removes the head with Array.shift, while Rust and Java keep ring buffers. How that wording is migrated is ruling D20 (clash conc-b#5, recommendation CB-4, decided (a)); the block is written against the behaviour, which every runtime has, so the wording edit does not change it. The section's Kind line is F, the kind of its one block, following the one-letter convention of the signed blocks (spec/04-execution-model.md:41, EXEC-002, Kind F with Q content); whether the Kind line changes for Q content is ruling D21, decided (a): one Kind letter per ID, with the matrix showing it.

Line 2 is the second quoted sentence. 'Whatever the capacity of the place's storage' is the growth of AC3: the store accepts the add at a full place too, and the token lands at the tail with every earlier token in order; the line does not test fullness, it holds at every capacity. 'Keep holding a queue for every place it held' is the S.ok conjunct, which keeps a bounded store from escaping the line by making ok false at a full place. A ring that never grows overwrites its oldest token (CONC_022_forbids_noGrow), and a growth that copies the ring from the start of its block instead of from its head reorders a wrapped ring (CONC_022_forbids_badGrow). The frame half ('leave the queue of every other place unchanged') is the section's 'dedicated' buffer: one queue shared by all places violates it (CONC_022_forbids_shared), and so does a growth in place whose new slots run on into the next place's block (CONC_022_forbids_inPlaceGrow).

Lines 2 and 3 are stated at a place the store holds, frame half included: an add or a removal at a place id the store does not hold is not constrained, and may change any queue. The quoted sentences say the same ('a place the token storage holds a queue for'). The ring model needs this: its fields are total functions, and Pool.addLast at a place id at or above nplaces grows into a block that may overlap a held place's. No runtime makes that call: Rust routes a token on a place outside the net to extra_marking (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:1331), and ring_add_last indexes place_offset by the place id, which panics out of range. Where such a token goes is CORE-072's subject.

Line 3 is the third quoted sentence, stated for a marked place (glossary: Marked) on the count of the view. Removing the first token of an unmarked place is not a call the precompiled executor makes (ring_remove_first unwraps the head slot, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:396-403, and the ring pool's well-formedness does not survive a removal at count zero), so it is left out; what a marking does there is CORE-070's subject. A LIFO removal is the mutant CONC_022_mutant_lifo.

Line 3 is about the storage operation that removes the first token, not about which tokens a firing consumes. Which tokens a firing consumes is EXEC-010's subject (oldest first, except on a correlated ν input, ruling D16); a correlated ν input removes the first matching token through a different operation (ring_remove_matching, Libpetri.Pool.removeMatching in Ring.lean), which this interface does not have. Ruling D30 (a), recommendation CB-3, is decided: AC2's text now carries D16's exclusion ('except on a correlated input of a match specification, [NU-020]'). Line 3 is the storage operation, not the consumption order of a firing, so no formula changes.

Line 4 is the fourth quoted sentence: the token storage reads a place's first token (the read arc's peek, glossary Queue order 'reads the head') without changing the store; peek takes the state and returns only a token, so it changes nothing by its type. On an unmarked place the head of the queue is nothing (glossary Head), which is the sentence's 'or nothing when the place is not marked'. A peek of the newest token violates the line (CONC_022_forbids_peekNewest), and so does a peek that returns a default token on an empty place (CONC_022_forbids_peekDefault).
Line 5 is the fifth quoted sentence, on the glossary's Token count of the view. A count that reports only whether the place is marked violates it (CONC_022_forbids_presenceCount).

AC1 (token access is O(1) by place ID, no hashing or map lookup) is cost, kind Q, and is not encoded: the statement only fixes that the store is addressed by place id. AC1 is false of the TypeScript precompiled executor's removal (Array.shift on a plain array, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:1098) and of tokens on places the compiled net does not know, which TypeScript keeps in a map keyed by name (unknownPlaceTokens, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:181-188, CORE-072); the wording is D20's.

AC2 (FIFO ordering is preserved, oldest token consumed first, except on a correlated input of a match specification, [NU-020]) is lines 3 and 4, together with line 2's tail append: a token added later is removed and read later (CONC_022_nonvacuous). The ν exception is the line 3 assumption above: a correlated input removes through ring_remove_matching, an operation this interface does not have.

AC3 (ring buffers grow dynamically when capacity is exceeded) is line 2 at a full place (CONC_022_nonvacuous: a full wrapped ring of capacity 2 takes a third token in order; CONC_022_nonvacuous_frame: a full ring grows next to another place's block and that place keeps its queue).
AC4 (token count per place is available in O(1)) is line 5; the cost is kind Q, not encoded.
The test derivation (add and consume tokens in various orders, verify FIFO ordering and counts) is CONC_022_nonvacuous and CONC_022_nonvacuous_frame on the ring pool.

The section depends on CORE-013 (token FIFO ordering). Both blocks use the glossary term Queue order; CORE-013 states it over the queue firing relation, and CONC_022_refQOps shows that the queue marking the EXEC and CORE-013 blocks step (refQOps, view the identity) is itself a store this block accepts. The consistency theorem spec_consistent_queue puts CONC-022 and CORE-070 on one store, the ring pool with its removal guarded by the count (core070_ringMarking, CONC_022_ringMarking).

requirements.title: Priority-Partitioned Ready Queues
requirements.statement:
fun O ↦
  ∀ (I : ReadyIn),
    ((O I).Perm I.readyList ∧
        List.Pairwise (fun a c ↦ I.prio a = I.prio c → I.clock a = I.clock c → a < c)
          (O I)) ∧
      (¬I.FastPath →
        ∃ blocks,
          O I = List.flatMap (fun x ↦ x.2) blocks ∧
            (List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 > x2) (List.map (fun x ↦ x.1) blocks) ∧
                ∀ b ∈ blocks, ∀ a ∈ b.2, I.prio a = b.1) ∧
              ∀ b ∈ blocks,
                List.Pairwise
                  (fun a c ↦ I.clock a < I.clock c ∨ I.clock a = I.clock c ∧ a < c) b.2)
requirements.scope: the ready order of the precompiled executor, and by AC4 of every backend; on the all-immediate fast path only what both outcomes of ruling D14 share
reading: For every input of a pass, fast path included:
the order holds every ready transition exactly once and no other transition;
two transitions of equal priority and equal stamp come in ascending declaration order;

and off the all-immediate fast path there are groups (a priority and a list of transitions each) such that the order is the groups drained one after the other, the groups' priorities are strictly descending, so each priority level has at most one group, and every transition of a group has the group's priority;
and within each group a transition with an earlier stamp comes first, and of two with equal stamps the earlier-declared one comes first.
quotes: *Where* the net does not take the all-immediate fast path, the ready order *shall* be the ready transitions grouped by priority level, at most one group per priority level, with the groups in descending order of priority.
*Where* the net does not take the all-immediate fast path, the ready order *shall* offer the ready transitions of one priority level in ascending order of stamp.
The ready order *shall* hold every ready transition exactly once and no other transition, on the all-immediate fast path as well.

The ready order *shall* offer ready transitions of one priority level with equal stamps in ascending declaration order, also when they were armed in different cycles and on the all-immediate fast path.
Within the same priority, FIFO ordering by enablement time is preserved.

Feeding a level's queue in declaration order is NOT sufficient: transitions enabled in different cycles must drain in enablement order even when it disagrees with declaration order, and equal enablement timestamps break by ascending declaration order — the identical order [EXEC-002] AC3/AC4 requires of every backend.
assumes: The model is EXEC-002's ordering function O from the inputs of one pass (ReadyIn: the transitions numbered in declaration order, their priorities, timings and stamps, and which are ready) to the list of ready transitions in the order the pass offers them for firing. A group of the formula is the content of one priority level's ready queue when the pass drains it; the formula does not model the queues, only the order they produce. Ready and stamp are the glossary terms (Armed, Ready, [TIME-010]); which transitions are ready and which reading becomes a stamp are EXEC-002's and TIME-010's inputs, free here.

The first quoted sentence is line 3 ('the ready transitions grouped by priority level' together with line 1: each ready transition in exactly one group, nothing else; 'at most one group per priority level, with the groups in descending order of priority' is the strictly descending group priorities). Levels that hold no ready transition need no group. It restates the body sentence 'Transition selection scans priority levels in descending order and picks the first non-empty queue, giving O(L) selection where L is the number of distinct priority levels (typically 1–3).' as far as the order of one pass shows it: 'picks the first non-empty queue' is read as the selection of the next transition, repeated until every queue is drained, not as a pass that offers the highest level only (conc023_topOnly is forbidden by line 1). Re-selection after a firing of the same pass has changed which transitions are ready is the executor's pass model (EXEC-001, EXEC-003), a Phase 2 behaviour line over RefExec, not this block; the test derivation's 'fire in correct priority order' is likewise checked as offer order. The selection cost O(L) is not encoded.

The second quoted sentence is line 4, which states it inside one group together with line 2 (equal priority holds inside a group), so that the groups are Sched.lean's LevelBlocks. The third quoted sentence is line 1 and the fourth is line 2, both on every input. 'Also when they were armed in different cycles': the interface has no cycle, the stamp is all a pass reads of the arming, and the firing clock's readings 'never decrease and may repeat' (glossary Firing clock, GlossaryTime ClockReading), so two transitions armed in different cycles can share a stamp, and line 2 then gives declaration order (conc023_Irep_forced).

AC4's first two sentences (quoted) are line 4 with line 2: within a level, stamp ascending, then declaration order ascending. 'Enablement time' and 'enablement timestamp' are the stamp, and 'enablement order' is stamp order. 'Transitions enabled in different cycles must drain in enablement order even when it disagrees with declaration order' is line 4 on two stamps that differ; on two stamps that are equal although the cycles differ, the clause 'equal enablement timestamps break by ascending declaration order' governs, as the fourth quoted sentence says. Rewording AC4's 'transitions enabled in different cycles' to 'transitions with different stamps' is an editorial edit that waits for the open ruling D20. 'Feeding a level's queue in declaration order is NOT sufficient' is the mutant exec002_tidOrder (each level in declaration order), killed by line 4 (CONC_023_mutant_tid_killed). 'The identical order [EXEC-002] AC3/AC4 requires of every backend' is CONC_023_iff_EXEC_002: the block holds exactly when EXEC-002 holds.

AC4's third sentence, 'The all-immediate single-priority fast path is exempt: it bypasses the ready queues and fires in declaration order, which [EXEC-002] AC4 requires of every backend alike.', is encoded by the premise 'not the all-immediate fast path' on lines 3 and 4 (ReadyIn.FastPath, EXEC-002's condition, which is the condition all three runtimes test), and by lines 1 and 2 on the fast path. Which order the fast path uses when stamps differ is EXEC-002's subject and the open ruling D14's: both outcomes, declaration order and the general sort, satisfy lines 1 and 2 (CONC_023_D14_neutral), and a fast path that offers only the first ready transition, offers transitions that are not ready, or reverses a tie is killed (CONC_023_mutant_generalOnly_killed, CONC_023_forbids_allFast, CONC_023_forbids_revFast).

AC1 (distinct priority levels precomputed and sorted descending) is a property of the precompiled program's data (the priority-level array built at compile time), kind Q, inspected in the runtimes; its observable consequence is line 3, whose strictly descending group priorities are the sorted distinct levels that hold a ready transition. The body sentence 'Distinct priority values are sorted descending at compile time.' is the same as AC1. 'Each transition maps to a priority index for O(1) ready-queue insertion.' is data layout and cost, kind Q, not encoded.

AC2 (each priority level has a separate FIFO queue) and AC3 (selection is O(L) in the number of distinct priority levels), and the body sentence 'Each priority level has its own FIFO queue.', are structure and cost, not encoded. As written they disagree with AC4 and with the runtimes (clash conc-b#6): a FIFO queue fed from the enablement bitmap gives declaration order, which AC4 calls not sufficient, so Rust and Java sort each level's queue by stamp and declaration order on every pass and TypeScript sorts one buffer. Their rewording waits for the open ruling D20 and is out of this block; lines 2 and 4 state the order the queues must deliver whatever their structure, so until D20 the quoted sentences are the binding ones.

The test derivation (three priority levels; priority order across levels, FIFO within each level) is checked by CONC_023_nonvacuous on conc023_I5: priorities 3, 2 and 1, with two transitions of the lowest level armed in the order opposite to their declaration and two with equal stamps.

Form: the quoted sentences use 'shall' inside a SHOULD requirement, as IO-016 and TIME-015 do. The SHOULD is the queue structure; the order the sentences state is required of every backend by EXEC-002 (MUST), so 'shall' is true whether or not a backend keeps per-level queues.

Equivalence: line 1 to line 4 together are the same as EXEC-002's three lines (CONC_023_iff_EXEC_002; off the fast path, the order is a permutation of the ready transitions strictly sorted by EXEC-002's canonical key, the hard direction being conc023_blocks_of_sorted). That the precompiled backends compute the drain is Q evidence: collect_ready_general_refines (Sched.lean) shows that a drain of level blocks of the ready set equals the reference's sort, and precompiled_refines_bitmap_immediate (Refinement.lean) covers the immediate fragment.

requirements.title: Precomputed Timing Arrays
requirements.statement:
fun K C ↦
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (tm : ℕ → Novel.TimedScg.Timing),
    (∀ i < n,
        (C n tm).earliest i = K.earliest (tm i) ∧
          (C n tm).hasDeadline i = K.hasDeadline (tm i)) ∧
      (∀ i < n, K.hasDeadline (tm i) = true → (C n tm).latest i = K.latest (tm i)) ∧
        ((C n tm).allImmediate = true ↔ ∀ i < n, tm i = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.immediate) ∧
          ((C n tm).anyDeadlines = true ↔ ∃ i < n, K.hasDeadline (tm i) = true)
requirements.scope: the precompiled net of every implementation
reading: For every timing contract K (the accessors of TIME-001) and every net of n transitions whose timings, by transition id, are tm:
for every transition id i below n, the earliest entry is K's earliest() of tm i (in K's unit, milliseconds) and the deadline flag is K's hasDeadline() of tm i;
for every transition id i below n with K's hasDeadline() of tm i true, the latest entry is K's latest() of tm i (in K's unit);
allImmediate is true exactly when tm i is Immediate for every i below n;
anyDeadlines is true exactly when K's hasDeadline() of tm i is true for some i below n.
quotes: *When* a net is precompiled, the timing arrays *shall* hold, for each transition, the `earliest()` of its timing in the array's unit and the `hasDeadline()` of its timing ([TIME-001]).
*When* a net is precompiled, the timing arrays *shall* hold, for each transition whose timing's `hasDeadline()` is true, the `latest()` of its timing in the array's unit.
*When* a net is precompiled, `allImmediate` *shall* be true exactly when every transition of the net has the timing `Immediate`.
*When* a net is precompiled, `anyDeadlines` *shall* be true exactly when some transition of the net has a timing whose `hasDeadline()` is true.
assumes: A timing compiler maps the number n of a net's transitions and the timing of each transition, by declaration index (the transition id of the precompiled net), to a timing table: an earliest entry, a latest entry and a deadline flag per transition id, and the two global flags. Entries at an id of n or more are not read and no line constrains them. Timing, enablement and the marking at run time play no part: the table is a function of the timings alone.

The entries are stated through the accessors of a timing contract K of TIME-001, not through Timing.earliest directly: this block says the table holds what the accessors return, TIME-001 says what they return. A joint model satisfies TIME_001 K and CONC_024 K C with the same K, and conc024_skipDeadlines needs both. Bounds are naturals in milliseconds, as in TIME-001.

The bullet list names a nanosecond and a millisecond array for each bound, and the body sentence 'Millisecond arrays are precomputed to avoid nanosecond-to-millisecond division on the hot path.' and AC4 (the millisecond values match the nanosecond values within rounding) concern that pair. Only Java keeps both units; Rust and TypeScript keep milliseconds only (clash conc-b#7). The block states one entry per bound in the contract's unit (milliseconds), which is what the quoted sentences mean by 'in the array's unit': Java's earliestNanos[] holds earliest() converted to nanoseconds, its earliestMillis[] the same bound in milliseconds. The unit pair and AC4 are a layout property of the Java runtime (Q) and no line encodes them; the wording that makes the bullet list unit-neutral waits for ruling D20, and until then those bullets, the body sentence and AC4 stay normative prose that only Java meets.

'MAX_VALUE if no deadline' is not encoded: no line constrains the latest entry of a transition whose deadline flag is clear, and conc024_noDeadlineLatest_free shows the block accepts any value there, 0 included (a compiler that zero-fills the array and writes only flagged entries, so delayed(5) gets the entries 5 and 0). The runtimes store three different values there (Java Long.MAX_VALUE, Rust f64::MAX, TypeScript the maximum duration, which is latest() of Immediate and Delayed). Each reads the entry only behind the flag: Rust precompiled_backend.rs:1033 and :1395, Java PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:2123 and :2790, TypeScript precompiled-net-executor.ts:839 and :1723. conc024_deadlineAt proves that such a flag-guarded read is the same under every compiler that satisfies CONC-024, so the free entry changes nothing a guarded reader sees. A fifth line 'the latest entry without the flag is no smaller than latest()' would hold of the three runtimes, but it would settle the D20 item (clash conc-b#7, whose recommendation is that the entry is meaningful only where the flag is set) ahead of the ruling, so it stays out; if D20 keeps a fixed value, that line is added and conc024_maxValueCompile 0 becomes its forbids evidence.

The deadline flag is hasDeadline() by variant (ruling D2, TIME-001 line 3): Exact has the flag although it is enforced softly and never reaped (TIME-006, TIME-013). A flag read off the bounds (latest below the maximum duration) is killed as CONC_024_forbids_latestBelowMax on window(0, maximum). The separate Exact flag every runtime keeps is not in the spec's list and is not encoded.

AC1 (populated at compile time, not computed per cycle) and the purpose 'to avoid virtual dispatch on timing types during execution' are cost and layout (Q), and no line encodes them. That a compiler is a function of n and the timings alone is the model's typing, not a checked property: it cannot tell a runtime that fills the table once from one that refills it every cycle.

Line 3 tests the variant (tm i is Immediate) while lines 1, 2 and 4 go through K, because the quoted sentence names the variant `Immediate` and the contract has no accessor for it. The two bases agree in a joint model: conc024_flags_exclusive proves that under TIME_001 K the flags allImmediate and anyDeadlines are never both set.

The bullets 'true if all transitions are immediate' and 'true if any transition has a deadline' state only the direction that makes the flag set; the quoted 'exactly when' sentences add the converse and fix the reading of 'immediate' as the variant (so delayed(0) does not count). The bullets themselves are left as written: rewording them is a D20 item. Both directions are killed when violated: the unsafe one by CONC_024_forbids_earliestZero, CONC_024_forbids_noDeadlineImmediate and CONC_024_mutant_reapable, the conservative one (allImmediate stuck false, anyDeadlines stuck true) by CONC_024_forbids_neverImmediate, CONC_024_forbids_alwaysDeadlines and CONC_024_mutant_safeDirection.

AC2 (allImmediate allows skipping timing checks entirely for immediate-only nets) is line 3, and conc024_skipTiming shows why the skip is sound: when the flag is set, every transition of the net is Ready exactly when it is Armed, so the checks of the earliest and the latest bound decide nothing. The flag read off the earliest bounds (a Deadline net then skips its deadline) is killed as CONC_024_mutant_earliestZero; the flag read as 'no deadlines' (a Delayed net then fires before its earliest bound) as CONC_024_forbids_noDeadlineImmediate.

AC3 (anyDeadlines allows skipping deadline enforcement when no deadlines exist) is line 4, and conc024_skipDeadlines shows why the skip is sound: with TIME-001's accessors, when the flag is clear no transition of the net is reapable, so none is ever Expired and enforcement reaps nothing. The flag read as 'some transition is reapable', which ignores Exact, is killed as CONC_024_mutant_reapable: it would reap the same transitions, but the text (hasDeadline() is true for Exact, D2) and the three runtimes count Exact.

Where a runtime takes the all-immediate fast path, it tests allImmediate together with a single priority level, which is EXEC-002's fast-path condition ReadyIn.FastPath (conc024_fastPath). The link states the condition only; what the fast path does is EXEC-002's subject (ruling D14, open), and the link does not depend on it.

The test derivation (compile nets with various timing configurations, verify array values and global flags) is CONC_024_nonvacuous: a net with one transition of each variant, a net of Exact transitions only, an all-Immediate net and the empty net.
The scope is the five variants of the spec (Novel.TimedScg.Timing). Java's deprecated sixth variant Unconstrained, which Java's allImmediate counts as immediate, is not in the spec and not modelled.

requirements.title: Lazy Marking Synchronization
requirements.statement:
fun S X ↦
  ∀ (s₀ s : X.σ),
    X.init s₀ →
      Relation.ReflTransGen X.step s₀ s →
        ∀ (p : PlaceId), S.ok (X.store s) p → X.mat s p = S.view (X.store s) p
reading: For every executor X over the token store S:

at every state that zero or more steps reach from a state a run starts from, the start state included, the materialised marking gives each place S holds a queue for exactly the queue S holds for it, oldest first.
quotes: The materialized Marking accurately reflects the current ring buffer state.
*When* the executor materializes a Marking, it *shall* give each place the token storage holds a queue for exactly the tokens of that queue at that moment, in queue order.
assumes: The executor is a Materialiser over the store interface MarkingOps of CONC-022 (glossary: Queue order): a state type, the states a run starts from (init: the executor is built and its store loaded from the initial marking, before any cycle), a step relation, the token store inside a state and the marking materialised at a state. A ring buffer is read as the store's queue for a place, S.view, and 'a place that has a ring buffer' (AC3), which the EARS sentence words as 'each place the token storage holds a queue for' in CONC-022's vocabulary, as S.ok. The witness store is refRingStore, the ring pool Libpetri.Pool. The TypeScript precompiled executor keeps a plain array per place instead of a ring (clash conc-b#5, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:179); the statement is over the store interface, so it reads an array store alike. The words 'ring buffer' stay only in the AC3 quote until ruling D20, which would move them to an implementation note.

The fields describe the executor; they are not chosen to suit the line. init holds of every state a run can start from, store is the token storage the firings consume from and deposit to, and step is every move between two moments at which a marking can be asked for. A description with no start state, with steps that skip such a moment, or with a store field that names a copy the firings never touch says nothing about the executor, as for every abstract relation a requirement block is stated over. Under that reading the snapshot hazard is caught: an executor that materialises from a copy of its rings taken at the start is rejected once store is its live storage (CONC_025_forbids_snapshot).

'Current' and 'at that moment' are read as: at a start state and at every state steps reach from it (Relation.ReflTransGen, whose reflexive case is the start state). So a materialisation asked for before the first cycle is constrained (CONC_025_forbids_earlyCache: a cache built before the store is loaded hands out nothing), and an executor that is wrong from the start is rejected there (CONC_025_forbids_seeded hands out every initial token twice, at every state it reaches). A store changed by something other than a step, such as the restore of a snapshot ([CORE-073]), starts a new run, so the state after it is a start state. The line does not require agreement at a state no run reaches: an honest cache whose stale states are unreachable satisfies it.

A step has the granularity at which a marking can be asked for. AC2's occasions include event emission ([EVT-014]), which the shipped executors do after each firing inside a cycle, so a step is one firing as well as one whole cycle. An executor that refreshes its marking only at the end of a cycle hands out a stale marking between two firings and is rejected (CONC_025_forbids_cycleRefresh). The step relation is abstract, so the line constrains no firing rule and needs no fragment limit: it holds or fails of one executor, timed or not. The reference steps are pcCycle and pcFire, the untimed immediate synchronous cycle of Refinement/Model.lean and one firing in it, but the reference satisfies the line whatever its steps do, because it materialises by reading the store, at every state (CONC_025_reference). A step relation of the executor model RefExec (W5) can be checked against the same statement.

The holds proof is definitional: the reference's mat is S.view composed with its store field, so CONC_025_reference is rfl at every state, reached or not, and by itself says nothing about the steps. The behavioural content, that the store the reference reads is the one its firings change and that its materialised marking agrees with the bitmap executor's after any number of cycles, is conc025_matches_bitmap (cited, marking_agreement). Tying the Materialiser's step on its store to the queue firing relation of the joint model, so that store cannot be a copy the firings never touch, is a W5 item for the executor model (RefExec).

S.ok includes the well-formedness of the store (for refRingStore, Pool.WF and a place id below the compiled place count), which the requirement does not state. It is the store interface's reading of 'holds a queue': a store that is not well formed holds no queue view reads faithfully, which is CONC-022's subject. The precompiled cycle keeps the pool well formed and its place count fixed on a compiled net (pcCycle_rel in Refinement), so on the reference every compiled place stays in S.ok at every state a run reaches from a well-formed start. Splitting ok into 'place known' and a separate well-formedness hypothesis would change the store interface CONC-022 is stated over, so the line uses S.ok as CONC-022 does.

Places outside the store are not constrained (clash conc-b#8): every shipped precompiled executor also merges into the materialised marking the tokens it keeps for unknown places (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:880-881 extra_marking, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:1587 extraTokens, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:1767-1771 unknownPlaceTokens), which no ring holds. That retention is CORE-072's subject (AC3 there); the line neither requires nor forbids it on places outside the store. On a place the store holds a queue for it forbids it: a side marking seeded with the whole initial marking, known places included, hands those tokens out twice (CONC_025_forbids_seeded). The editorial rewording of AC3 that names those tokens waits for ruling D20.

AC1 (normal execution cycles do not create or update a Marking object) is not encoded: whether an object is allocated or written is not observable in a state model, so AC1 is a quality criterion, shown by the test derivation (a run with a noop event store creates no Marking until the result is requested), which is not encoded either. That a token deposited on an unknown place updates the retained marking in a normal cycle (clash conc-b#8) is AC1's and waits for D20 with it. The Kind line is B, the kind of its one encoded line, following the one-letter convention of the signed blocks; the laziness of the title and AC1 are quality criteria with no line, and whether the Kind line changes for Q content is ruling D21, which is open.

AC2 (the Marking is materialized on demand for event emission, debug or the result) is not encoded: when the executor materialises is the subject of the requirements that ask for a marking ([EVT-014], [EXEC-041], and the snapshot request of [ENV-014], which the body's list of occasions omits, clash conc-b#8). The line says what every materialisation returns, at whatever reachable state it is asked for.

AC3 is the line. CONC_025_forbids_stale rejects an executor that materialises once and hands out that marking after later cycles (the hazard the TypeScript getMarking docstring names, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:1778-1794; caching outside a run, which TypeScript does, is allowed, since no step runs between). CONC_025_forbids_blockOrder rejects one that reads each ring from the start of its block instead of from its head: it hands out the right tokens in the wrong order once a ring has wrapped, so 'accurately reflects' is read with queue order, as the EARS sentence says.

requirements.title: Optional output validation skip (option enabled)
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
      Builds t →
        ∀ (m : CountMarking N),
          Enabled t m →
            ∀ (d : List N),
              (∀ (p : N), Produced d p → OutputArc t p) → ∃ m', F t m d m') ∧
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N),
        on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦
          ∀ (p : N), Produced d p → OutputArc t p) ∧
      ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
        ¬Builds t → ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ), ¬F t m d m'
requirements.scope: an executor that offers the option, with the option enabled
reading: For every transition t that builds, whatever its output spec (an And, an Xor, or a single Place or ForwardInput leaf), every marking m at which t is enabled and every deposit d that writes only output places of t:
some firing of t from m deposits d.
Every firing of every transition deposits only in output places of the transition.
A transition that does not build never fires.
quotes: *While* the option is enabled, the executor *shall* deposit the tokens an action wrote without validating them against the transition's output spec.
The skip covers the whole spec, its `Place` and `ForwardInput` leaves included: a transition whose output spec is a single leaf is not checked for a write to that place either.
While the option is enabled they do not apply: a firing that ends with its action deposits the action's write whether or not it equals an output branch.
The option skips nothing else.
A write to a place the transition does not declare as an output still fails ([CORE-063]).
The build-time checks of [IO-011], [IO-012], [IO-013] and [IO-014] run when the transition is built, before any executor exists, and no executor option reaches them.
When enabled, output tokens are deposited without validation.
assumes: The model is the firing relation F of one executor that has the option and has it enabled, each firing read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. The action may write any tokens into the transition's output places, so 'deposit the tokens an action wrote without validating them' is read as: every such write is the deposit of some firing (the first two lines). Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036), so several tokens in one place are one more such write.

'The skip covers the whole spec, its Place and ForwardInput leaves included' is why the first line ranges over every output spec: a transition whose output spec is Place(P) also fires with a write that misses P (CONC_026_forbids_leafValidated).

'It also covers the join-relay check of [NU-054] and the multiplicity warning of [IO-016] AC4, both of which run as part of validation.': a correlation name and a diagnostic are below the token-count granularity of the firing semantics; not encoded.

The paragraph naming IO-010, IO-011, IO-012, the per-firing check of IO-015 and the last two firing lines of CORE-036 is a scope: those blocks describe an executor with output validation enabled (their scope strings say so), and this block describes the executor with the option enabled. Theorem CONC_026_scoped shows both hold at once, each of its own executor, and that every firing of the validating executor on a transition that builds is a firing of the skipping one.
