Rep X env m0 is the list of every read, inhibitor and reset arc of X in report order (deadArcCandidates: the transitions in the order X holds them, within a transition its read, then inhibitor, then reset arcs, each kind in the transition's own order), keeping exactly the entries Rep X env m0 holds, each as often as X lists it;
the warning text of a read arc entry (t, p) is the template with kind `read`, the transition name t, the place name p and effect `the transition can never be enabled`;
the warning text of an inhibitor arc entry is the template with kind `inhibitor` and effect `the arc never blocks`;
the warning text of a reset arc entry is the template with kind `reset` and effect `the arc has no effect`.
quotes: The dead-arc report *shall* contain a read, inhibitor or reset arc of a transition of the net exactly when no transition has an input arc on the arc's place, no transition's output spec names that place anywhere in its tree (every `And` and `Xor` branch, the `Timeout` child and the `ForwardInput` target included), the place is not an environment place and the initial marking holds no token on it, and *shall* contain nothing else.

The dead-arc report *shall* list each dead arc once, as its own entry (two dead arcs on one place are two entries), in the order the net holds its transitions (the order they were added to the builder) and, within a transition, its read arcs, then its inhibitor arcs, then its reset arcs, each kind in the order the transition declares those arcs.

The warning text of a read, inhibitor or reset arc of a transition *shall* be `<kind> arc of '<transition>' on '<place>': no transition produces into or consumes from it and it starts empty; <effect>.` with `<kind>` the arc's kind (`read`, `inhibitor` or `reset`), `<transition>` the name of the transition that declares the arc, `<place>` the name of its place, and `<effect>` `the transition can never be enabled` for a read arc, `the arc never blocks` for an inhibitor arc and `the arc has no effect` for a reset arc.
assumes: The model is a pair: a dead-arc report Rep from a net (Reference.Net String: its transitions, in order), its environment places (a predicate on places) and its initial marking (token counts) to a list of entries (kind, name of the declaring transition, place), and a warning text Msg of one entry. The environment places and the initial marking are parameters, as in all three runtimes (`dead_arcs` in the dead_arcs module of the Rust core crate, `findDeadArcs` in typescript/src/core/internal/dead-arcs.ts, `ArcDiagnostics.deadArcs` in Java): an executor passes the environment places registered for the run and the initial marking it was given, the verifier its own initial marking and environment places ([VER-001]). 'Starts empty' and 'the initial marking holds no token' are m0 p = 0.

Places and transitions are identified by name (ruling D10), so a place of the model is its name and `<place>` in the text is that string, written as is. A text that prints some other rendering of the place, such as a Java Place record, is killed (CORE_037_forbids_recordMsg). Java tests whether a place is fed on its Place record (name and token type, the divergence MOD-024 records), Rust and TypeScript on its name; a net with two same-named places of different token types is that divergence and is not encoded. Lines 1 and 2 hold of refDeadArcs at every place type (core037_line1_ref, core037_line2_ref).

Transition order is the order of the net's transition list. That this list is the order in which the transitions were added to the builder is CORE-040's line under ruling D32 (wave W2, RefNetBuild); the W2 integrator may then add a [CORE-040] link to the second sentence. Within one kind the order is the transition's own arc list (NTransition.reads, inhibitors, resets), which is the order the transition declares the arcs in all three runtimes. A transition that lists one place twice under one arc kind declares two arcs, and line 2 lists both, which is the sentence's 'each dead arc once, as its own entry'; whether a builder accepts such a transition is not this block's subject.

The text lines fix Msg on every read, inhibitor and reset arc entry, dead or not, as the third sentence says: the text is a pure template of the entry, and an implementation uses it only for the entries of the report.

The output-spec clause of line 1 is outPlaces: the place of a Place node, both children of an And, both branches of an Xor, the child of a Timeout and the target of a ForwardInput. The source of a ForwardInput is not named by the output spec; IO-014 requires it to be an input place of the transition, so the input-arc clause covers it.

The section's definition is its bullets (ruling D20, clash core-b#1): the lead-in ends at 'is dead when:', because 'nothing can ever put a token on P' is not equivalent: a place with an input arc but no producer, no initial token and no injection also stays empty for the whole run, yet its read arc is not dead, so the report holds nothing for it (core037_gap_nonvacuous). The sentence 'No firing ever puts a token on such a place, …' is a consequence on the reference firing semantics: a dead place is empty in every reachable marking (core037_dead_stays_empty), so a dead read arc's transition is never enabled (core037_deadRead_never_enabled), a dead inhibitor never blocks (core037_deadInhibitor_never_blocks) and a dead reset clears nothing (core037_deadReset_clears_nothing). Reach has no injection step: an environment place is not dead by line 1, and the sentence's 'a host injects tokens only into environment places' is ENV-001's; that the Rust and Python executors accept an injection into a place that is not registered, under a host assumption (ruling D89, clash env-a), is the environment requirements' subject, not this block's.

The executor bullet (one log-message event per dead arc when the executor is constructed, through the CORE-072 AC4 mechanism: logger `libpetri.runtime`, level `WARN`, the declaring transition's name, emitted only where events are recorded and never changing execution) and the verifier bullet (one report line per dead arc, the warning text prefixed with `WARNING: `, no result field and no verdict depending on it) are SHOULD sentences over the event model and the verifier pipeline. They are the second block of this ID (kind B, wave W11: RefEvents for EVT-013, RefVerifier for VER-001) and are not encoded here. Their text 'One message per dead arc, not per place: two dead arcs on one place are two messages.' and 'Arcs are reported in transition order and, within a transition, read, inhibitor, then reset.' is lines 1 and 2 of this block: a report with one entry per place loses an entry line 1 requires (CORE_037_forbids_perPlace), a report in kind order across transitions breaks line 2 (CORE_037_forbids_kindMajor), and so do a report with the kinds in another order within a transition (CORE_037_forbids_resetFirst) and a report with one kind's arcs in reverse order (CORE_037_forbids_reverseWithinKind).

AC1 (a reset arc on a place no transition consumes from or produces into, not an environment place and empty in the initial marking, gives exactly one warning naming the transition and the place) is line 1 and the reset text; CORE_037_nonvacuous checks the test derivation's net (`hub_kill` resets `answer/IN`) and the message bytes of AC1's example; a report that counts a reset arc as consuming its place drops AC1's arc (CORE_037_forbids_resetConsumes), and a text with another reset effect (CORE_037_forbids_resetMsg) or with the transition and the place swapped (CORE_037_forbids_swapNames) is killed. That the warning is one WARN log-message event and one `WARNING:` report line is the B block (W11).

AC2 (the same for a read arc and an inhibitor arc, with their effects) is line 1 and the read and inhibitor texts, checked by CORE_037_nonvacuous; a text that swaps the read and inhibitor effects is killed (CORE_037_forbids_swapMsg).

AC3 (no warning when the initial marking puts a token on the place, when it is an environment place, when any transition has an input arc on it, or when any transition's output spec contains it in any branch) is line 1, the clauses of DeadPlace; CORE_037_nonvacuous checks a seeded place, an environment place, a consumed place and a place only a Timeout child inside an Xor names, and core037_outSpec_nonvacuous a place only an And child names and a place only a ForwardInput target names. Reports that ignore the initial marking (CORE_037_forbids_ignoreInit), ignore the environment places (CORE_037_forbids_ignoreEnv), count producers only (CORE_037_forbids_producersOnly), read only a top-level output place (CORE_037_forbids_topOnly), skip the Timeout child (CORE_037_forbids_noTimeout) or skip the ForwardInput target (CORE_037_forbids_noForward) are killed.

AC4 (the warning never rejects a net and never changes execution, a verdict or a result field): the report is a total function with no failure value, and no line of this block constrains a builder, a firing or a verdict; that a dead arc never makes a builder reject is CORE-040's (W2), and that execution, verdicts and result fields do not depend on the warning is the B block (W11).
The SHOULD priority applies to the requirement: an implementation that reports dead arcs follows the three shall sentences.

The test derivation (a transition `kill` that resets `x`, nothing else touching `x`, one warning naming `kill` and `x` with an empty initial marking and none with `x` seeded; the same with a read and an inhibitor arc, and with `x` produced by another transition's Xor branch) is CORE_037_nonvacuous on the reference report: `kill` with a read, an inhibitor and a reset arc on untouched places, a seeded place, and a place only an Xor branch of `use` names. The event, the report line and their counts are the B block's.

requirements.title: Marking State
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} Ops ↦
  (∀ (P : List N),
      ∃ s, (∀ p ∈ P, Ops.ok s p) ∧ ∀ (q : N), Ops.view s q = [] ∧ Ops.count s q = 0) ∧
    (∀ (p : N), Ops.view Ops.empty p = [] ∧ Ops.count Ops.empty p = 0) ∧
      (∀ (s : Ops.σ) (p : N) (x : T),
          Ops.ok s p →
            Ops.view (Ops.add s p x) p = Ops.view s p ++ [x] ∧
              Ops.count (Ops.add s p x) p = Ops.count s p + 1 ∧
                ∀ (q : N),
                  Ops.ok s q →
                    Ops.ok (Ops.add s p x) q ∧
                      (q ≠ p →
                        Ops.view (Ops.add s p x) q = Ops.view s q ∧
                          Ops.count (Ops.add s p x) q = Ops.count s q)) ∧
        (∀ (s : Ops.σ) (p : N),
            Ops.ok s p →
              Marked (Ops.count s) p →
                (Ops.removeFirst s p).1 = (Ops.view s p).head? ∧
                  Ops.view (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 p = (Ops.view s p).tail ∧
                    Ops.count (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 p = Ops.count s p - 1 ∧
                      ∀ (q : N),
                        Ops.ok s q →
                          Ops.ok (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q ∧
                            (q ≠ p →
                              Ops.view (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q = Ops.view s q ∧
                                Ops.count (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q = Ops.count s q)) ∧
          (∀ (s : Ops.σ) (p : N),
              Ops.ok s p →
                ¬Marked (Ops.count s) p →
                  (Ops.removeFirst s p).1 = none ∧
                    ∀ (q : N),
                      Ops.ok s q →
                        Ops.ok (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q ∧
                          Ops.view (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q = Ops.view s q ∧
                            Ops.count (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q = Ops.count s q) ∧
            ∀ (s : Ops.σ) (p : N), Ops.ok s p → Ops.count s p = (Ops.view s p).length
reading: Let Ops be a store of markings: view s p is the queue place p holds in state s, oldest token first; ok s p says that s holds a queue for p; empty, add, removeFirst and count are the operations.
For every list of places P there is a state that holds every place of P, and in which every place holds the empty queue and has token count 0.
In the designated empty marking every place holds the empty queue and has token count 0.

For every state s holding p: add s p x holds at p the queue of s followed by x, and its count at p is one more; every place q that s holds is still held, and if q is not p it keeps its queue and its count.

For every state s holding p, with p marked: removeFirst s p returns the head of p's queue, leaves p holding the rest of its queue in order, and its count at p is one less; every place q that s holds is still held, and if q is not p it keeps its queue and its count.
For every state s holding p, with p not marked: removeFirst s p returns no token, and every place q that s holds is still held and keeps its queue and its count.
For every state s holding p, the token count of p is the length of p's queue.
quotes: A marking represents the current distribution of tokens across all places.
Internally, each place maps to a FIFO queue of tokens.
A marking *shall* hold a queue of tokens for each place of its net, oldest token first, and the token count of a place *shall* be the length of its queue.
An empty marking *shall* hold no token in any place.
*When* a token is added to a place, the marking *shall* append it at the tail of that place's queue and leave the queue of every other place unchanged.

*When* the first token of a marked place is removed, the marking *shall* return the head of that place's queue and keep the rest of that queue in order, leaving the queue of every other place unchanged.
*If* the first token of a place that is not marked is removed, *then* the marking *shall* return no token and change no queue.
*When* a token is added to or removed from a marking, the resulting marking *shall* still hold a queue for each place of its net.
assumes: The model is a store Ops : MarkingOps N T (glossary GlossaryQueue.lean), the one interface CORE-070 and CONC-022 are stated over. N is the place identity (glossary: Place; identity by name, CORE-002) and T the token, kept abstract: a token's value and created_at are not constrained here, only which token sits where in a queue. view reads each place's queue, so 'FIFO queue' and 'queue order' are the glossary term Queue order; Marked is the glossary term on the count view (count s p not zero).

ok s p is 'the store s holds a queue for p'. The queue marking of the reference (refQOps) holds one for every place in every state (ok is True); a store compiled for one net (the precompiled ring pool, CONC-022) holds one for each place of that net, and only while it is well formed. 'The places of its net' is read as a finite list of places P, so the first line says that every net has an empty marking that holds all of its places (for the ring pool, a pool with one ring per place id up to the largest one, CORE_070_ringStore). The three closure clauses (a place the marking held is still held after add, after a marked removal and after an unmarked removal) are the last quoted sentence, which is the third applied to the marking an operation leaves. Together with the first line they make the third quoted sentence hold of every marking reached from the empty marking of a net by the operations (CORE_070_reach), which is how 'a marking holds a queue for each place of its net' is read: a state the store never reaches from such an empty marking is not a marking of that net, and nothing is claimed of it. Without the closure clauses the operation lines constrain one step from a held state only (CORE_070_mutant_noClosure_ring and CORE_070_mutant_noClosure_map); without the first line's 'every place of P at once' a store whose states each hold one place passes (CORE_070_mutant_somePlace_killed).

The operation lines protect the places q that the state holds (ok s q), which by the reading above are the places of its net; 'every other place' in the add and removal sentences is read as every other place of the net, the places the marking holds a queue for. A place outside the net is not part of the marking and is not constrained. The precompiled ring pool shows why the premise is needed: a place id beyond the pool's place count has no ring, and the pool says nothing about what reading it would show.

The designated empty marking Ops.empty is read at the view only (the second line): it holds no token in any place. It is not required to hold a place. The glossary store refRingStore takes as Ops.empty the pool over no place (emptyPool), which holds no place (core070_ringEmpty_holds_none), because a ring pool is sized when the net is compiled; the empty marking of a net is the state the first line provides. A consequence: a store whose designated empty state holds no place and whose add from that state loses the token is accepted, since adding to a place a marking does not hold is not an operation the spec describes. Tying Ops.empty to the places of a net needs an empty marking indexed by the place list in the glossary interface (MarkingOps, shared with CONC-022), which is outside this block.

The first two quoted sentences are prose that the EARS sentences after them restate: 'the current distribution of tokens across all places' is the first line together with the count line and the closure clauses, and 'Internally, each place maps to a FIFO queue' is the view of each place and the add and removal lines. Across a sequence of operations the queue is first in, first out: from the empty marking of a net, a sequence of adds leaves at each place exactly the tokens added there, in the order added (CORE_070_adds), and a removal then returns the first of them (CORE_070_fifo). 'Internally' does not single out one storage: both the queue marking (CORE_070_reference) and the precompiled ring pool (CORE_070_ringStore) satisfy the block.

The removal lines are read at the view and at ok: removing from a place that is not marked changes no queue and no count and keeps every place held, which is what an observer of the marking can see. Whether the store's internal state is untouched is not claimed. The precompiled ring pool's own removal (ring_remove_first, precompiled_backend.rs:396-403) is a private operation with the precondition 'the place is marked': on an unmarked place it would panic on its unwrap, and its callers check the count first. Its Lean model Pool.removeFirst advances the head index there, which leaves a pool that is no longer well formed (core070_ringRaw_unmarked_breaks). The block is therefore checked against the ring pool with the removal its callers perform, guarded by the count (core070_ringMarking), which is the marking interface (Marking.remove_first in Rust, removeFirst in Java and TypeScript, all returning no token on an unmarked place).

The operations are one step each; a sequence of operations is their composition (CORE_070_reach). Which operations a firing performs, and in which order, is EXEC-010, EXEC-012, EXEC-013 and EXEC-020: a firing's deposit is one add per emitted token, in emission order (refQFire_deposit_adds). Removal of a matching token (the correlated ν input, NU-020) and removal of every token (the reset drain, CORE-034, EXEC-013) are other operations, not stated here; so is peek (EXEC-012, CONC-022), which CORE-070 does not mention.
Who may call the operations (only the orchestrator; actions never touch the live marking) is CORE-071, and the snapshot form of a marking is CORE-073; neither is encoded here.
AC1 (an empty marking has zero tokens in all places) is the first line (the empty marking of a net) and the second line (the designated empty marking).

AC2 (tokens can be added and removed from specific places) is the first line (every place of a net is held by its empty marking) together with the add line and the two removal lines, each of which changes only the place it names and keeps every place held, so any sequence of adds and removals on the places of a net is constrained at every step (CORE_070_reach).
AC3 (the token count per place is queryable) is the count line: count is the length of the place's queue, and the add and removal lines say how it moves.

The test derivation (empty marking, three tokens added to P, count 3, one removed, count 2) is a consequence of the statement for every store, from the empty marking of any net containing P (CORE_070_derivation), which also gives that the token removed is the first one added; CORE_070_nonvacuous runs it on the reference.

requirements.title: Initial Marking
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] I R Q ↦
  (∀ (X : TimedNet N) (m0 : CountMarking N) (now0 : ℕ), (I X m0 now0).m = m0) ∧
    (∀ (X : TimedNet N) (m0 : CountMarking N) (now0 : ℕ) (u : Reference.Trans N),
        InNet X u →
          Enabled u m0 →
            (I X m0 now0).stamp u.core.name = some (ClockReading (I X m0 now0))) ∧
      (∀ (X : TimedNet N) (p : N),
          UnknownPlace X p →
            (∀ (δ : ℕ),
                on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.delay δ) s', shall fun s s' ↦ s'.m p = s.m p) ∧
              (∀ (u : Reference.Trans N),
                  on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.reap u) s', shall fun s s' ↦ s'.m p = s.m p) ∧
                ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N),
                  on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.fire t d) s', shall fun s s' ↦
                    s.m p ≤ s'.m p) ∧
        ∀ (X : TimedNet N) (p : N),
          UnknownPlace X p →
            ∀ t ∈ X.net.transitions,
              ∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
                on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦ M p <+: M' p
reading: For every initialiser I, timed step relation R and queue firing relation Q:
for every timed net X, initial marking m0 and start reading now0, the state I X m0 now0 holds exactly m0, on every place, whether or not the net declares it;

in the state I X m0 now0, every transition of the net that m0 enables holds the state's own clock reading as its stamp (with line 1: a transition of the net is armed there exactly when m0 enables it, and its elapsed time is 0);
for an unknown place p of X, a delay of R and a reap of R leave p's token count as it is, and a firing of R leaves p with at least the tokens it had;
every firing under Q of a transition of X leaves the queue an unknown place of X had before the firing as a prefix of its queue after it: every token kept, in its order, at the head.
quotes: An executor can be initialized with an initial marking that pre-populates places with tokens before execution begins.

*When* an executor is initialized with an initial marking, its marking *shall* hold, before execution begins, exactly the tokens the initial marking puts on each place, whether or not the net declares that place.

*When* execution begins, a transition of the net *shall* be armed exactly when its enablement check passes on the initial marking, with the firing clock's reading at that moment as its stamp, so that its elapsed time starts at 0 ([TIME-010]).
*While* a place is an unknown place, the executor *shall* retain its tokens in the marking, in their order and ahead of any token that reaches the place later, and *shall not* drop any of them.
*While* a place is an unknown place, the executor *shall not* change its tokens when the firing clock advances or when it reaps a transition ([TIME-013]).
assumes: The initialiser I X m0 now0 is the state an executor starts from (glossary: Init): the marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name, for the timed net X, the initial marking m0 as token counts and the first clock reading now0. A step of R (glossary: TRel) is a delay of the clock, a reap or an atomic firing. A firing of Q (glossary: QFireRel) is one step Q t M δ e M' on queue markings, which carry token identity and order. Unknown place, Armed, Elapsed time and Enabled are the glossary terms.

The second quoted shall sentence speaks of the enablement check (glossary: Enablement check), read here as Enabled in the initial marking: for a transition that has no match specification the enablement check passes exactly when the transition is enabled (CONC-008, its fourth shall sentence), and the transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every transition of the net is such a transition (ruling D30). For a transition with a match specification the check also needs a name of which every correlated input holds at least its required count of tokens (NU-020); that case is not encoded here.

Unknown place (glossary): no transition of the net has an arc on the place or names it in its output spec. A net of the model is its list of transitions and a place exists by use, so a place declared through the builder but touched by no arc (CORE-040 AC1) is an unknown place here, although AC3 speaks of 'places the net does not declare' and the runtimes warn only for a place the compiled net does not hold. Lines 3 and 4 therefore cover more places than AC3 names, never fewer, and line 1 is on every place. The places list of a Lean net plays no part in the statement; the mutant initialiser core072_dropInit uses it as the compiled place set.

Places are identified by name here, as transitions are under ruling D10: a place of the model is its name. Java identifies a place by its name and its token type together (the Place record, the divergence MOD-024 records), so in Java an initial token on a place with the net's name but another token type is on an unknown place there, retained, inert and warned about, while in TypeScript and Rust it is on the net's place and can enable a transition. Line 2 therefore arms differently across the runtimes for such a marking; the block does not encode that case, which is MOD-024's divergence, not CORE-072's.

Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10): line 2 ranges over the transitions the net holds under their own names (InNet), line 4 over the members of the transition list, and under pairwise distinct names (NamesDistinct) the two are the same set (inNet_iff_mem).

Fusion sets (MOD-060, MOD-061) are not modelled: a Lean net has no fused members. Initial tokens on a non-canonical member of a fusion set stay on that name, which the built net no longer declares, in the runtimes: the built net keeps no fusion map (the Rust core rebuilds the fused `PetriNet` from its places, transitions, subnet membership and terminals only), no executor knows a fusion set, and Java tells the caller to concentrate initial tokens on the canonical place itself (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/FusionSet.java:36-44; clash mod-c#1). Whether MOD-061 AC2 is restated to match is ruling D54 (W8); line 1 states CORE-072's own text, which the runtimes follow, and does not depend on D54.

Line 1 is the body sentence and the first quoted shall sentence, on token counts: the initial state's marking is the initial marking, as a function on every place, so an initialiser that drops the tokens of an undeclared place (core072_dropInit, the declared-only mutant) or starts from the empty marking (core072_emptyInit) violates it. The quoted sentence says 'exactly the tokens'; the timed state of Phase 1 carries counts only, so token identity and order in the initial state are not visible here. A state with queues is the executor cycle relation's (RefExec, W5), and that a restored marking keeps identity and order is CORE-073's subject (W3).

Line 2 is the second quoted shall sentence: every transition of the net that the initial marking enables holds the initial state's clock reading as its stamp. With line 1 it gives InitArms in full (core072_initArms): a transition of the net is armed in the initial state exactly when the initial marking enables it (the 'only when' half follows from line 1 alone, since Armed includes Enabled in the state's own marking), and its elapsed time is 0 (initArms_elapsed). This is the first case of TIME-010's quoted sentence on being newly armed ('A transition is newly armed when it is enabled in the initial marking'), which TIME_010.lean leaves outside its step relation. An initialiser that holds the marking but arms nothing (core072_noArmInit) violates line 2, and so does one that arms the right transitions with a stale stamp (core072_staleStampInit: the reading 0 while the clock reads now0, as a runtime that seeds its enable times from a zeroed buffer), which the arming-only mutant reading accepts; under it a Deadline(5) transition is expired before the first step (core072_staleStamp_expired) where the reference has it ready (core072_ref_ready). Line 2 does not fix the clock reading itself: elapsed times, which are all that timing reads, depend on the difference between the clock and the stamp, and the clock is TIME-010's and TIME-015's.

AC2 ('Execution begins with these tokens available') is read as line 2: the initial tokens are available to a transition when it is armed on them with elapsed time 0, so its earliest bound counts from the start of the run. No line ties I to R: lines 3 and 4 hold on every state, the initial one included, and that a run starts at I X m0 now0 and that an armed ready transition does fire are the executor cycle relation's (RefExec, W5) and the consistency witness's (Covers in ConsistencyTime.lean), not CORE-072's. The relation that never fires from the initial state is not forbidden here; CORE_072_nonvacuous shows the reference firing from it.

Line 2 does not cover a terminal place ([EXEC-042]): a run whose initial marking marks a terminal place ends before its first enablement update, so no transition is armed (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor_core/executor.rs:385-394). The Phase 1 state has no terminal places; the exception belongs to the executor cycle relation (RefExec, W5) and is not encoded.

Lines 3 and 4 are the third and fourth quoted shall sentences, which restate the first sentence of AC3 ('retained in the observable marking (inert ...) but never silently dropped'). Line 3 is on token counts: a delay or a reap leaves an unknown place's count as it is (the fourth sentence; neither is a seam, so 'inert' means unchanged there), and a firing leaves at least the count it had. Line 4 is on queues over every firing of a transition of the net: the old queue is a prefix of the new one, so every token stays, in its order, ahead of any token added later. The timed state has no order, so the order clause of the third sentence is line 4's alone.

A firing is held to retention, not to 'unchanged' (the test derivation's word), because AC3 lets tokens reach an unknown place through the production seam, which ruling D63 (W3) settles; any deposit appends at the tail (EXEC-020), so the prefix and count lines hold under every option of D63. On the reference the unknown place is in fact unchanged on every step (core072_ref_count, core072_ref_queue), as CORE-035 lines 1 and 3 and EXEC-020 say of a place a firing does not deposit into, so a firing that adds a token to an unknown place is CORE-035's to forbid, not this block's. The injection seam is not a label of R or Q (it waits for RefExec's injection label, W5); lines 3 and 4 name the delay, reap and firing labels and so do not constrain it.

Wrong models of lines 3 and 4: a step relation whose storage keeps only the places the net lists (core072_clearR, the shape of the pre-fix precompiled pool, whose produce_token dropped a token for a place the program does not know; Libpetri.unknown_place_drop cites CORE-072 AC3) one that doubles an unknown place on every delay, as a backend that merges its side map of uncompiled-place tokens into the marking each cycle without clearing it (core072_doubleMergeR, clash conc-b#8; the retention-only mutant reading accepts it), one that rebuilds the store from the listed places on a reap (core072_clearOnReapR, the reap clause) and one that does so on a firing (core072_clearOnFireR, the firing clause) violate line 3; CORE_072_nonvacuous_delayReap shows the reference keeping the unknown place's tokens across a delay and a reap. A queue firing that rebuilds the marking from the places it touches (core072_dropQ), one that reverses an untouched queue (core072_reverseQ; the count-only mutant reading accepts it) and one that rotates it with stale copies (core072_staleRingQ, a ring whose head index moved without clearing its slots; the retention-only mutant reading accepts it) violate line 4.
AC1 (initial marking distributes tokens to specified places) is line 1 (CORE_072_nonvacuous: places 1, 2 and the unknown place 9 hold 2, 1 and 4 tokens in the initial state).

AC3 is lines 3 and 4 for its first sentence. Its second sentence, 'every backend regardless of its internal token storage', is the scope 'all executors': the Lean models are one store, and that the production backend's ring store agrees with it is CONC-022's and CONC-025's subject. Its seams are deferred as above: production into an uncompiled place through a raw output that bypasses the context waits for ruling D63 (CORE-063 errors on a context call naming an undeclared place, and CORE-035 line 1 and CONC-026 line 2 forbid a firing to deposit outside its output places, so no relation of the joint model can witness the seam today); injection into a registered environment place that no arc touches needs RefExec's injection label (W5, ENV-002 AC2 and AC3). The quoted sentences restate AC3's first sentence only and leave the seams to the markdown. Its last sentence, that verification models such a place as one with no arcs whose tokens stay, is VER-001's subject; the Lean side is Novel.Seam.inertNet, which appends an arc-less place per inert place and adds no transition (inertNet_transitions).

AC4 (the SHOULD diagnostic: one WARN log-message event per distinct unknown place per executor, its logger, transition name and message) needs the event model (RefEvents, EVT-013, W7) and the events-wave rulings on payloads (D38) and wording (D20, clash evt-b#4 on the transition name); no quoted sentence states it and it is not encoded. Retention does not depend on it, as lines 3 and 4 show.

The test derivation is AC1 to AC3 on one net: CORE_072_nonvacuous starts from {1: 2 tokens, 2: 1 token, 9: 4 tokens} with 9 unknown, fires once, and keeps the unknown place's tokens unchanged, on counts and as the queue 90, 91, 92, 93; the WARN count is AC4's.

requirements.title: Priority-Based Firing Order
requirements.statement:
fun O ↦
  ∀ (I : ReadyIn),
    (O I).Perm I.readyList ∧
      List.Pairwise I.tieLt (O I) ∧ (¬I.FastPath → List.Pairwise I.key.lt (O I))
requirements.scope: every executor backend; on the all-immediate fast path only what both outcomes of ruling D14 share
reading: For every input of a pass, fast path included:
the order holds every ready transition exactly once and nothing else;
two transitions of equal priority and equal stamp come in ascending declaration order;
and off the all-immediate fast path, the order is strictly sorted by priority descending, then stamp ascending, then declaration order ascending.
quotes: When multiple transitions are ready to fire (armed, past their earliest bound and not expired; see the glossary), they are sorted by:
Priority, descending: a higher priority fires first.
Stamp, ascending (FIFO): among equal priority, the transition armed first fires first ([TIME-010]).
Declaration order, ascending: among equal priority and equal stamp, the transition declared first fires first.
The ready order of a firing pass *shall* hold every ready transition exactly once and no other transition.
*Where* the net does not take the all-immediate fast path, the ready order *shall* offer a ready transition of higher priority before a ready transition of lower priority.
*Where* the net does not take the all-immediate fast path, the ready order *shall* offer, among ready transitions of equal priority, the one with the earlier stamp first.
The ready order *shall* offer, among ready transitions of equal priority and equal stamp, the earlier-declared one first.
The sort above describes the general path.

Equal priority and equal stamp (transitions newly armed by the enablement update of the same orchestrator cycle share one stamp, [TIME-010]): the tie breaks by ascending declaration order, so the order is fully deterministic.
assumes: The model is an ordering function O from the inputs of one pass (ReadyIn: the net's transitions numbered in declaration order, their priorities, their timings, their stamps and which are ready) to the list of ready transitions in the order the pass offers them for firing. Ready is the glossary term (armed, past the earliest bound, not expired); the stamp is the firing-clock reading taken by the enablement update that most recently newly armed the transition (glossary: Armed, [TIME-010]); the field ReadyIn.clock holds it. In the block these are free inputs; ReadyIn.ofTSt reads them off a timed state of the reference step (the state's stamp, glossary Ready as the ready bit), and ClashesTime shows a bridged input reached by the timed reference step. Which reading becomes a stamp is TIME-010's, not this block's. Which of the offered transitions fires is EXEC-003, not this block.

The four 'shall' sentences are the three lines of the formula. The first is line 1. The fourth, on every input, is line 2. The second and third, off the fast path, are line 3 together with lines 1 and 2: since the order holds every ready transition exactly once, being strictly sorted by the key (priority descending, stamp ascending, declaration order ascending) is the same as offering, of every two ready transitions, the one of higher priority first, of equal priority the one with the earlier stamp first, and of equal priority and stamp the earlier-declared one first (EXEC_002_iff_sentences). The three items of the sort list are the same key, item by item.

'All-immediate fast path': ruling D14 is open. The section names the condition: 'When every transition is `Immediate` and all priorities are equal, backends fire straight from the enablement bitmap in ascending declaration order and do not read the enablement timestamp at all — including when two ready transitions carry different timestamps because one was held across cycles while in flight.' On the fast path the block asks only what both outcomes of D14 share: the first two lines. Whether the fast-path order is declaration order or the general sort when timestamps differ is not encoded; both satisfy the block (EXEC_002_D14_neutral). 'This is deliberate, and every backend takes the path under the same condition.' is part of that paragraph and is not encoded either.

AC1 (priority 10 before priority 5) and AC2 (equal priority on the general path, the one armed first, with the earlier stamp, fires first) are the third line; AC3 (equal priority and equal stamp, ascending declaration order) is the second line, on every input. That transitions newly armed by the enablement update of one cycle share one stamp is TIME-010's stamp rule at the grain of a cycle, deferred to Phase 2 (RefExec); in the block the stamps are free inputs, so AC3 is checked on every pair with equal stamps. EXEC_002_nonvacuous checks the test derivation (priorities 5, 10, 5, all Immediate, armed together), AC2 and AC3 on the reference order, and the fast path.

AC4 (every backend produces the identical ready order) follows on the general path: two ordering functions that satisfy the block agree on every input that does not take the fast path (EXEC_002_unique), because the key is total on distinct transitions. 'Stamp order is the general-path order' is line 3. That the shipped backends compute it is Q evidence, cited from Sched.lean (collect_ready_general_refines) and Refinement.lean (precompiled_refines_bitmap_immediate, the immediate fragment). AC4's 'Backends MUST NOT differ in which order they use, nor in the condition that selects it.' is covered only through the one fixed condition ReadyIn.FastPath, which the block uses for every backend; a backend whose own fast-path condition is narrower or wider is visible only where its order then breaks the first two lines or, off ReadyIn.FastPath, the third (a narrower condition that checks only the ready transitions is killed, EXEC_002_forbids_readyFast). Pinning the fast-path order, which would make every condition disagreement visible, waits for D14.

'Fires first' is read as 'is offered first in the pass's order'; with tokens to compete for, the earlier transition takes them (EXEC-003). That a pass starts its firings in this order is a Phase 2 behaviour line over the executor, not this block.

requirements.title: FIFO Token Consumption
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
      ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,
        ¬ResetArc t p →
          on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦
            List.drop (Consumes t (Counts M) p) (M p) <+: M' p ∧
              (M' p).Perm (List.drop (Consumes t (Counts M) p) (M p) ++ EmittedTo e p)) ∧
    ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
      ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,
        on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦
          δ.inputs p = OldestFirst M p (Consumes t (Counts M) p)
reading: For every queue firing relation Q:

for every firing of a transition t and every input place p of t that is not a reset place of t: the queue p holds after the firing begins with the tokens of p's queue before the firing after its oldest Consumes tokens, in their queue order, and it holds exactly those tokens and the tokens the action emits to p, in some order;
for every firing of a transition t and every input place p of t: the tokens delivered to the action from p are the oldest Consumes tokens of p's queue before the firing, in queue order.
quotes: When a transition fires, it consumes tokens from the oldest-first (FIFO) end of each input place's queue.
The number of tokens consumed is determined by the input cardinality's `consumptionCount(available)`.

*When* a transition fires, it *shall* consume from each of its input places that is not a correlated input of its match specification ([NU-020]) the oldest tokens the place holds, as many as the consumption count of the input arc.
*When* a transition fires, its action *shall* receive the tokens consumed from each input place that is not a correlated input of its match specification in queue order, the oldest first.

A correlated input of a ν-net match specification is the one exception to oldest-first consumption: it takes the matched tokens of the chosen name, oldest first among the tokens of that name, so it can pass over an older token of another name ([NU-020]).
Its non-correlated inputs consume as above.
assumes: A firing relates a queue marking before it to the queue marking after it, with what it delivered to the action and the emissions of the action (glossary: Queue order, QueueMarking, Delivered, QFireRel). Consumes t (Counts M) p is the consumption count of t's input arc on p at the token counts of M (glossary: Consumption count, Consume), so 'as many as the consumption count of the input arc' is the length of the prefix both lines name, and the paragraph 'The number of tokens consumed is determined by the input cardinality's consumptionCount(available)' is the same count.

Correlated inputs (ruling D16): the transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no ν-net match specification, so every input place is an input that is not a correlated input of a match specification, and the lines quantify over every input place. The exception paragraph is therefore not a line of the formula: how a correlated input consumes (the matched tokens of the chosen name, oldest first among them) is NU-020's, not encoded here; this block makes no claim about a correlated input, and a mutant that consumed a correlated input oldest first would not be killed by it.

Line 1 is the first 'shall' sentence. It is stated at every input place that is not a reset place, including a place the action also emits to (a self-loop): the place keeps its tokens after the oldest Consumes ones, in queue order and ahead of every token emitted to it, and gains exactly the tokens emitted to it, so the tokens that left it are the oldest. Keeping the kept tokens ahead (a prefix, not only a subsequence) is what makes the consumed tokens the oldest when token values repeat: a place holding 10, 11, 10 whose action emits 10 back would otherwise pass with 10, 11, 10, the newest 10 consumed, which no count or value check can tell from the oldest 10 consumed and the emission put at the head (killed by EXEC_010_mutant_sublist_killed). That the emitted tokens follow the kept ones agrees with EXEC-020's tail append; the order among the emitted tokens is EXEC-020's, so line 1 fixes them only up to order. A reset place is left to line 2: it ends the firing holding exactly what was deposited there (CORE-034). With nothing emitted to the place, line 1 says the queue before the firing is its oldest Consumes tokens followed by the queue after it (exec010_line1_noEmission). The line is exercised by EXEC_010_nonvacuous; a relation that removes the newest tokens from a self-loop place is killed by EXEC_010_forbids_selfLoopNewest.

Line 2 is the second 'shall' sentence: the action receives, from each input place, the consumed tokens in queue order, the oldest first (OldestFirst, the FIFO prefix). On an input place that is also a reset place line 2 is the only line: the consumed prefix is still the oldest, the rest is drained. Line 2 says nothing about what is delivered from a place that is not an input place; the spec is silent there, and this block makes no claim about it.

The firing is the atomic firing of the reference: the counts the consumption count reads are the counts at the start of the firing. Same-pass deposits (EXEC-003 AC5: a draining arc ships the pass-start count, not the live one) need the cycle relation of Phase 2 (RefExec) and are deferred to it; consume_faithful (Conservation.lean) states the same FIFO prefix for one firing on the compiled consume program, under the module's assumption that no same-pass deposit is outstanding.
A transition with two input arcs on one place is rejected when it is built (CORE-030); the model reads the first arc (nspecAt), as Consumes does.

AC1 (tokens A, B, C added in that order; One consumes A), AC2 (Exactly(2) consumes A, B) and AC3 (All consumes A, B, C) are EXEC_010_nonvacuous, with tokens 10, 11, 12 for A, B, C: the reference delivers [10], [10, 11] and [10, 11, 12] and leaves [11, 12], [12] and [].
The test derivation (identifiable token values, fire, check the consumed tokens are in FIFO order) is the same check as AC1 to AC3.

requirements.title: Read Arc Peek
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build Q ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
      NoInputRead t →
        ReadArc t p →
          on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦
            (δ.reads p).head? = Head M p ∧
              (∀ y ∈ δ.reads p, Head M p = some y) ∧
                (List.count p t.core.reads = 1 → (δ.reads p).length ≤ 1)) ∧
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
        NoInputRead t →
          ReadArc t p →
            ¬ResetArc t p →
              on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦ AppendedAtTail M M' e p) ∧
      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N), ¬NoInputRead t → Build t ≠ none) ∧
        (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
            InputsDistinct t →
              InputCountsPositive t →
                firstInputRead t = some p → Build t = some (msgInputRead t p)) ∧
          (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
              ¬InputsDistinct t ∨ ¬InputCountsPositive t →
                Build t ≠ some (msgInputRead t p)) ∧
            ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
              NoInputRead t → Build t ≠ some (msgInputRead t p)
reading: Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg) and Q the queue firings.

For every transition t with no input arc and read arc on one place, every read place p of t, every delivery δ and every emission e, every firing of t from the queue marking M that delivers δ and emits e delivers at p the head of p's queue in M: the first token delivered at p is the head of M at p, every token delivered at p is that head, and when t has one read arc on p at most one token is delivered there;

for every such t, every read place p of t that is not a reset place of t, every δ and every e, every firing of t from M to M' that delivers δ and emits e leaves at p the queue M held at p, identity and order, followed by the tokens e emits to p in emission order (AppendedAtTail);
every transition with an input arc and a read arc on one place fails to build;

every transition whose input places are distinct and whose input arcs each require at least one token, and whose first read arc on an input place, in declaration order, is on p, fails to build with the message msgInputRead t p;
no transition whose input places are not distinct, or one of whose input arcs requires fewer than one token, fails to build with this message, for any place;
no transition with no input arc and read arc on one place fails to build with this message, for any place.
quotes: When a transition fires, read arc values are provided to the action without consuming the tokens.
The oldest token in the read place is peeked.
*When* a transition fires, its action *shall* receive, for each of its read places, the oldest token the place holds.

*When* a transition fires, each of its read places that is not one of its reset places *shall* end the firing holding the tokens it held before the firing, in the same queue order, followed by the tokens the firing deposits there.
*If* a transition declares an input arc and a read arc on the same place, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with
The message is the same, byte for byte, in every implementation.
"The same place" is the implementation's own `Place` equality, as for [CORE-030] ([CORE-002]; name-and-type in Java, name-only in TypeScript and Rust).
It runs after every input-arc check ([CORE-030], [IO-002], [IO-004]) and before the timing check ([TIME-001]) and the output-spec checks ([IO-011]–[IO-014]).
It walks the read arcs in declaration order and names the place of the first read arc whose place is an input place of the transition.
assumes: The model is the pair (Build, Q). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the witness is the reference builder refBuild (glossary: Build-time checks), which runs the [IO-002]/[IO-004] count checks (stand-in message msgCount) and the D15 check after its CORE-030 check and before its output-spec checks; it is the builder of the CORE and IO blocks too. Q is a queue firing relation (glossary: Queue order; QFireRel in GlossaryQueue.lean): a firing of t from the queue marking M, the head of each queue the oldest token, that delivers δ (the consumed input tokens and the read tokens, per place) to the action, whose action emits e (places and tokens, in emission order), and that leaves M'. The witness is the reference queue firing RefQFire. Timing and priority play no part.

Ruling D17: a Q step is a firing whose completion the executor admits and whose produced tokens pass output validation ([EXEC-020], [EXEC-021]), so e is what the firing deposits. A firing whose completion is not admitted (its timeout outcome [EXEC-022], a stop on a terminal place [EXEC-042], an immediate termination [ENV-015]) or whose output validation fails ([EXEC-021], TransitionFailed) is not a Q step, and line 2 says nothing about it; what such a firing leaves in its read places (the queue, plus the tokens [IO-015] already published) is [EXEC-020]'s and [EXEC-021]'s. The witness RefQFire has only admitted, validated firings (deposit ... = some (e.map fst)).

Firings are atomic: line 2 is the firing's own effect on p, with no other firing consuming from p or depositing to p between the firing's start and its completion. In the runtimes an action can be in flight while other firings consume from a shared read place or deposit to it first ([EXEC-003]; ruling D7, live intermediate marking), so the second shall sentence read of the whole interval does not hold of them; which of the two the sentence means is not ruled and is not encoded.

Ruling D15: the third shall sentence is lines 3 to 6. The firing lines (1 and 2) speak only of transitions with no input arc and read arc on one place (NoInputRead), because line 3 rejects every other transition when it is built, so no executor holds one. On those transitions the queue of a read place after input consumption is its queue before the firing (exec012_head_postInput), so the read sees the head 'after input consumption' ([EXEC-013] AC4) and 'the oldest token the place holds' at once; and draining a reset place comes after the peek, so a read and a reset on one place deliver the pre-drain head (line 1 reads M, before the drain; [EXEC-013]).

Line 1 reads 'receive, for each of its read places, the oldest token the place holds' as: every token the firing delivers at the read place is the head of its queue, the first is the head, and a single read arc on p delivers at most one token there, so a marked p with one read arc delivers exactly its head (a firing that hands the head over twice is killed as EXEC_012_mutant_noCount). How many copies a transition that declares two read arcs on one place gets is not fixed by the sentence, so for it the line constrains only which token they are. That a firing needs its read places marked is [CORE-032]'s and [CORE-022]'s; on an unmarked read place line 1 forbids a delivered token (its head is none).

Line 2 is the second shall sentence and 'without consuming the tokens': the read place keeps its queue, identity and order, and the firing's deposits there follow at the tail ([EXEC-020]). A read place that is also a reset place is drained ([EXEC-013], [CORE-034]) and is excluded, as the sentence says. Keeping only the count (a firing that reorders the read place) is killed as EXEC_012_mutant_countOnly, and a read that consumes the head as EXEC_012_mutant_readConsumes.

Lines 4 to 6 are the check order and the named place. The message is msgInputRead, the fenced message with the transition's name and

the place; exec012_msg pins the template byte for byte, and how an implementation renders and

follows its sibling build messages (ruling D15: Java may differ only there). Line 4 names the first read arc, in declaration order, whose place is an input place (firstInputRead), when the input-arc checks that run before it pass: distinct input places ([CORE-030], InputsDistinct) and input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002] AC1, [IO-004] AC1; InputCountsPositive). Line 5 is 'after every input-arc check': a transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, not this one (two input arcs on one place: the [CORE-030] stand-in, EXEC_012_forbids_early; an exactly(0) input arc: the count stand-in, EXEC_012_forbids_beforeCounts). Line 6 says the message names only an input-and-read pair: a builder that also rejects a read and a reset on one place with it is forbidden as EXEC_012_forbids_readReset.

'Before the output-spec checks' is encoded by line 4, which asks for this message whatever the output spec, so a transition that also breaks an output-spec check fails with this message (EXEC_012_before_output). 'Before the timing check ([TIME-001])' is quoted but not encoded: the transition of this model carries no timing (timing is TimedNet's, and TIME-001's builder is a separate contract over timings), so this builder never runs that check, and nothing here tells the order against it apart.

'The same place' is equality on N, read as the implementation's own Place identity ([CORE-002]): N is abstract with decidable equality (the place name in TypeScript and Rust, name and type in Java), and ToString N renders the place's name in the message. 'On every construction path' (channel merge [MOD-021], instantiation [MOD-020], fusion [MOD-061]) is not encoded: Build reads one transition definition, and the construction paths that reach it are the composition model's.

AC1 (read place has tokens A, B; the action receives A; both A and B remain after firing) is EXEC_012_nonvacuous: a reference firing with one input arc on place 0 and one read arc on place 1, which holds 20 then 21, delivers 20 at 1 and leaves 20, 21 there, followed by the token 30 the action emits to 1.
AC2 (a one() input arc and a read arc on one place is rejected with the message, and so are all(), exactly(2) and atLeast(1)) is EXEC_012_ac2, under the reference builder.

AC3 (inputs on a and b with reads declared b then a names b; two input arcs on p and a read on p give the CORE-030 message) is EXEC_012_ac3; the CORE-030 message is the reference builder's stand-in, which line 5 keeps apart from this message.

AC4 (an input on a and a read on b builds; a read and a reset on one place builds) is EXEC_012_ac4 for the witness. The statement asks of AC4's transitions only that they do not fail with this message (line 6); that they build at all is the build-time checks' (glossary: Builds), not this requirement's.

Without ruling D15 a read on an input place could be read as a peek before consumption. That reading (a builder with no D15 check and a firing that reads the pre-firing head on every transition) is EXEC_012_mutant_preFixReads. It is killed by the build line alone: on transitions with no input arc and read arc on one place its pre-consumption peek and RefQFire agree, as D15 intends. The reference builder without the check (exec012_buildNoCheck, refBuild as it was before ruling D15) is forbidden as EXEC_012_forbids_noCheck.

requirements.title: Reset Arc Execution
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
    NoInputRead t →
      (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
          on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun x M' ↦
            ∀ (p : N), ResetArc t p → M' p = EmittedTo e p) ∧
        (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
            on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦
              ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,
                ResetArc t p →
                  (δ.inputs p).length = Consumes t (Counts M) p ∧
                    (δ.inputs p).Sublist (M p)) ∧
          (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
              on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦
                ∀ (p : N),
                  ReadArc t p →
                    ResetArc t p →
                      δ.reads p ≠ [] ∧ ∀ tok ∈ δ.reads p, Head M p = some tok) ∧
            ∀ (M : QueueMarking N T) (e : List (N × T)),
              (∃ p, ResetArc t p ∧ M p = []) →
                Enabled t (Counts M) →
                  (∃ ch,
                      deposit (Consumes t (Counts M)) (OutputSpec t) ch =
                        some (List.map Prod.fst e)) →
                    ∃ δ M', Q t M δ e M'
reading: For every transition t with no input arc and read arc on one place (ruling D15):
every firing of t that emits e leaves each reset place of t holding exactly the tokens e sends there, in emission order;

every firing of t from M that delivers δ hands the action, from each input place of t that is also a reset place, as many tokens as the input arc consumes, taken from the place's queue in M and kept in queue order;

every firing of t from M that delivers δ hands the action, for each place that is both a read place and a reset place of t, a nonempty read bag whose every token is the head of the place's queue in M;
from every queue marking M at which t is enabled and one of its reset places is unmarked, every emission e whose places are a deposit t offers is the emission of some firing of t from M.
quotes: When a transition fires, all tokens are removed from each reset place.
This happens during the firing step, before the action executes.
*When* a transition fires, it *shall* drain each of its reset places ([CORE-034]) before its action starts.
*When* a transition fires, it *shall* consume from its input places first, then peek its read places, then drain its reset places.
*When* a transition with a read arc and a reset arc on the same place fires, its action *shall* receive as the read token the oldest token the place held before the drain.
*If* a reset place of a firing transition is unmarked, *then* the drain *shall* remove nothing and the firing *shall* proceed.
assumes: A firing is one step Q t M δ e M' (glossary: QFireRel): t fires from the queue marking M, delivers δ to its action (the consumed tokens per input place and the read tokens per read place), the action emits e (places and tokens, in emission order) and the firing leaves M'. Queue order, Head, Emitted to and Appended at the tail are the glossary terms of GlossaryQueue.lean. Timing, priority and events play no part. Correlated ν inputs are not modelled (NU-020); ruling D16 excludes them from EXEC-010's oldest-first consumption, and line 2 does not say which tokens an input consumes, only that they are taken from the queue before the drain, so it makes no claim that D16 would contradict.

e is the emission of a completion the executor admitted and output validation accepted ([EXEC-020], [EXEC-021], ruling D17); a discarded, timed-out, stopped or failed completion is not a step of Q. Tokens an action published before it completed ([IO-015]) are not modelled: they land after the drain and survive it, also when the completion then fails validation (ruling D17). Both are Phase 2 (RefExec).

Every line is stated for transitions satisfying NoInputRead (ruling D15): a transition with an input arc and a read arc on one place is rejected when it is built (EXEC-012) and never fires. Under D15 no place is both an input place and a read place, so the 'input consumption, then read peeks' half of the fourth quoted sentence is not observable in a single firing: a read place is untouched by input consumption, and the read sees its pre-firing head whichever comes first. That half is therefore not a line; the halves 'input consumption, then reset draining' and 'read peeks, then reset draining' are lines 2 and 3.

Line 1 is the first quoted sentence and the single-firing consequence of the second and third: the drain comes before the action's outputs land, so every token the action emits to a reset place survives it, and the place ends with exactly those tokens, in emission order. A drain after the action's outputs would leave the place empty (exec013_outputsFirst violates it). The other half of 'before its action starts', that the drained marking is the intermediate marking other transitions see while the action runs (the unquoted body sentence 'Like input consumption, the drain lands in the intermediate marking, so it restarts the clocks of transitions it disables there'), is TIME-012's and the Phase 2 executor model's (RefExec), not a line here. On token counts line 1 is CORE-034's first line.

Line 2 is the fourth quoted sentence's 'input consumption, then reset draining': an input place that is also a reset place hands the action as many tokens as the input arc's consumption count (IO-007) on the pre-firing counts, taken from its pre-firing queue in queue order; a drain first would hand it nothing (exec013_drainFirst violates it). Which tokens they are (the oldest, except for a correlated ν input) is EXEC-010's subject; the queue an input place that is not a reset place keeps, and the tail append of the emitted tokens, are EXEC-010's and EXEC-020's. What is delivered from a place that is not an input place (for instance the drained tokens of a reset place that is not an input place) is not constrained by this block, nor by any other requirement block: the spec has no shall sentence on it, so that the action receives nothing from such a place is not encoded.

Line 3 is the fifth quoted sentence, which is the 'read peeks, then reset draining' half of the fourth: the read token of a place that is both a read place and a reset place is the head of its queue before the drain. The read bag is nonempty and every token in it is that head; how many copies a transition with several read arcs on one place receives is CORE-032's and EXEC-012's subject and is not fixed here.

Line 4 is the sixth quoted sentence's 'the firing shall proceed': an unmarked reset place blocks no firing, so every firing the counts allow (enabled, an offered deposit, glossary Enabled, Consumes and OutputSpec) is a firing of Q. Its 'the drain shall remove nothing' is line 1 at an unmarked reset place: the place ends with exactly the emitted tokens, which is the empty queue followed by them (EXEC_013_unmarked_removes_nothing).

The body sentence 'A token a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same firing pass survives the drain ([EXEC-003] AC5).' is about a firing pass of several firings; a single queue firing has no earlier firing, so it is EXEC-003's subject and the Phase 2 cycle relation's, not encoded.

AC1 (reset place with 5 tokens, all removed) is line 1 at a reset place that is not an output place: it ends empty (EXEC_013_nonvacuous, the five-token place 3). On token counts it is CORE-034's first line (cited on CORE_034_reference).

AC2 (reset place empty, no error) is line 4 and line 1 at an unmarked reset place (EXEC_013_nonvacuous). On token counts it is CORE-034's second line: a reset arc does not affect whether its transition can fire (cited on CORE_034_reference).

AC3 (the reset place is also an input or read place of another enabled transition, whose clock restarts) is read in TIME-012's form and is not encoded here: the queue firing has no clocks. TIME-012 says the other transition loses its clock in the intermediate marking and is newly armed with a fresh clock when it is enabled again; AC3's bare 'restarts' is read as that, not as a restart of a transition that the drain leaves disabled. The evidence is TIME-012's AC3 example TIME_012_ac3 (cited there).

AC4 (reset draining after read peeking; a read arc and a reset arc on one place observe the pre-reset front token; the overall order is input consumption, read peeks, reset draining) is lines 2 and 3; the mutants exec013_resetFirst (draining before the peek) and exec013_drainFirst (draining before input consumption) are killed by lines 3 and 2.
The test derivation's clock-restart check is AC3's and is TIME-012's subject.

requirements.title: Output Token Deposition
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (M : QueueMarking N T) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T))
    (M' : QueueMarking N T),
    Q t M δ e M' →
      ∃ base,
        (∀ (p : N), AppendedAtTail base M' e p) ∧
          (∀ p ∉ inPlaces t, ¬ResetArc t p → base p = M p) ∧
            ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t, ¬ResetArc t p → (base p).Sublist (M p)
reading: For every queue firing of Q, of a transition t from the queue marking M, delivering δ, emitting e and leaving M', there is a queue marking base (the queues the firing leaves before its deposit) such that:
every place p holds after the firing the queue base holds at p, followed by the tokens e emits to p, in emission order (AppendedAtTail base M' e p);
on every place p that is neither an input place nor a reset place of t, base holds the queue M held at p;
on every input place p of t that is not a reset place, base holds at p tokens M held at p, in the order M held them (a sublist of M's queue at p).
quotes: Each token is added to the end of the target place's FIFO queue, in the order the action produced it.

*When* the executor admits the completion of an action and output validation does not reject the produced tokens ([EXEC-021], [CONC-026]), the executor *shall* add each produced token at the tail of its place's queue, in the order the action produced the tokens.
assumes: A queue firing relates a transition, the queue marking it fires from, what it delivers to its action, the tokens the action emits (places and tokens, in the order the action produced them) and the queue marking it leaves (glossary: QFireRel, Queue order). The firing is atomic: the step that starts it deposits its emission.

Phase 1 has no completion and no admission. Every firing of the reference queue relation (RefQFire) deposits an emission whose places are an offered deposit of the output spec, so it stands for an admitted completion whose produced tokens pass output validation, which is the trigger of the quoted 'shall' sentence. Which completions the executor admits (not one whose firing ended with its timeout outcome, [EXEC-022] and [IO-013]; not one a stop on a terminal place abandoned, [EXEC-042]; not one an immediate termination abandoned, [ENV-015]; every in-flight one a close waits for, [ENV-013]) is the executor model of Phase 2 (RefExec) and is deferred to it, as is the moment of admission ([EXEC-001] step 1, or the firing pass for a synchronous action).

The sentence 'If the completion of an action is not admitted, or output validation rejects the produced tokens, then the executor shall not deposit any token the action produced at completion.' is deferred to Phase 2: it speaks of completions that are not admitted and of a validation that fails, neither of which is a firing of the atomic Phase 1 relation. The joint model's QProjectsTo Q RefFire excludes every step whose emitted places are not an offered deposit, so at Phase 1 grain no step deposits an emission validation would reject; it is not a line of this block. It does not model the rejected completion itself: a firing that consumes, fails validation and deposits nothing (TransitionFailed, [EXEC-021], [EVT-008]) is not a step of the atomic relation, and neither is a firing of an executor with the validation skip of [CONC-026], which deposits a write that is not an offered deposit. Both are Phase 2 (RefExec).

Tokens an action published before it completed ([IO-015]) are not modelled: the Phase 1 action emits only at the end of the firing. That they are not deposited again and survive a failed or abandoned completion is deferred to Phase 2.

Line 1 is the quoted sentences: the emitted tokens are the tail of each queue, in emission order. Lines 2 and 3 say what 'its place's queue' is, the queue the deposit goes after: on a place the firing does not consume from or reset, the tokens already there (line 2); on an input place that is not reset, tokens the place held, kept in queue order (line 3, glossary Queue order: 'The tokens of a place are kept in the order they were added'). Line 3 does not say which tokens the firing consumes: oldest first is [EXEC-010], and a correlated input of a ν-net match ([NU-020], ruling D16) may take other tokens, which also leaves a sublist; the exact queue left is [EXEC-010] and [EXEC-013]. On a reset place base is unconstrained here; [EXEC-013], [CORE-034] and the count guard QProjectsTo Q RefFire make it empty. Without line 3 an executor that reorders the tokens left on an input place it also deposits to would satisfy the block (EXEC_020_mutant_restOrder_killed).
AC1 (an action produces V to P; V appears at the end of P's queue) is line 1 with line 2: the nonvacuous example EXEC_020_nonvacuous deposits 30 to a place already holding 40 and leaves 40 then 30.

AC2 (multiple tokens to the same place are added in order) is line 1 for an emission with several tokens to one place. The reference queue firing deposits one token per claimed place on an action outcome (Reference.deposit, as every branch-enumerating analysis, [IO-016]), and the count guard QProjectsTo Q RefFire imposes the same on every Q, so the joint model has no step with two tokens to one place until the projection compares places as a set, as [IO-015] does. AC2 is therefore witnessed outside the joint model, by executors that accept several tokens into one claimed place under that set comparison: the in-order one satisfies EXEC-020 and leaves 40, 30, 31 when 30 then 31 go to a place holding 40 (EXEC_020_allows_several), and the reverse-order one violates it (EXEC_020_forbids_reversed).

AC3 (a completion that is not admitted deposits none of the action's tokens) and AC4 (a completion whose produced tokens fail validation deposits none of them) are the deferred sentence above, Phase 2.

requirements.title: Output Spec Validation
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    C.SetValidated →
      ∀ (i : ℕ),
        (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.commit i) s', shall fun s s' ↦
            ∃ f ∈ s.fl,
              f.id = i ∧
                ∃ e,
                  f.out = some (Outcome.ok e) ∧
                    C.validate f.t (validIn f e) = true ∧
                      C.relay f.t f.deliv e = true ∧ s'.M = qAppend s.M e) ∧
          (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.fail i) s', shall fun s s' ↦
              s'.M = s.M ∧ s'.pq = s.pq) ∧
            (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.fail i) s', shall fun s x ↦
                ∃ f ∈ s.fl,
                  f.id = i ∧
                    (f.out = some Outcome.err ∨
                      (∃ e,
                          f.out = some (Outcome.ok e) ∧
                            (C.validate f.t (validIn f e) = false ∨
                              C.relay f.t f.deliv e = false)) ∨
                        ∃ e,
                          f.out = some (Outcome.timedOut e) ∧
                            C.relay f.t f.deliv e = false)) ∧
              (on fun s s' ↦
                  (∃ ok, R C s (XLbl.ret i ok) s') ∨ ∃ p x, R C s (XLbl.write i p x) s',
                  shall fun s s' ↦ s'.M = s.M) ∧
                on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.tdeposit i) s', shall fun s x ↦
                  ∃ f ∈ s.fl,
                    f.id = i ∧
                      ∃ e,
                        f.out = some (Outcome.timedOut e) ∧ C.relay f.t f.deliv e = true
reading: For every executor R, every configuration C whose output verdict reads a set of places, and every firing identity i:

a commit step of i deposits exactly the emission e the action of i returned, each token at the tail of its place in emission order, and only when output validation accepts the places of e followed by the places i has already published, and the join-relay check accepts e;
a fail step of i changes neither the marking nor the queue of publications not yet deposited;

a fail step of i happens only when the action of i failed, or it returned an emission e that output validation (over the same places as in the first line) or the join-relay check rejects, or i ended with a timeout outcome e that the join-relay check rejects;
a step in which the action of i writes a token or returns leaves the marking unchanged;
a step that deposits the timeout outcome e of i happens only when the join-relay check accepts e.
quotes: Before depositing tokens, the executor validates that the produced tokens satisfy the declared output specification (see [IO-015]).
An executor with the validation skip of [CONC-026] enabled does not validate.

*When* an executor with output validation enabled admits the completion of an action, it *shall* validate the produced tokens against the transition's output spec ([IO-015]) before it deposits any of them.
*If* the produced tokens of an admitted completion fail output validation, *then* the executor *shall* deposit none of them and *shall* emit a TransitionFailed event ([EVT-008]).

*If* the produced tokens of an admitted completion fail output validation, *then* the executor *shall not* restore the tokens the firing consumed and *shall not* remove the tokens the action published before it completed ([IO-015]).

*When* an executor with output validation enabled validates the produced tokens of an admitted completion, it *shall* count the places of every batch the action published before it completed ([IO-015]) as produced, together with the places of the produced tokens.
*If* the produced tokens of an admitted completion pass output validation, *then* the executor *shall not* fail the firing.
The timeout outcome is not a completion of the action: [EXEC-022] and [IO-013] govern its deposit.
*When* a firing ends with its timeout outcome, the executor *shall not* validate the timeout outcome against the transition's output spec; the join-relay check of [NU-054] still runs on it.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A firing starts in a firing pass and settles in a later step; the outside steps write, flush and ret are its action writing a token, publishing what it wrote, and returning normally (with what it wrote since the last flush as its emission) or with an error. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), the graph of a step function checked rule by rule against the Rust executor.

Naming: the markdown's 'admits the completion' is the executor taking the completion up in step 1 or inside the pass (glossary: Admitted completion). The model splits what follows into two labels: commit i, the admitted completion passes validation and is deposited, and fail i, it is rejected (or the action failed, [EXEC-030]). The quoted sentences are read through that split: 'deposits' is a commit step, 'fail the firing' and 'emit a TransitionFailed event' is a fail step.

Output validation is two checks of the configuration: C.validate, the IO-015 verdict on a produced set, and C.relay, the join-relay check of NU-054, which the markdown of NU-054 puts 'as part of output validation (IO-015)'. Both are parameters, as the verdict function is IO-015's subject: this block fixes when the executor consults them and what it does with the answer. With the validation skip of CONC-026 both accept everything (Cfg.SkipsValidation), so the quoted 'An executor with the validation skip of [CONC-026] enabled does not validate.' needs no line of its own: under the skip a fail step happens only for an action that failed (theorem EXEC_021_skip). The first quoted sentence is the body's summary of the first shall sentence. A batch the action flushes is checked by the join-relay check when it is flushed (Rust's flush guard): a rejected batch is dropped, and the firing ends with an error whatever its action returns, so its fail step is line 3's first case (exec021_relayBad_fails).

The first shall sentence is lines 1 and 4: a commit step happens only after validation accepted, and the steps in which the action produces its tokens (write, ret) deposit nothing, so no produced token is deposited before the settle step that validates it. Line 1 also says which tokens were validated: exactly the emission the step deposits, at the tails ([EXEC-020]'s deposit, CORE-013), so the check and the deposit are of one set of tokens. An executor that deposits without consulting the validator breaks line 1 (EXEC_021_forbids_ignoreValidate); one that deposits a rejected emission when the action returns, and settles as the reference, breaks only line 4 (EXEC_021_forbids_depositAtReturn).

Validation reads a set of places ([IO-015]; every validator satisfying IO-015 does, IO_015_setOnly), so the lines quantify over configurations whose verdict reads sets (Cfg.SetValidated). The order and repetition of the list validIn builds are then not part of the requirement: an executor validating the published places before the returned ones meets it. The configurations of the examples are of that kind (exec021_cfg_set).

The second shall sentence is lines 1, 2 and 4: a rejected emission is never the emission of a commit step (line 1), its fail step deposits nothing (line 2), and the action's write and return steps deposit nothing (line 4).
