That no other executor step deposits it is EXEC-020's companion line (deposits of a firing only through commit, tdeposit and publish) and EXEC-022's (tdeposit deposits exactly the timeout outcome), both later blocks over this model. 'Emit a TransitionFailed event' is the event kind the fail label carries (design table R-EXEC-8); the event and its payload are EVT-008's, on the event model of wave W7. That a rejection is in fact settled by a fail step, and not left in the queue, is coverage, stated in the consistency theorem (ValidatedBy), not here.

The third shall sentence is line 2: the fail step leaves the marking as it is, so the consumed tokens stay consumed (EXEC_021_forbids_failRestores) and the tokens the action already published stay. A publication still queued when the completion fails is deposited later by its publish step (ruling D17), so line 2 also keeps the publication queue (EXEC_021_forbids_dropPublication).

The fourth shall sentence (ruling D27 (a)) is the places line 1 and line 3 read, validIn f e: the places of the returned emission e followed by the places of every batch firing f flushed. Rust validates the returned outputs together with flushed_places (executor.rs output_conforms). A validation over the returned places alone fails a firing that published one child of And(A, B) and returned the other (EXEC_021_mutant_noPub_killed).
The fifth shall sentence is line 3 for a returned emission: a fail step of a firing whose emission passes both checks does not exist. With line 2 it excludes an executor that fails every completion.

The timeout sentences (ruling D24 (a)) are line 3's last case: a firing that ended with its timeout outcome is failed only when the join-relay check rejects it, never by the IO-015 verdict. Rust skips validation on the timeout path and runs the relay check (executor.rs handle_completion); Java and TypeScript validate the timeout outcome, which fails And(A, Timeout(d, B)) on every timeout (EXEC_021_forbids_validateTimeout); under D24 (a) that is an executor defect. That the relay check runs on the timeout outcome is NU-054's sentence 'Every token the firing deposits in a relay target is checked, whatever wrote it, including an Out.forwardInput or Out.timeout branch'. Line 5 is the relay half of the sentence: a deposit of the timeout outcome happens only when the relay check accepts it (EXEC_021_forbids_timeoutNoRelay). What the timeout outcome deposits is EXEC-022's and IO-013's subject.

Validation reads sets of places (IO-015), so an emission with several tokens in one claimed place passes; a run whose emission is not a deposit the output spec offers is a real run (IO-016 AC4), so a link from this model to the queue firing RefQFire carries the per-run hypothesis OfferedEmission (glossary).
Firing identities are drawn from one supply (XSt.nextId), so 'the firing i' is unique in every reachable state; the lines read 'some firing in flight with identity i', which is the same there.
AC1 (And, every child received tokens, valid) is IO-015's verdict; EXEC_021_nonvacuous admits And(1, 2) with child 1 published and child 2 returned.
AC2 (Xor, exactly one child selected, overlapping branches without a tie-break) is IO-015's verdict (IO_015_ac9, IO_015_ac10), not restated.

AC3 (violation, failure event emitted) is line 1 (a rejected emission has no commit step) with the event kind of the fail label; that the fail step is offered is ValidatedBy in the consistency theorem. EXEC_021_nonvacuous fails Xor(1, 2) written in both branches. The event itself is EVT-008's.
AC4 (validation applied by every executor backend a language ships) is about which code paths exist: both backends are runs of RefExec (CONC-020, a later block); not encoded here (test evidence).

AC5 (violation: the event is TransitionFailed, no produced token deposited, consumed tokens not restored, published tokens stay) is lines 1 and 2; EXEC_021_nonvacuous deposits the publication of a failed firing after its fail step.
The test derivation (Xor output with tokens to both branches, a violation, neither branch place receives a token) is EXEC_021_nonvacuous's rejection run.

requirements.title: Cardinality Labels
requirements.statement:
fun L ↦
  L Card.one = none ∧
    (∀ (n : ℕ),
        0 < n →
          L (Card.exactly n) = some ("×" ++ toString n) ∨
            L (Card.exactly n) = some (toString n)) ∧
      (L Card.all = some "*" ∨ L Card.all = some "all") ∧
        ∀ (m : ℕ), L (Card.atLeast m) = some ("≥" ++ toString m)
requirements.scope: every exporter, on the input arcs of a net (the only arcs with a cardinality)
reading: For the cardinality labeller L of an export (none: no cardinality label):
One has no cardinality label;
for every count n of at least 1, Exactly(n) is labelled ×n or n;
All is labelled * or all;
for every minimum m, AtLeast(m) is labelled ≥m.
quotes: Multi-token arcs (Exactly(n), All, AtLeast(m)) display count notation on the arc label:
Exactly(n): label shows "×n" or "n"
All: label shows "*" or "all"
AtLeast(m): label shows "≥m"
The export *shall* give an input arc with cardinality `One` no cardinality label.
The export *shall* give an input arc with cardinality `Exactly(n)` the cardinality label `×n` or `n`.
The export *shall* give an input arc with cardinality `All` the cardinality label `*` or `all`.
The export *shall* give an input arc with cardinality `AtLeast(m)` the cardinality label `≥m`.
assumes: The model is the cardinality labeller L : Card → Option String of an export: the cardinality label it gives an input arc, from the arc's cardinality alone, none for no cardinality label. Only input arcs have a cardinality (glossary: Input arc; the output specs of IO-011 to IO-014 carry none), so the opening sentence 'Multi-token arcs (Exactly(n), All, AtLeast(m)) display count notation on the arc label:', which names no arc kind, is read as input arcs, and the four shall sentences name input arcs to say so. Output, inhibitor, read and reset arcs are out of scope. Correlation (EXP-018, NU-020) plays no part in L: the ⟨n⟩ prefix is not a cardinality label.

Where the label is drawn is not encoded. The sentence 'The export shall draw the cardinality label of an input arc on the edge of the arc.' needs the export model RefExport and lands in wave W4 with EXP-018 as the bridge line 'the label of an uncorrelated input edge of an arc with cardinality c is L c; the label of a correlated one is ⟨n⟩, followed by a space and L c when L c is a label'. Until then this block does not rule out an export that draws no label, or a label other than L's, on an input edge. The W4 line must also reject a mapper that writes ⟨n⟩ alone on a correlated Exactly(2) edge: its uncorrelated labeller is the correct one, so this block cannot see it.

'×n' is read as the character × (U+00D7) followed by n in decimal, 'n' as n in decimal alone, '≥m' as ≥ (U+2265) followed by m in decimal, as every runtime writes them (Lean toString on Nat); an ASCII lookalike such as x3 or >=5 is a different label (EXP_006_forbids_ascii). 'No cardinality label' is none: some "" is a label, although DOT draws label="" like no label; no runtime writes it (EXP_006_forbids_emptyOne).

Line 2 ranges over counts of at least 1, since IO-002 defines Exactly(n) only for N >= 1 and its AC1 rejects N < 1, so no export labels Exactly(0). Line 4 has no such guard: IO-004 states no lower bound on the minimum (only the runtimes reject a minimum below 1), so the bullet 'AtLeast(m): label shows ≥m' is taken for every m, AtLeast(0) included; the reference labeller meets it, and a labeller that drops the label of AtLeast(0) violates the block (EXP_006_mutant_atLeastGuard_killed).

Lines 2 and 3 are disjunctions because the spec allows both forms, and the choice is free per value: Exactly(1) may be labelled 1 while Exactly(2) is labelled ×2, and ×n may go with all. The block does not ask one form for every n, nor matching forms across Exactly and All (EXP_006_allows_mixed). Pinning ×n and * (all three runtimes write ×n, *, ≥m) is the question of open ruling D41 and is not encoded; that later line must make both exp006_bare and exp006_mixed violations, and until then both satisfy the block (EXP_006_allows_bare, EXP_006_allows_mixed).

The opening sentence names Exactly(n) as a multi-token arc for every n; Exactly(1) moves one token and is still labelled, by AC1 ('Non-One cardinality is displayed on the arc') and by every runtime (×1). Line 2 therefore holds at n = 1, and the reading that labels only arcs moving more than one token is a mutant (EXP_006_mutant_multiOnly_killed).

AC1 (non-One cardinality is displayed on the arc) is encoded in its label half by lines 2, 3 and 4: every buildable non-One cardinality has a cardinality label (EXP_006_labels_nonOne). Its 'on the arc' half is the W4 bridge line above.

AC2 (One cardinality has no label, by default) is encoded only as line 1, 'no cardinality label'. AC2's text asks for no label at all on the edge; the edge label is not modelled here, so this block does not rule out a One input edge drawn with some other label (for example 1). The uncorrelated case is closed by the W4 bridge line, under which an uncorrelated One edge carries L one = none. EXP-018 labels a correlated One input edge ⟨n⟩; whether that contradicts AC2's bare 'no label' is clash exp-a#6, tied to open ruling D41, and is decided with the edge-level line in W4. Line 1 holds under either outcome. The word 'default' is read as 'the label of an uncorrelated One input edge'; no configuration option of EXP-007 changes the cardinality label in any runtime.
The test derivation (a net with Exactly(3) and AtLeast(5) inputs, labels show the counts) is EXP_006_nonvacuous on the reference labeller: ×3 and ≥5.

requirements.title: Styling
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] C ↦
  ∀ (X : Reference.Net N) (env term : N → Bool) (p : N),
    (term p = true → C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.terminal) ∧
      (term p = false → env p = true → C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.environment) ∧
        (term p = false →
          env p = false →
            (C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.start ↔ HasOutputArc X p = false) ∧
              (HasOutputArc X p = true →
                  HasInputArc X p = false →
                    HasReadArc X p = false → C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.end) ∧
                (HasInputArc X p = true → C X env term p ≠ Export.NodeCat.end) ∧
                  (C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.start ∨
                      C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.end ∨
                        C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.place) ∧
                    (HasOutputArc X p = true →
                      HasInputArc X p = false →
                        HasReadArc X p = true →
                          ∀ (X' : Reference.Net N) (env' term' : N → Bool) (p' : N),
                            term' p' = false →
                              env' p' = false →
                                HasOutputArc X' p' = true →
                                  HasInputArc X' p' = false →
                                    HasReadArc X' p' = true →
                                      C X' env' term' p' = C X env term p))
requirements.scope: every exporter's mapper, on the place nodes of a net (before a documentation generator restyles interface ports)
reading: For the place classifier C, every net X with environment places env and terminal places term, and every place p:
a terminal place is terminal;
an environment place that is not terminal is environment;
for a place that is neither (an ordinary place): it is start exactly when no transition has an output arc on it;
it is end when some transition has an output arc on it and none has an input arc or a read arc on it;
it is not end when some transition has an input arc on it;
it is start, end or the regular place row;

and if some transition has an output arc on it, some has a read arc on it and none has an input arc on it, then every ordinary place p' of every net X' (with any env' and term') of which the same holds gets the same row as p.
quotes: The export applies visual styling to distinguish node categories:
The export *shall* give a terminal place the terminal category.
The export *shall* give an environment place that is not a terminal place the environment category.
The export *shall* give an ordinary place the start category exactly when no transition's output spec names it.
The export *shall* give the end category to an ordinary place that some transition's output spec names and on which no transition has an input arc or a read arc.
The export *shall not* give the end category to an ordinary place on which some transition has an input arc.
The export *shall* give an ordinary place the start, the end or the regular place category.

The export *shall* give the same category to all ordinary places, in one net or in different nets, that some transition's output spec names, on which some transition has a read arc and on which no transition has an input arc.
assumes: The model is a place classifier C : PlaceClassifier N: the node row (glossary of the style table, Libpetri.Export.NodeCat) the export's mapper gives place p of net X, given the environment places env (ENV-001) and the terminal places term (EXEC-042) as predicates. C reads only the arcs of X, as every runtime's analysis does (analyze_places in the Rust crate libpetri-export, PlaceAnalysis.java, analyzePlaces in petri-net-mapper.ts); the marking, the timing and the configuration play no part. Lines 1 to 6 fix C from the arc kinds on p in every case but one, and line 7 makes that one case, too, the same answer for every place and every net, so C reads no more of X than whether p has an output arc, an input arc and a read arc. That the exporter draws each place node with the row C gives, and that a place row is not a transition shape, is EXP-002's join line on the export model (RefExport, wave W4), cited there; this block does not see the graph.

C is the mapper's classification, the one the production export pipeline gives. The three documentation generators (SubnetDotExport.java, subnet-dot-export.ts, and the Rust subnet_dot_export module; compile-time diagrams, EXP-011) afterwards rewrite the DOT of a subnet body and redraw its interface-port places with the interface-port row; that rewrite is a later step on the DOT text, not C's answer, and is out of scope. The markdown says so in the sentence after the bullets. A mapper that gives an ordinary place the interface-port row itself violates line 6 (EXP_008_forbids_otherRow).

Which places get a node at all is EXP-001's subject (ruling D60): Rust draws every declared place, Java and TypeScript only places some arc touches. Line 3 gives a place that no arc touches the start category, which is what Rust draws; Java and TypeScript draw no node for it, so their answer for it is never seen (PlaceAnalysis.category answers place for an unknown name). The reference classifier answers start, as Rust does.

The words 'incoming' and 'outgoing' of the body bullets ('no incoming arcs', 'no outgoing arcs') are read as the markdown's sentence after the bullets defines them, which is how all three runtimes count: an incoming arc of a place is an output arc of some transition on it (glossary: Output arc, the target of a ForwardInput included), and an input arc on it is an outgoing arc. Whether a read arc is an outgoing arc is the open case of ruling D51 (next assumption). Inhibitor arcs and reset arcs count as neither, although the glossary draws them from the place to the transition and the reset edge of EXP-004 and EXP-013 is drawn from the transition to the place (clash exp-a#5 and exp-a#9): a classifier that counts them as outgoing violates line 4 (EXP_008_forbids_glossaryDirections), one that counts a reset arc as incoming violates line 3 (EXP_008_forbids_resetIncoming).

Ruling D51 (a): the common form of 'end place'. A place that an output spec names, on which no transition has an input arc and some transition has a read arc, is regular in Java and TypeScript (a read arc counts as outgoing) and end in Rust (only input arcs count). Lines 4 and 5 hold of both shapes and leave that place open (EXP_008_readOnly_open); the Rust shape is an allowed classifier (EXP_008_allows_inputsOnly). The case is open per classifier, not per place: line 7 says a classifier answers it the same way for every such place of every net, so a mix of the two shapes is rejected, whether the answer hangs on whether the reader writes elsewhere (EXP_008_forbids_readByWriter) or on whether the reader is the place's own writer (EXP_008_forbids_selfReadSkipped). The end state of D51, that a read arc keeps a place from being an end place, is the reference classifier's answer; the later line that makes line 4 an 'exactly when' with read arcs counted waits for the Rust mapper to change and is not encoded. The markdown records the open case and the intended answer in a sentence without shall.

The precedence terminal, environment, start, end is all three runtimes' (ruling D51) and is lines 1 to 3 and 6: a terminal environment place is terminal (EXP_008_forbids_envFirst), an environment place no output spec names is environment, not start (EXP_008_forbids_startFirst), and a place with no arcs at all is start, not end (EXP_008_forbids_endFirst). EXEC-042 builds reject a terminal place with an input or read arc, which the precedence does not need.

AC1 (start places are visually distinct from other places) and AC2 (end places are visually distinct from other places) are read on the style table: the start row and the end row each differ from every other place row and from the transition row (EXP_008_rows_distinct, decided on the generated table), and lines 1 to 7 decide which places get the start and the end row. Until EXP-002's join line lands (wave W4), nothing ties the drawn style to C, so AC1 and AC2 are accounted for here but not yet proven; EXP_008_rows_distinct carries no evidence tag for that reason, and the W4 block for EXP-002 closes the dependency. The colours of the body bullets ('e.g., green', 'e.g., blue', 'e.g., yellow') are examples; the values are the table's and are checked by the runtimes' tests, not here. The bullet on transitions (a distinct colour) is the transition row's difference from the place rows in EXP_008_rows_distinct; that transitions are drawn with the transition row is EXP-003's subject.

The test derivation (a net with start and end places, export, styling applied) is EXP_008_nonvacuous on the reference classifier: a net with a start, a regular, an end, an environment, a terminal and an inhibitor-only place.

Out of scope: the rows of composition (interface-port, sync-channel), which only the documentation generators' rewrite of a subnet diagram uses (see the second assumption; MOD-040 and EXP-016 add grouping only), and the rows of junctions (EXP-012), which are synthetic nodes, not place nodes; ν correlation (NU-020, EXP-018) changes no place category. Places are compared by identity (DecidableEq N); export IDs and sanitising are EXP-014's (ruling D46).

requirements.title: XOR/AND Junction Nodes
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (t : String) (R : List String) (o : OutTree),
    ∃ ρ,
      (∀ (i j : ℕ), ρ i = ρ j → i = j) ∧
        (List.map (fun kj ↦ (kj.1, ρ kj.2)) (E t R o).junctions).Perm o.junctions.zipIdx ∧
          (List.map (XEdge.seen R ρ) (E t R o).edges).Perm
            (List.map (DrawnEdge.seen R) (Drawing t o))
requirements.scope: every exporter, the output side of one transition
reading: For every transition name t, reset places R and output tree o (any tree, short and empty groups included), there is a one-to-one renumbering ρ of the junction indices the emitter E uses, such that:
the junctions E draws, renumbered, are the groups of o with two or more children, one junction each, of the group's kind (OutTree.junctions), in any order;

the edges E draws, renumbered, are the edges of the drawing rule (Drawing t o), one each, in any order: both ends of every edge, and for every edge that does not end in a reset place also its arc type output, style row output, dash and label as the rule gives them.
quotes: For every `Out.Xor` or `Out.And` group with **two or more children**, the mapper MUST insert a synthetic *junction node* between the transition and the children.
A group with fewer than two children MUST NOT produce a junction (it is a pass-through).
The mapper *shall* draw one junction node for each `And` or `Xor` group of an output spec that has two or more children, of the group's kind, and no other junction node.
*Where* an `And` or `Xor` group has fewer than two children, the mapper *shall* draw its child, if it has one, from the group's parent and with the label the edge into the group would carry.

The mapper *shall* draw exactly one solid output edge into each junction node, into the place of each `Place` leaf and into the target place of each `ForwardInput` leaf, from the nearest junction node above it, or from the transition when there is none, and no other edge for the output spec.
The edge into a child of an `Xor` junction *shall* carry the child's branch label: the place name of a `Place` child, `⏱<n>ms` for a `Timeout` child of n ms, and no label for an `And` or `Xor` child.
The edge into a child of an `And` junction, and the edge from the transition into the output spec, *shall* carry no label of their own.
*Where* a `Timeout` node of n ms is in an output spec, the edge drawn into its child *shall* carry `⏱<n>ms` in place of the label the edge into the `Timeout` would carry.

*Where* a leaf is a `ForwardInput` from place F to place P, the mapper *shall* draw its edge as the edge of a `Place` leaf for P at the same position, dashed instead of solid, and with `⟵F` after its label and a space, or as its only label when it has none.
*Where* [EXP-013] combines a leaf edge into a reset place, that edge *shall* take the arc type, label and style [EXP-013] gives it in place of the ones above.
assumes: The model is an output emitter E : Emitter (glossary): from a transition name t, its reset places R and its output tree o (glossary OutTree: n-ary And and Xor groups, a Timeout with its duration in ms, Place and ForwardInput leaves), the junctions, as (kind, index), and the edges (glossary XEdge: ends, arc type, style row, dash, label) the exporter draws for the output side of t. The input, inhibitor, read and standalone reset edges and the place and transition nodes are drawn outside the emitter and are other blocks' subject (EXP-001 to EXP-004, EXP-013).

The drawing rule Drawing t o is the glossary's drawOut from the transition, with no inherited label, junctions numbered from 0, one clause per sentence: a group with two or more children gives one junction of its kind and one solid output edge into it from the parent with the inherited label, then its children below it (the first and third shall sentences); a shorter group gives no junction and draws its children from the parent with the inherited label (the second); a Place leaf gives one solid edge into its place from the parent with the inherited label (the third); below an Xor junction a child inherits its branch label (glossary branchLabel), below an And junction and from the transition nothing (the fourth and fifth); a Timeout hands its child the label ⏱<n>ms in place of the inherited one (the sixth); a ForwardInput leaf from F into P is the Place leaf for P, dashed, labelled forwardLabel (⟵F after the inherited label and a space, or ⟵F alone) (the seventh). The two body sentences that open the section say what the first two shall sentences say.

Junction indices are compared up to a one-to-one renumbering ρ: which index each junction gets (pre-order from 0) is EXP-014's line, so an emitter that numbers its junctions in post-order still meets this block. The renumbering must be one to one, so an emitter that draws the edge into a junction at one index and the edges out of it at another (two nodes in the graph for one group) violates the block (EXP_012_forbids_split).

Order is not stated: the junctions and edges are compared as lists up to permutation (List.Perm), membership and multiplicity only. Node and edge order across languages is open ruling R2 (exp-b) and kind Q; the order of an Xor junction's children is EXP-005's line.

The last shall sentence is the guard of the third line: for an edge that ends in a place of R only its two ends are compared, and its arc type, style row, label and dash are EXP-013's. Its ends and the count, one edge per leaf, still bind, so an emitter that draws a combined edge next to an output edge for one leaf violates this block.

The block quantifies over every output tree, including a group with fewer than two children (Rust's Out::Xor is a public variant and a TypeScript node a plain object, so a short Xor reaches the mappers' pass-through arm), an empty group (no junction and no edge, as all three mappers draw it) and a ForwardInput below an Xor junction, which no transition that builds has (IO-013, IO-014): the seventh shall sentence draws it as the Place leaf for its target, so its label is the target name, a space and ⟵F, which is what all three mappers draw.

The junction node attributes (shape diamond, fill, stroke, pen width, size, the glyphs ✕ and ✚, font size, fixed size) and the node categories xor-junction and and-junction belong to the exporter's nodes and the style table (Libpetri.Export.Styles, JKind.cat), not to the emitter: the category line of a junction node is a later line of the exporter blocks in wave W4, and the constants are checked by tests (kind Q).

AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 are EXP_012_nonvacuous on the reference emitter: XOR(P_a, P_b) gives one xor junction and the edges junction to P_a and junction to P_b; AND(P_c, P_d) one and junction and two edges; AND(P_a) a direct edge from the transition to P_a and no junction (AC3 is stated with AND by ruling D26 item 1, since IO-012 gives every Xor two or more children); XOR(AND(P_a, P_b), P_c) an and junction nested below the xor junction. Their junction attributes (diamond, ✕, ✚) are the exporter's, as above.

AC5 (Java, TypeScript and Rust mappers produce byte-identical junction nodes and edges) is kind Q: a Lean function is deterministic and cross-language equality is a property of three programs (export design P3, ruling D60 (c)); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration. The test derivation is AC1 to AC4.

requirements.title: Input One
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    InputArc t p Card.one →
      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),
            Marked m p →
              ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (io001_withoutInput t p) m m')) ∧
          (¬ResetArc t p →
            ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
              F t m d m' →
                m' p + 1 = m p + Deposits d p ∧ (¬OutputArc t p → m' p + 1 = m p))
reading: For every transition t and place p such that the input arc of t on p is One:
t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;
from a marking in which p is marked, t can fire exactly when t without its input arc on p can fire;

unless p is also a reset place of t, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) + 1 = m(p) + d(p): p loses exactly 1 token, besides what the firing deposits there; and if p is not an output place of t either, m'(p) + 1 = m(p): p loses exactly 1 token, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: `One(place)` is an input arc whose required count and consumption count are both 1.
*While* the input place of a `One` input arc is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* the input place of a `One` input arc is marked and is not a correlated input of the transition's match specification ([NU-020]), the arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.
*When* a transition with a `One` input arc fires, it *shall* consume exactly 1 token from the input place.

*When* a transition with a `One` input arc fires, and the input place is neither a reset place nor an output place of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing holding exactly 1 fewer token than it held before the firing.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enables' are both read as 'some firing exists'.

Correlated inputs (ruling D30, extending D16): the third quoted sentence excludes a correlated input of a ν-net match specification (NU-020), on which the arc also requires a token of the chosen name. The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every input place is one that is not a correlated input, and the second line quantifies over every `One` input arc. How a correlated input counts and consumes is NU-020's, not encoded here.

The first quoted sentence and the bullets (`requiredCount()` returns 1, `consumptionCount(available)` returns 1) are IO-007's contract for `One`. Here it is observed through firing: the required count is the second and third lines, the consumption count the fourth. The bullet values themselves are `io001_counts`.

AC1 (enables when the place has >= 1 token) is the second line (not with 0 tokens) and the third line (with >= 1 token the arc does not stand in the way; whether the other arcs allow the firing is theirs to say, IO-005 and CORE-022).

AC2 (exactly 1 token consumed on firing) is the fourth line for the count. Which token is consumed (the oldest) is below the count granularity of the firing semantics and is the glossary's reading of Consume (CORE-030); it is not encoded here.
AC3 (remaining tokens stay in the place) is the fourth line: p holds m(p) - 1 tokens plus the firing's deposit there afterwards.

Consumption is observed through the marking: p loses 1 and gains what the firing deposits there (p may also be an output place). A place that is both the input place and a reset place of t ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), so the consumed token is not visible in the marking; the fourth line excludes that case.

The deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count: on a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so there the consumed token shows in the marking alone, as exactly 1 token fewer. Without this a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit of 1 in the input place would pass the count.
The input arc of t on p is the first input arc on p (glossary: Input arc), and t without its input arc on p drops that arc only; CORE-030 rejects a second input arc on p at build.

requirements.title: Input Exactly
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (n : ℕ),
    InputArc t p (Card.exactly n) →
      (while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p < n, never Fire F t) ∧
        (¬ResetArc t p →
          ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
            F t m d m' →
              m' p + n = m p + Deposits d p ∧ (¬OutputArc t p → m' p + n = m p))
reading: For every transition t, place p and count N such that the input arc of t on p is Exactly(N):
t does not fire from a marking in which p holds fewer than N tokens;

unless p is also a reset place of t, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) + N = m(p) + d(p): p loses exactly N tokens, besides what the firing deposits there; and if p is not an output place of t either, m'(p) + N = m(p): p loses exactly N tokens, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: `Exactly(place, n)` is an input arc whose required count and consumption count are both N, where N >= 1.
*While* the input place of an `Exactly(n)` input arc holds fewer than N tokens, the transition *shall not* fire.
*When* a transition with an `Exactly(n)` input arc fires, it *shall* consume exactly N tokens from the input place.

*When* a transition with an `Exactly(n)` input arc fires, and the input place is neither a reset place nor an output place of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing holding exactly N fewer tokens than it held before the firing.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Enables' is read as 'some firing exists'.

The first quoted sentence (required count N, consumption count N; the bullets `requiredCount()` returns N and `consumptionCount(available)` returns N) is IO-007's contract for `Exactly(n)`. Here it is observed through firing: the required count is the second line, the consumption count the third. The bullets' qualifier 'when available >= N' is implied: by the second line no firing starts with fewer.

AC1 (construction with N < 1 rejected, also when the transition is built from a spec written out without the constructor): a property of construction, not of firing, so the formula does not encode it. The formula quantifies over every N, N = 0 included; for N = 0 both lines hold of the reference semantics trivially, so the restriction N >= 1 neither weakens nor strengthens what is checked about firing.

AC2 (enables only when the place has >= N tokens) and AC4 (N-1 tokens, not enabled) are the second line. The converse ('enables when the place has >= N tokens', given the other arcs allow it) is the AND-join of IO-005 and CORE-022, not this block's subject.

AC3 (exactly N consumed on firing, the N oldest, FIFO) is the third line for the count; its second part (the fourth quoted sentence) states it without the deposit for an input place that is neither a reset place nor an output place. Which tokens are consumed (the oldest, FIFO) is below the count granularity of the firing semantics and is the glossary's reading of Consume (CORE-030); it is not encoded here.

Consumption is observed through the marking: p loses N and gains what the firing deposits there (p may also be an output place). A place that is both the input place and a reset place of t ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), so the N tokens consumed are not visible in the marking; the third line excludes that case, as the fourth quoted sentence does.

The deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count: on a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so there the consumed tokens show in the marking alone, as exactly N tokens fewer (the fourth quoted sentence, IO-001's guard). Without this a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit of N in the input place would pass the count, and the block would lean on CORE-035 to stand.

Deposits are counts per place (glossary: Deposit, [CORE-036]): `Deposits d p` counts the tokens d puts in p and ignores their order. The build-time output-spec checks of IO-011 to IO-014 (ambiguity, one Timeout, ForwardInput only under a Timeout) and the validation skip of CONC-026 do not touch input consumption, so the formula quantifies over every transition, built or not, and every executor.
The input arc of t on p is the first input arc on p (glossary: Input arc); CORE-030 rejects a second one at build.

requirements.title: Input All
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    AllArc t p →
      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),
            Marked m p → ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (withoutAll t p) m m')) ∧
          (∀ (d : List N),
              on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ m' p = Deposits d p) ∧
            (¬OutputArc t p →
              ∀ (d : List N), on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ m' p = 0)
reading: For every transition t and every place p on which t has an `All` input arc:
t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;
from a marking in which p is marked, t can fire exactly when t without its `All` input arcs on p can fire;
every firing of t that deposits d leaves p holding exactly the tokens d puts there;
if p is not an output place of t, every firing of t leaves p empty, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: *While* the place of an `All` input arc of a transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.

*While* the place of an `All` input arc of a transition is marked and is not a correlated input of the transition's match specification ([NU-020]), the `All` input arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.
*When* a transition fires, it *shall* consume every token from the place of each of its `All` input arcs that is not a correlated input of its match specification ([NU-020]).
*When* a transition fires, the place of each of its `All` input arcs that is neither an output place of the transition nor a correlated input of its match specification *shall* end the firing empty.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' is read as 'some firing to some marking exists'.

Correlated inputs (ruling D30, extending D16): the second, third and fourth quoted shall sentences exclude a correlated input of a ν-net match specification (NU-020), where an `All` arc consumes the tokens of the chosen name only and leaves the others, as the section's last sentence says. The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every input place is one that is not a correlated input, and the second to fourth lines quantify over every `All` input arc. How a correlated input counts and consumes is NU-020's, not encoded here.
The first two lines together say that the `All` arc requires exactly one token: `requiredCount()` returns 1 (the first bullet; `Card.required .all = 1`).

'Consume every token' is read through the place's count after the firing: p ends holding only what this firing deposited in p, so it kept none of its own tokens. This is the second bullet, `consumptionCount(available)` returns `available`. A firing that also deposits into p (p is an output place of t) leaves those tokens in p.

AC1 (enables when the place has >= 1 token) is the second line: with p marked the `All` arc removes no firing. AC3 (0 tokens, not enabled) is the first line. AC2 (all tokens consumed, place empty after) is the third line, with 'empty' read as 'empty apart from this firing's own deposit into p', and the fourth line, where p is not an output place and 'empty' is literal.

The fourth line is the guard IO-001 also carries: it does not trust the deposit a firing reports. On a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing can deposit (CORE-035, CORE-063), so there the drain shows in the marking alone, as an empty place. Without it, a firing that keeps p's tokens and reports them as its own deposit into p would pass the third line. The fourth line stands alone: it needs neither the third line nor CORE-035.

A reset arc on p does not weaken the fourth line: the spec sentence has no reset exclusion, and a reset place that is not an output place ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), which is nothing.
Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036): the lines read the count `Deposits d p` and the marking's count at p, never the order of d.
Which token is consumed first, and that the consumed tokens reach the action, are below the count granularity of a firing relation; they are not encoded.

A firing is one step at the count granularity: EXEC-003 AC5 (an `All` or `AtLeast` arc that fires later in a firing pass drains only the tokens the firing may drain, and leaves in place the tokens a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same pass) is below this granularity; that refinement is EXEC-003's subject and the reference executor's (RefExec, wave W5), not this block's.

A transition with two input arcs on p is rejected at build by CORE-030. On such a transition the formula reads the first arc on p, as the reference does (`InputArc`); `withoutAll` removes only the `All` arcs on p.

requirements.title: Input AtLeast
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (n : ℕ),
    InputArc t p (Card.atLeast n) →
      (while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p < n, never Fire F t) ∧
        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),
            n ≤ TokenCount m p →
              ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (withoutInputArc t p) m m')) ∧
          (∀ (d : List N),
              on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧
            (¬OutputArc t p →
              ∀ (d : List N),
                on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ TokenCount m' p = 0)
reading: For every transition t, place p and number n such that the input arc of t on p is AtLeast(p, n):
t does not fire from a marking in which p holds fewer than n tokens;
from a marking m in which p holds at least n tokens, t can fire from m exactly when t without its input arc on p can fire from m;
every firing of t, with whatever deposit d, leaves p holding exactly the tokens d deposited there (every token p held was consumed);
if p is not an output place of t, every firing of t leaves p empty, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: *While* the input place of an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc holds fewer than `minimum` tokens, the transition *shall not* fire.

*While* the input place of an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc holds at least `minimum` tokens and is not a correlated input of the transition's match specification ([NU-020]), the input arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.

*When* a transition with an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc fires, it *shall* consume every token the input place holds, unless the input place is a correlated input of its match specification ([NU-020]).

*When* a transition with an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc fires, and the input place is neither an output place nor a correlated input of the match specification of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing empty.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' is read as 'some firing from m exists', whatever marking it leads to: removing the arc changes what the firing consumes from p, so only whether t fires is compared, not where it leads.

Correlated inputs (ruling D30, extending D16): the second, third and fourth quoted shall sentences exclude a correlated input of a ν-net match specification (NU-020), where an `AtLeast` arc requires and consumes the tokens of the chosen name only, as the section's last sentence says. The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every input place is one that is not a correlated input, and the second to fourth lines quantify over every `AtLeast` input arc. How a correlated input counts and consumes is NU-020's, not encoded here.

'The input arc on p' is the first input arc on p, as the glossary term Input arc reads it; `withoutInputArc` removes that one arc. [CORE-030] allows at most one input arc per place, so on a well-formed transition it is the only one.

AC1 (construction with minimum < 1 is rejected): not encoded. It is a build-time check on the net definition, outside the firing relation. The statement quantifies over every n, n = 0 included; the reference semantics satisfies it there too (AtLeast(p, 0) never blocks and drains p).

AC2 (transition enables when the place has >= minimum tokens) is the second line: with p holding at least n tokens the arc does not stop t from firing. Read with [IO-005], the other arcs of t still decide.

AC3 (all tokens consumed on firing, not just minimum) is the third line, stated on the marking the firing leaves: p ends holding what was deposited there and nothing it held before. A reset arc on p ([CORE-034]) gives the same end count, so neither the third nor the fourth line needs a reset guard.

The fourth line is the guard IO-001 carries, so the block stands alone: the deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count. On a place the output spec of t does not name, no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so the drain shows in the marking alone, as an empty place. Without it a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit in p equal to what p held would pass the third line.
AC4 (place with minimum - 1 tokens, transition not enabled) is the first line, at the count minimum - 1.

A firing is one step at the count granularity: EXEC-003 AC5 (an `All` or `AtLeast` arc that fires later in a firing pass drains only the tokens the firing may drain, and leaves in place the tokens a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same pass) is below this granularity; that refinement is EXEC-003's subject and the reference executor's (RefExec, wave W5), not this block's.

The two bullets (`requiredCount()` returns `minimum`, `consumptionCount(available)` returns `available`) are the pure-function contract of [IO-007] and the glossary terms Required count and Consumption count; this block encodes their effect on firing (lines 1 to 4), not the functions themselves.

The output-spec build checks ([IO-011] to [IO-014]) and the output validation skip ([CONC-026]) do not touch input consumption; the block holds of every firing relation over every transition, built or not.

requirements.title: Input AND-Join Semantics
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
    (∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs,
        while fun m ↦ TokenCount m s.place < requiredCount s.card, never Fire F t) ∧
      ∀ (m : CountMarking N),
        (∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs, requiredCount s.card ≤ TokenCount m s.place) →
          ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (withoutInputs t) m m')
reading: For every transition t:
for every input arc s of t, t does not fire from a marking in which the input place of s holds fewer tokens than the required count of s;
from a marking m in which every input place of t holds at least the required count of its input arc, t can fire from m exactly when t without its input arcs can fire from m.
quotes: *While* any input place of a transition holds fewer tokens than the required count of its input arc, the transition *shall not* fire.

*While* every input place of a transition that has no match specification ([NU-020]) holds at least the required count of its input arc, the input arcs *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists' (to some marking): the input arcs change what a firing consumes, so the second line compares whether t fires, not where it leads.

Correlated inputs (ruling D30, extending D16): the second quoted shall sentence is scoped to a transition that has no match specification; a transition with one also needs a name of which every correlated input holds at least its required count of tokens (NU-020). The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so the second line quantifies over every transition. The first quoted shall sentence needs no exclusion: a correlated input that holds fewer tokens than its required count holds fewer tokens of any one name.
'Simultaneously satisfied' is read as 'satisfied in the one marking the firing starts from': both lines fix a single marking m.
Input arcs are read from the transition's list of input arcs, every one of them. A transition with two input arcs on one place, which [CORE-030] rejects at build, is gated by both.

AC1 (a transition with 3 inputs enables only when all 3 places have sufficient tokens) is the first line, for any number of input arcs, 3 included; the test derivation's 'satisfy all 3; verify enabled' is the second line together with a transition that, without its input arcs, can fire (no read or inhibitor arc blocks it).
AC2 (any one input unsatisfied disables the transition) is the first line.
How many tokens an input arc requires (requiredCount) is IO-001 to IO-004 and IO-007, not this block: the statement takes requiredCount as given.

requirements.title: requiredCount and consumptionCount Contract
requirements.statement:
fun K ↦
  (∀ (c : Card),
      K.required c =
        match c with
        | Card.one => 1
        | Card.exactly n => n
        | Card.all => 1
        | Card.atLeast m => m) ∧
    (∀ (c : Card) (a : ℕ),
        K.required c ≤ a →
          K.consume c a =
            some
              (match c with
              | Card.one => 1
              | Card.exactly n => n
              | Card.all => a
              | Card.atLeast n => a)) ∧
      ∀ (c : Card), ∀ a < K.required c, K.consume c a = none
reading: requiredCount() is 1 for One, n for Exactly(n), 1 for All and m for AtLeast(m);
for every cardinality c and every available ≥ requiredCount(c), consumptionCount(available) returns 1 for One, n for Exactly(n), available for All and available for AtLeast(m);
for every cardinality c and every available < requiredCount(c), consumptionCount(available) fails (none).
quotes: The required count *shall* be 1 for `One` and `All`, `n` for `Exactly(n)` and `m` for `AtLeast(m)`.
*While* `available` is at least the required count, `consumptionCount(available)` *shall* return 1 for `One`, `n` for `Exactly(n)` and `available` for `All` and `AtLeast(m)`.
*If* `consumptionCount(available)` is called with `available` less than the required count, *then* the call *shall* fail with an error.
assumes: A contract is the pair of functions of one implementation; a call that raises (an exception, a panic, an assertion failure) is read as `none`, a call that returns `k` as `some k`. Which error is raised, and its message, are not part of the statement.
AC1 (each variant returns the values of the table) is the first two lines: the first line is the requiredCount column, the second the consumptionCount column on every call the third line allows.
AC2 (calling consumptionCount with insufficient tokens is an error) is the third line.
The counts n and m range over all naturals. That Exactly(n) and AtLeast(m) are built only with n, m ≥ 1 is IO-002 AC1 and IO-004 AC1, not this block's subject; the table holds for 0 too.

'(matching) tokens' in the definition of requiredCount() is read at the granularity of a token count: which tokens of a place count as matching (the ν correlation of NU-020) is decided before the count reaches these functions, so `available` is already the matching count.

That an executor calls consumptionCount only on an enabled transition, where every input place holds its required count, is enablement (CORE-022, IO-005), not this block's subject; that a firing removes exactly consumptionCount(available) tokens is CORE-030's subject (glossary: Consume, bridge lemma `consumes_eq`).

requirements.title: Output place (leaf)
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    OutputSpec t = some (Out.place p) →
      ∀ (d : List N),
        (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦ Produced d p) ∧
          (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦ ∀ (q : N), Produced d q → q = p) ∧
            on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦
              (if ResetArc t p then 0 else TokenCount m p - Consumes t m p) +
                  Deposits d p ≤
                TokenCount m' p
requirements.scope: executors with output validation enabled (the default)
reading: For every transition t whose output spec is the leaf Place(p), and every deposit d:
every firing of t that deposits d puts at least one token in p;
every firing of t that deposits d puts no token in any place other than p;
every firing of t that deposits d, from m to m', leaves p holding at least what p kept (nothing if t has a reset arc on p, else m p minus what t consumed from p) plus what d put in p.
quotes: `Place(place)` is a leaf node of an output spec that names a single output place.
*When* a transition whose output spec is `Place(place)` fires, it *shall* deposit one or more tokens in `place`.
*When* a transition whose output spec is `Place(place)` fires, it *shall not* deposit a token in any other place.

*When* a transition whose output spec is `Place(place)` fires, the marking the firing leaves *shall* hold in `place` the tokens the firing deposited there, in addition to the tokens `place` kept through the firing.
This requirement applies to an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]).
assumes: The firing relation F is that of an executor with output validation enabled, the default (CONC-026). An executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled deposits whatever the action wrote, its Place leaf included, so it may write nothing; CONC-026 lifts IO-010 for it, and the evidence below shows that such an executor's firing relation (io010_skipFire) does not satisfy IO-010 (IO_010_forbids_skip), which is why the scope is stated.

A transition whose output spec is the leaf Place(p) passes every build-time check of its output spec (IO-011 to IO-014: one place, no Timeout, no ForwardInput, one output branch), so the statement ranges over transitions that build; no well-formedness hypothesis is needed.

A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A completion that fails, by an action exception or by IO-015 validation, deposits no outcome and is not a firing here.

The statement covers a transition whose whole output spec is the leaf. A Place leaf inside And, Xor or Timeout contributes its claim {place} to an output branch (IO-015); what that branch must receive is the subject of IO-011, IO-012, IO-013 and IO-015, not of this block.

'One or more tokens' is read on the deposit (glossary: Produced set): p is in the produced set. How many tokens beyond one is not constrained: an output branch is a set of places, and several tokens into p conform (IO-015, IO-016 AC4, CORE-036); the reference semantics deposits exactly one (IO-016). Deposits are compared per place (Deposits d p, Produced d p), never by list order (CORE-036).
The second clause (nothing outside p) reads 'a single output place' together with IO-015's exact-explanation rule: the produced set of a firing of a Place(p) spec is exactly {p}.

AC1 (output spec declares a single place) is structural and holds by construction: the leaf names one place, outPlaces (Place p) = [p] (checked by example below); the statement's hypothesis selects exactly these transitions.

AC2 (produced tokens appear in the place) is the first clause on the deposit and the third clause on the marking. The third clause is a lower bound: it rules out a lost write (the firing reports [p] but leaves p as it was) and a misrouted write (the token lands in another place), also when p already holds tokens. The exact count of p (no extra tokens) is [CORE-030]'s on an input place, [CORE-034]'s on a reset place and [CORE-035]'s third line on every other place; tokens appearing in other places are [CORE-035]'s.

'The tokens place kept' is the glossary's effect of a firing on one place: a reset place keeps none [CORE-034], an input place keeps its count minus the consumption count [CORE-030], [IO-007], any other place keeps its count. Inhibitor and read arcs consume nothing [CORE-031], [CORE-032].

requirements.title: Output And
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build F ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),
      OutputSpec t = some o →
        DupBranch o →
          Build t ≠ none ∧
            (PreOutputChecks t →
              ∀ (p : N), firstDup o = some p → Build t = some (msgDup t p))) ∧
    ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (l r : Out N),
      OutputSpec t = some (l.and r) →
        Builds t →
          (l.and r).findTimeout = none →
            (∀ c ∈ andChildren (l.and r),
                ∀ (d : List N),
                  on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦ ChildReceived d c) ∧
              ∀ (d : List N),
                on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦
                  IO_011_uniqueBranch (l.and r) d
requirements.scope: executors with output validation enabled (the default, CONC-026)
reading: Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg) and F the firings.

For every transition t whose output spec o names a place twice in one output branch (DupBranch), building t fails; and if t's input places are distinct, it fails with IO-011's message for t and the place p the walk of o reports (firstDup o = some p, msgDup t p).
For every transition t that builds (Builds) whose output spec is an And node o with no Timeout node in it:
for every child c of o (nested Ands flattened) and every deposit d, every firing of t that deposits d produces some place that c names;

for every deposit d, every firing of t that deposits d has as its produced set, on the places o names, exactly the places of the output branch at one index of o's branch list, and of no branch at any other index (IO_011_uniqueBranch).
F is the firing relation of an executor with output validation enabled.
quotes: `And(children)` is a node of an output spec that represents a parallel fork in which all children are active.

*When* a transition whose output spec is `And(children)` fires and its action completes, every child, with nested `And`s flattened, *shall* have received tokens: the produced set contains a place that the child names.
The same holds for an `And` nested in the alternative that an inner `Xor` chose: the produced set *shall* equal, on the places the output spec names, one output branch of the output spec.
That output branch is unique, because the output branches of a spec that builds are pairwise distinct sets ([IO-012]).
This requirement applies to an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]).
*If* a single output branch (one choice at every `Xor`, with nested `And`s flattened) names the same place twice, *then* the output spec *shall* be rejected, with

*If* the output spec names a place twice in one output branch, *then* `

` in the message *shall* be the place that the following walk of the spec reports first, so that every implementation names the same place:
A `Place(P)` node and a `ForwardInput(from, P)` node name `P`.
A `Timeout` node walks its child and names the places its child names.
An `Xor` node walks its children left to right.
*If* a child reports a place, *then* the `Xor` *shall* report that place.
Otherwise the `Xor` names the places its children name, each once, in the order the walk first meets them.
An `And` node walks its children left to right.
*If* a child reports a place, *then* the `And` *shall* report that place.
Otherwise, *if* a place the child names, taken in the order the walk first met them, is already named by an earlier child, *then* the `And` *shall* report the first such place.
Otherwise the `And` names the places its children name, each once, in the order the walk first meets them.
The walk reports a place exactly when some output branch names a place twice, because the alternatives of an `Xor` under an `And` are chosen independently of the `And`'s other children.
assumes:
The model is the pair (Build, F). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the witness is the reference builder refBuild, which runs the build-time checks of the Output Composition preamble in order (glossary: Build-time checks). The build error is msgDup, byte for byte: the message of the paragraph 'A place at most once per branch' with the transition's name and

the place the walk reports. The preamble does not place the CORE-030 input-arc check among the output-spec checks; refBuild runs it first, so on a transition with two input arcs on one place the build line only requires that building fails.

The walk is firstDup, through dupScan, clause for clause: steps 1 and 2 are its place, forward and timeout clauses, step 3 its xor clause (xorJoin: the first child's report, else the second's, else the places of both, each once, in first-seen order), step 4 its and clause (andStep at each child: the child's report, else the first place the child names that an earlier child of the And names, else the child's places join the pool). The reference Out is binary: an n-ary And or Xor is right-nested, and dupScan walks a .and met as a child of a .and as part of its parent, so the children of And(c1, ..., cn) are walked as the n-ary node's children. A spec with an And written as a direct child of an And is the one shape the binary Out cannot tell from the flat n-ary node; on it the builders walk the inner And first, the loader's walk (Load.dupWalk, over the spec as written) does the same, and firstDup reads the flat node.

'The walk reports a place exactly when some output branch names a place twice' is the theorem firstDup_eq_none_iff, and the place it reports is named twice in some output branch (firstDup_some); the build line therefore names a place exactly when it rejects a duplicate. AC5's And(Xor(A, B), Xor(B, A)) names B (IO_011_ac5); naming the first place repeated in the first repeating output branch, in IO-016 order, would name A, and that builder violates the build line (IO_011_forbids_firstBranchName).

'Which place the message names' is a constraint on the message only: which transitions build is the first build line together with the other build-time checks, and IO-013's third line ties Builds to the builder.

Ruling D15: the premise PreOutputChecks t (glossary) is the checks the reference builder runs before the output-spec checks: distinct input places ([CORE-030]), input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]) and no input arc and read arc on one place ([EXEC-012]). A transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, so on it the build lines only require that building fails, as for CORE-030 before the ruling.

A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A completion that fails validation (AC3) deposits no outcome and is not a firing here.

Scope: 'applies to an executor with output validation enabled' is read as a restriction on the model: F is the firing relation of such an executor. An executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled is not an F this block speaks of; what it does (an And(A, B) firing that deposits only A, CONC-026 AC4) is exactly what io011_leftOnlyFire models, and this block forbids it of a validating executor (IO_011_forbids_leftOnly).

Scope: the statement quantifies over transitions that build. Building runs the checks of the Output Composition preamble (WellFormedOut: no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every ForwardInput's from an input place, no two output branches at different indices with the same set of places). CORE-022 applies to transitions that build, and a definition the checks reject is not a transition of any net. Build reads one transition definition, so the construction paths that reach the builder are not encoded.

The reference semantics reads an n-ary And as right-nested binary `Out.and` nodes; `andChildren` flattens them back, so the children of And(A, B, C) are A, B and C. Flattening is the recursive reading of 'ALL child output specs must receive tokens': a nested And has received tokens exactly when each of its own children has.

'Received tokens' and 'the produced set' are read on the set of places the deposit touches (Produced, membership in d), and an output branch is read as a set of places (glossary: Output branch): several tokens into one place of the chosen branch conform, and the order of the deposit plays no part (CORE-036). How many tokens is IO-016's subject. Places outside the output spec are not constrained here (CORE-035 ties the marking to the deposit).

'Fires and its action completes' is read on output specs with no Timeout node (findTimeout = none), where every firing ends with its action. An output spec with its one Timeout node anywhere in it, such as And(A, Timeout(d, B)), is IO-013's: the deposit alone cannot tell the timeout outcome from the action outcome, so this block does not restate it there.

The second clause is the recursive reading of 'ALL children receive tokens' below an Xor: an And under the Xor alternative the action chose must give every one of its children tokens, and the Xor itself must take one alternative (IO-012). Without it a deposit [0, 3] for And(Xor(And(0, 1), 2), 3) (a partial write of the chosen alternative) and a deposit [0, 1, 2] for And(0, Xor(1, 2)) (both alternatives) satisfy the first clause.

'That output branch is unique' is read by index: one entry of the IO-016 branch list, one per assignment. On a transition that builds it follows from the existence half and the last build check (IO_011_unique_of_wf), so it adds no constraint on F beyond the scope; no weaker mutant can tell it apart, and the evidence for it is that lemma and IO_011_reference_ambiguous, which shows that without the scope the reference fires And(Q, Xor(P, P)) with two exact branches.
AC1 (requires at least 1 child) is structural and not encoded: the reference output spec has binary And nodes only, so an And with no child cannot be written; an And with one child is that child.
AC2 (after the action completes, all children have received tokens) is the first clause, and the second at every depth.

AC3 (validation failure if a child received no tokens) is read on firings: a completion in which a child received no tokens is not a firing, so the marking never shows it. That the failure is reported (an ActionFailed outcome, the error the user sees) is not observable in the firing relation, which has no events or errors; it is EXEC-030's and IO-015's subject and is not encoded here.

AC4 and the paragraph 'A place at most once per branch' are the build line, and the first build check of WellFormedOut (every output branch Nodup, equivalently no BranchDuplicate, IO_011_noDuplicate_of_wf) for the firing lines' scope: And(P, P), And(P, And(Q, P)) and Xor(A, And(P, P)) are rejected with the message naming P, and Xor(And(P, A), And(P, B)) builds (IO_011_ac4). The construction paths and MOD-020's more specific message are not in the model. The reference semantics still fires And(P, P) depositing two tokens in P (IO_011_reference_fires_duplicate); that transition does not build, so the firing lines do not speak of it.
AC5 (And(Xor(A, B), Xor(B, A)) is rejected naming B) is the build line on that spec, checked under the reference builder (IO_011_ac5).

requirements.title: Output Xor
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] C Build F ↦
  (∀ (o : Out N), C o = none ↔ IO_012_unambiguous o) ∧
    (∀ (o : Out N) (i j : ℕ) (ps : List N),
        C o = some (i, j, ps) ↔ IO_012_reported o i j ps) ∧
      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),
          OutputSpec t = some o →
            ¬IO_012_unambiguous o →
              Build t ≠ none ∧
                (PreOutputChecks t →
                  ¬DupBranch o →
                    timeoutCount o ≤ 1 →
                      xorInTimeout o = false →
                        forwardOutside o = none →
                          (∀ s ∈ forwardSources o, s ∈ inPlaces t) →
                            ∀ (i j : ℕ) (ps : List N),
                              C o = some (i, j, ps) →
                                Build t = some (msgAmbiguous t i j ps))) ∧
        ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (l r : Out N),
          OutputSpec t = some (l.xor r) →
            IO_012_unambiguous (l.xor r) →
              ∀ (d : List N),
                on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m' ∧ ¬IO_012_timeoutLike t m d, shall fun x x_1 ↦
                  ∃ b ∈ (l.xor r).branches, ExactOn (l.xor r) d b
requirements.scope: build check: every transition, on every construction path; firing lines: executors with output validation enabled (the default, CONC-026)
reading: Build check. For every output spec o (the output spec of the transition being built), with bs its output branches (Out.branches, one entry per assignment, numbered from 0):
the check C passes (C o = none) exactly when no two entries of bs at indices i < j claim the same set of places (IO_012_unambiguous; IO_012_clash compares the entries as sets, SameSet);

the check fails reporting (i, j, ps) (C o = some (i, j, ps)) exactly when the entries i < j clash, no entry before j clashes with an earlier one, no entry before i clashes with entry j, and ps is entry i as a list (IO_012_reported).

Building. For every transition t whose output spec o is ambiguous (not IO_012_unambiguous): building t fails (Build t ≠ none); and when every earlier build-time check passes (input places distinct, CORE-030; no output branch naming a place twice, IO-011; at most one Timeout node and no Xor node inside its child, IO-013; no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child and every forward from an input place, IO-014), building fails with IO-012's message for the pair (i, j) and the places ps the check reports (msgAmbiguous t i j ps).

Firing. For every transition t whose output spec is Xor(l, r) and passes the check, every deposit d, and every firing of t under F from m to m' that deposits d and whose deposit is not, place by place, a timeout-outcome deposit of t from m (IO_012_timeoutLike): some output branch b of Xor(l, r) is exact for d: on every place q the output spec names, d puts one or more tokens in q exactly when q is in b (ExactOn).

The second firing line is a consequence, not a clause: on an output spec that passes the check two exact branches would be the same set (both lie within outPlaces), so at most one is exact (theorem IO_012_unique).
`on R, shall Q` reads: every step from m to m' with R m m' satisfies Q m m'; here Q ignores both markings.
quotes: `Xor(children)` is an output spec node with two or more children; it represents a decision point where the action chooses one child.

*When* a transition whose output spec is `Xor(children)` fires and the firing ends with its action, its produced set *shall* equal, on the places the output spec names, one output branch of the output spec.

*When* a transition whose output spec is `Xor(children)` fires and the firing ends with its action, its produced set *shall not* equal, on the places the output spec names, two output branches that take different children at some `Xor` node.
This requirement applies to an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]).
A firing ends with its action when it does not end with the timeout outcome ([IO-013]).

Deposits are compared per place ([CORE-036]): a firing whose deposit puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout-outcome deposit of the transition from the same marking may have ended with the timeout outcome, and the two lines above do not constrain it.
An *assignment* of an output spec chooses one child at each `Xor` node it reaches ([IO-015]).
`Xor` nodes are told apart by their position in the spec, never by what they contain, so `Xor(P, P)` has two assignments.
Two assignments are *distinct* when they choose different children at some `Xor` node that both reach.
*If* two distinct assignments of a transition's output spec claim the same set of places, at any depth of the spec, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with
Enumerate the output branches of the spec per [IO-016], numbered from 0 in enumeration order (the numbering of the virtual transitions `<t>_b<i>` of [VER-001]).
The enumeration lists exactly one branch per assignment, so two branches at different indices come from distinct assignments.
Read each branch as the set of places it names, a `ForwardInput(from, to)` naming `to`.
Visit the branches in index order.
The first branch `j` whose set equals the set of an earlier branch fails the check, and `i` is the smallest index of such an earlier branch.
If no branch fails, the check passes.
`<places>` lists the places of branch `i` by name, separated by `, `, in the order the spec as written names them (leaves left to right).
An implementation MAY decide the check without enumerating every branch, provided it reports the same `i`, `j` and `<places>`.
A transition that builds therefore has pairwise distinct output branches, so at most one output branch equals any produced set, and the second line above holds of every firing of such a transition.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A completion that fails, by an action exception (EXEC-030) or by IO-015 validation, deposits no outcome and is not a firing here: an action failure does not end the firing with its action.

F models an executor with output validation enabled, the default; an executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled is not constrained by the firing line (scope). The build check is independent of any executor: C is the check itself.

The check is modelled by what it reports, not by its text: C o = some (i, j, ps) stands for the message `output spec of transition '<t>' is ambiguous: output branches <i> and <j> both claim {<places>}; no write can tell them apart (IO-012)`, with <places> the names of ps joined by ', '. The transition name, the rendering of names, the message text, and the claim that it is byte-identical across implementations are not in the model; the cross-language tests of AC5 pin them.

The check C is stated for one output spec in isolation; the third line ties it to the builder. In the builder it runs last of the build-time checks (the Output Composition preamble: CORE-030's input check, then IO-011, IO-013's two checks, IO-014 before it), so a spec that an earlier check rejects reports that check's message instead: the third line asks for IO-012's message only when every earlier check passes, and otherwise only that building fails. The message is the glossary's msgAmbiguous, the text the markdown gives. That the check runs on every construction path (builders, composition, channel merge, fusion) and that no executor option skips it is read as: every transition in a net has an output spec C passes. The firing line is stated for such transitions; the model has no construction paths to enumerate.

'An implementation MAY decide the check without enumerating every branch' is the extensional reading: the block constrains C only by what it returns, so any algorithm that returns the same (i, j, ps) satisfies it. IO_012_check is one such algorithm, the enumeration of the numbered steps.

Place identity is equality on N, the implementation's own Place equality (names in TypeScript, Rust and Python, name and token type in Java; CORE-002, MOD-024). A ForwardInput(from, to) claims `to`, a Timeout its child's claim (Out.branches).

Branches are numbered by the reference enumeration Out.branches over the right-nested binary Out: an n-ary Xor(c₁, …, cₙ) is xor c₁ (xor c₂ … cₙ) and concatenates its children's lists in child order; an n-ary And is the cartesian product with the first child varying slowest. These are IO-016's lists and VER-001's <t>_b<i> numbering, so the binary nesting changes no index.

'Receives tokens' is read as IO-015's exact explanation, as AC4 directs: a child whose output branch is a strict subset of the produced set has received tokens but is not satisfied. Read literally, `Xor(And(A, B, C), And(A, B))` writing {A, B} would have two children receiving tokens; under the exact reading only the second child's branch equals it.

The produced set is compared on the places the output spec names (outPlaces), as IO-015 compares on declared places: a token in a place the spec never names is CORE-072's business. A token in a named place outside the selected branch still breaks the firing line (IO-015 AC9). A branch fixes which places receive tokens, not how many (glossary: Output branch): several tokens into one place of the branch conform.

A firing ends with its action unless it is the timeout outcome (glossary: Timeout outcome, IO-013); the abstract firing relation does not label the outcome, so a firing whose deposit puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout-outcome deposit of t from the same marking is not checked (IO-012), whatever the order of its tokens. When the action happens to write such a deposit, that firing is not checked either. An Xor that contains a Timeout node is otherwise covered.

The firing line covers a transition whose whole output spec is an Xor. An Xor nested inside And or Timeout is covered by IO-015, which validates every Xor an assignment reaches. The build check covers every output spec, an Xor at any depth included: And(Q, Xor(P, P)) is rejected.

AC1 (at least two children) is structural: the binary xor node has the two children l and r, and an n-ary Xor nests as xor c₁ (xor c₂ … cₙ) (checked by example below); the reference loader rejects an xor with fewer than two children.

AC2 (exactly one child received tokens) is the firing line (at least one exact branch, so one child of the top Xor) together with its consequence IO_012_unique (not two). An output branch takes exactly one child of the top Xor.

AC3 (zero branches satisfied → validation error) is the firing line: such a completion is not a firing. The test derivation's 'action produces to both' case is also the firing line under the exact reading: Xor(P1, P2) has no output branch {P1, P2}.

AC4 (two branches whose claims are the same set never reach a firing) is the build check: such a spec does not pass C, and the firing line is stated only for specs that pass. The strict-subset remark of AC4 is the exact reading above: Xor(And(A, B, C), And(A, B)) passes the check (checked by example below).

AC5 (the rejected and accepted specs and their reported pairs and places) is checked by example on IO_012_check below, with the places A, B, C, P, Q, a named by the numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The Timeout duration d is not in the reference Out. The composition case (two output ports in different alternatives bound to one host place) is the check applied to the composed spec; composition itself is MOD-024's model, not this block's.
The Test derivation's build cases are AC5's; its firing cases are AC3's.

Ruling D15: the premise PreOutputChecks t (glossary) is the checks the reference builder runs before the output-spec checks: distinct input places ([CORE-030]), input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]) and no input arc and read arc on one place ([EXEC-012]). A transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, so on it the build lines only require that building fails, as for CORE-030 before the ruling.

requirements.title: Output timeout
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] Build F T ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),
      OutputSpec t = some o →
        2 ≤ timeoutCount o →
          Build t ≠ none ∧
            (PreOutputChecks t →
              ¬DupBranch o → Build t = some (msgTimeouts t (timeoutCount o)))) ∧
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N), Builds t → Build t = none) ∧
      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
          Build t = none →
            ∀ (d : List N), on fun m m' ↦ T t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦ F t m d m') ∧
        (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
            Build t = none →
              ∀ (d : List N),
                on fun m m' ↦ T t m d m', shall fun m x ↦
                  ∃ d₀,
                    TimeoutOutcome t (Consumes t m) d₀ ∧
                      ∀ (p : N), Deposits d p = Deposits d₀ p) ∧
