          (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
              Build t = none →
                ∀ (m : CountMarking N),
                  Enabled t m →
                    ∀ (d : List N),
                      TimeoutOutcome t (Consumes t m) d → ∃ m', T t m d m') ∧
            (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
                Build t = none →
                  HasTimeout t →
                    ∀ (d : List N),
                      on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦
                        T t m d m' ∨
                          ∃ b, OutputBranch t b ∧ ∀ (p : N), Produced d p ↔ p ∈ b) ∧
              ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),
                OutputSpec t = some o →
                  timeoutCount o ≤ 1 →
                    xorInTimeout o = true →
                      Build t ≠ none ∧
                        (PreOutputChecks t →
                          ¬DupBranch o → Build t = some (msgXorInTimeout t))
reading: Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg), F the firings and T the firings that end with the timeout outcome.

For every transition t whose output spec o holds two or more Timeout nodes, building t fails; and if t's input places are distinct and no output branch of o names a place twice, it fails with the IO-013 message for t and the number of Timeout nodes in o.

Every transition that passes every build check (distinct input places, no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every forward from an input place, no two output branches claiming one set of places) builds.
For every transition t that builds: every firing of t in T is a firing in F, with the same deposit and target marking.
For every transition t that builds: every firing of t in T from m deposits, place by place, exactly the tokens of the timeout outcome of t (for what t consumes at m), and nothing else.
For every transition t that builds: from every marking m at which t is enabled, every timeout outcome d of t (for what t consumes at m) is the deposit of some firing in T.
For every transition t that builds and whose output spec has a Timeout node, every firing of t in F is in T, or has as its produced set exactly the places of one output branch of t.

For every transition t whose output spec o holds at most one Timeout node and an Xor node at any depth of that node's child (xorInTimeout), building t fails; and if t's input places are distinct and no output branch of o names a place twice, it fails with IO-013's Xor message for t (msgXorInTimeout).
quotes: `Timeout(duration, child)` is a node of an output spec that gives the action of a firing a budget of `duration` to complete.
*If* the action does not complete within `duration`, the firing *shall* end with the timeout outcome: it is abandoned, and it deposits the tokens of `child`.
*When* a firing ends with the timeout outcome, it *shall not* deposit any output of the action, so the marking receives the tokens of `child` and nothing else.
*If* an output spec holds more than one `Timeout` node, whether one is nested in the child of another or they sit apart, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with
where `<n>` is the number of `Timeout` nodes in the spec.
The check runs when the transition is built, on every construction path, as the check of [IO-011] does.
A transition that builds therefore has at most one timeout outcome, and the `child` of its `Timeout` holds no `Timeout` node.
The executor, not the action, makes the deposit of the timeout outcome, so nothing chooses among alternatives inside the `Timeout` child.
*If* the child of an output spec's `Timeout` node holds an `Xor` node at any depth, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with
The check runs after the `Timeout` count check above, so the spec it sees holds at most one `Timeout` node.
The timeout outcome of a transition that builds therefore deposits in one fixed set of places: every place the `Timeout` child names.
assumes: The model is the triple (Build, F, T). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the reference builder refBuild runs the checks the model can see in the order of the output composition preamble of spec/02-input-output-specs.md. F is the firing relation and T the firings that end with the timeout outcome (glossary: Timeout outcome), each read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A plain FireRel cannot carry T: on Xor(Place 0, Timeout(Place 1)) the timeout deposit [1] is also the action branch {1}, so a timed-out firing that deposits the sibling branch [0] would look like an action firing. The witness triple is refBuild, RefFire and refTimeoutOutcomeFire.

The build error is msgTimeouts, byte for byte: output spec of transition '<t>' has <n> Timeout nodes; an output spec has at most one, nested or not (IO-013), with <n> the number of Timeout nodes in the spec, nested and sibling ones alike (timeoutCount). The preamble's order puts the IO-011 check (a place twice in one output branch) first, so on such a spec the message is IO-011's and the second line only requires that building fails. The preamble does not place the CORE-030 input-arc check, so on a transition with two input arcs on one place the second line likewise only requires that building fails.

'On every construction path' is read as: Build is the one builder every construction path goes through (builders, composition, channel merge, fusion), so a transition that a path yields builds exactly when Build accepts it. Which paths exist is not in the model.

The third line is the converse that makes 'builds' checkable (AC7's specs that build): a transition passing the checks before the output spec (CORE-030, the IO-002/IO-004 input counts and EXEC-012's input-and-read check, PreOutputChecks) and every build check of the output composition preamble builds. The checks are the glossary terms Builds and WellFormedOut, the build-time checks of IO-011, IO-012, IO-013 and IO-014; checks the model cannot see (AC1's positive duration, a spec that names no place) are outside it.

A transition that builds has at most one Timeout node, so its timeout outcome is the one Timeout node's child (Out.findTimeout finds it), and that child holds no Timeout node. The firing lines are stated for transitions that build only: a transition building rejects is not a transition of any net (CORE-022) and never fires.

The duration is not in the model, so whether the budget expires is nondeterministic: from every marking at which t is enabled, the action may overrun it. The sixth line therefore reads 'if the action does not complete within duration, the firing shall end with the timeout outcome' as 'the timeout outcome is always one of the ways a firing of t can end'. That overrunning forces the timeout, and that completing in time rules it out, are statements about time that a model of untimed steps cannot express.

'It is abandoned' is the action's output being excluded, which the fifth line states for the deposit. Whether the action is stopped is the side-effect paragraph that follows the first paragraph, not encoded.

'The marking receives the tokens of child and nothing else' is read at the deposit (fifth line). Which marking a firing leads to is the effect rule of the glossary term Fire (CORE-030, CORE-034, CORE-035); the fourth line ties every timed-out firing to a firing of F, so that rule applies to it.

'The tokens of child' is the glossary term Timeout outcome, as the reference reads it (Out.timeoutDeposits): one token per Place leaf of child, the product at every And, and one token in to per token consumed from from at every ForwardInput (IO-014), counted per place, so the order of the deposit list does not matter (CORE-036). Token values and created_at (the minted tokens of AC3, forwarded values and their stamps, IO-014 AC5) are below the count granularity.

The eighth line is the paragraph 'One fixed timeout deposit'. Its message is msgXorInTimeout, byte for byte. Any Xor at any depth of the Timeout child counts, under an And or a ForwardInput's sibling included (hasXor). It runs after the Timeout count check, as the premise timeoutCount o ≤ 1 states: with two Timeout nodes the message is the first line's. The preamble's order puts the IO-011 check before it, so on a spec that names a place twice in one output branch the eighth line only requires that building fails, and on a transition with two input arcs on one place likewise (CORE-030). 'The executor, not the action, makes the deposit' is the reason the markdown gives and is not a separate constraint.

'The timeout outcome of a transition that builds therefore deposits in one fixed set of places' is a consequence, not a clause: on a transition that builds the Timeout child holds no Xor node, so Out.timeoutDeposits of the child has one entry and the fifth and sixth lines name one deposit (theorem IO_013_one_fixed_deposit, from the glossary's timeoutOutcome_unique). Without the check the reference offers one timeout outcome per alternative of an Xor in the child (IO_013_reference_xorChild_two_outcomes).

The seventh line is AC5 for a firing that does not report the timeout outcome: it ended with its action, whose produced set is one output branch (IO-015, exact explanation; how many tokens per place is IO-016's). A deposit that merges a timeout outcome with output the action wrote and reports it as an action firing is neither, unless its places happen to form a whole output branch, in which case it is a legal action firing and no observation of the marking can tell the two apart. The line is a requirement on an executor with output validation enabled, the default (CONC-026); F models such an executor, as RefFire does. With the skip enabled an action firing deposits the action's write and the line is not claimed of it, while the timed-out lines hold under every executor: CONC-026 skips nothing on the timeout outcome.
AC1 (duration must be positive) is a build-time validation of the duration, which the model does not carry; not encoded.
AC2 (action completes within duration, normal output validation) is the produced-set disjunct of the seventh line; the validation itself is IO-015's subject.

AC3 (action exceeds duration, every place the timeout child names receives tokens: one minted token for a Place, the forwarded tokens for a ForwardInput) is the fifth and sixth lines, read on token counts.
AC4 (an ActionTimedOut event is emitted on timeout) is an event-store obligation (EVT-009); the firing relation has no events, so it is not encoded.

AC5 (output produced before the budget expired is discarded, the marking receiving the tokens of the timeout child's one fixed set of places and nothing else; a partial write under an Xor sibling is not a second satisfied branch) is the fifth line for a firing in T and the seventh for a firing outside it; 'one fixed set' is IO_013_one_fixed_deposit.

AC6 (a TimeoutException the action raises is an ordinary action failure, not the timeout branch) is about which trigger ends the firing; an action failure deposits no outcome (EXEC-030) and is not a firing in this model, so it is not encoded.

AC7 is the second and third lines: its three rejected specs (Timeout(d, Timeout(e, P)), Xor(Timeout(d, A), Timeout(e, B)), And(Timeout(d, A), Xor(B, Timeout(e, C)))) fail with the message for n = 2 and its two accepted specs (Xor(A, Timeout(d, B)), Timeout(d, And(A, B))) build, under the reference builder (IO_013_ac7_rejected, IO_013_ac7_builds).

AC8 is the eighth and third lines: its two rejected specs (Timeout(d, Xor(A, B)), Xor(C, Timeout(d, And(A, Xor(B, D))))) fail with the Xor message, and its two accepted specs (Xor(A, Timeout(d, B)) and, with i an input place, Timeout(d, And(A, ForwardInput(i, B)))) build, under the reference builder (IO_013_ac8_rejected, IO_013_ac8_builds).
The test derivation's build cases are AC7's and AC8's; its timing case (an action sleeping past its budget, the event) is outside the model: the duration and the event store are not in it.

Ruling D15: the premise PreOutputChecks t (glossary) is the checks the reference builder runs before the output-spec checks: distinct input places ([CORE-030]), input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]) and no input arc and read arc on one place ([EXEC-012]). A transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, so on it the build lines only require that building fails, as for CORE-030 before the ruling.

requirements.title: Output ForwardInput
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build T ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N) (src dst : N),
      OutputSpec t = some o → forwardOutside o = some (src, dst) → Build t ≠ none) ∧
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N) (src dst : N),
        OutputSpec t = some o →
          forwardOutside o = some (src, dst) →
            PreOutputChecks t →
              ¬DupBranch o →
                timeoutCount o ≤ 1 →
                  xorInTimeout o = false → Build t = some (msgForward t src dst)) ∧
      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N) (src : N),
          OutputSpec t = some o →
            src ∈ forwardSources o → src ∉ inPlaces t → Build t ≠ none) ∧
        (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N), Builds t → Build t = none) ∧
          ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (src dst : N),
            (∀ (o : Out N), OutputSpec t = some o → timeoutCount o ≤ 1) →
              TimeoutForwards t src dst →
                ∀ (d : List N),
                  on fun m m' ↦ T t m d m', shall fun m x ↦
                    ∃ e,
                      TimeoutOutcome t (Consumes t m) e ∧
                        (∀ (p : N), Deposits e p ≤ Deposits d p) ∧
                          ∀ (p : N), Deposits d p ≤ Deposits e p
reading: Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg) and T the firings that end with the timeout outcome.
For every transition t whose output spec o has a ForwardInput(from, to) outside the child of a Timeout node, the first in pre-order, building t fails;

and if t's input places are distinct, no output branch of o names a place twice, o has at most one Timeout node and no Xor node inside its Timeout child, building t fails with the IO-014 message naming t, from and to.
For every transition t whose output spec has a ForwardInput from a place that is not one of t's input places, building t fails.

Every transition that passes every build check (distinct input places, no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every forward from an input place, no two output branches claiming one set of places) builds.

For every transition t whose output spec has at most one Timeout node and a ForwardInput(from, to) anywhere in that node's child (also under And or Xor), every deposit d and every firing of t from m in T that deposits d, there is one timeout deposit e of the Timeout child, built with every ForwardInput(a, b) of the child putting in b one token per token the firing consumes from a, such that e puts no more tokens than d in any place (no consumed token is lost, at any forward of the child) and d puts no more tokens than e in any place (one token per consumed token, none extra).
quotes: `ForwardInput(from, to)` is a node of an output spec that, on the timeout outcome, deposits in `to` the tokens a firing consumed from its input place `from`.
*If* a `ForwardInput` node of an output spec is not inside the child of a `Timeout` node, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with
naming the first such node in the order the spec is written (pre-order, children left to right).
The check runs when the transition is built, on every construction path, as the check of [IO-011] does.

*When* a firing ends with the timeout outcome, every `ForwardInput(from, to)` in the `Timeout` child *shall* deposit in `to` one token for each token the firing consumed from `from`, carrying the token's value, in consumption order.
The count *shall* be the consumption count of the input arc on `from` ([IO-007]): 1 for `One`, `n` for `Exactly(n)`, and the whole drained batch for `All` and `AtLeast(m)`.

*If* a firing consumed more than one token from `from`, *then* the forward *shall not* deposit fewer tokens in `to` than the firing consumed; in particular it *shall not* forward only the first consumed token.
*If* a firing consumed no token from `from`, which a declared input cannot do but a mis-declared spec can, *then* the forward *shall* deposit no token in `to`.
assumes: The model is the pair (Build, T). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the reference builder refBuild runs the CORE-030 input-arc check and then the output-spec checks in the order of the output composition preamble of spec/02-input-output-specs.md (IO-011, IO-013's Timeout count, IO-013's Xor inside the Timeout child, IO-014, IO-014 AC3, IO-012), with each message byte for byte except CORE-030's, which the spec does not give. Place names are rendered with the place type's ToString.

T is the relation of firings that end with the timeout outcome (glossary: Timeout outcome), read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the Timeout child's tokens (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A plain FireRel cannot be used: on Timeout(ForwardInput(from, to)) the action branch [to] and a forward of one token are the same deposit. The witness refTimedOutFire is the part of RefFire whose outcome is a timedOut choice (refTimedOutFire_refFire). That the resulting marking receives d is the effect rule (CORE-030, CORE-034, CORE-035) on the plain firing relation, not restated here.

The build error is msgForward, byte for byte: output spec of transition '<t>' uses ForwardInput('<from>', '<to>') outside the child of a Timeout node; a forward deposits only on the timeout outcome (IO-014). 'Not inside the child of a Timeout node' and 'the first such node' are forwardOutside: the pre-order walk, children left to right, that does not enter a Timeout node. The preamble's order runs the IO-011 check (a place twice in one output branch) and the IO-013 checks (more than one Timeout node, an Xor node inside the Timeout child) first, so on such a spec the message is theirs, and the second line only requires that building fails; CORE-030's input-arc check is not placed by the preamble and is treated the same way.

'On every construction path' is read as: Build is the one builder every construction path goes through (builders, composition, channel merge, fusion), so a transition that a path yields builds exactly when Build accepts it. Which paths exist is not in the model. No executor option reaches Build (CONC-026).

The fifth line is the converse that makes 'builds' checkable (AC7's specs that build): a transition passing the checks before the output spec (CORE-030, the IO-002/IO-004 input counts and EXEC-012's input-and-read check, PreOutputChecks) and every build check of the output composition preamble builds. The checks are the glossary terms Builds and WellFormedOut, the same checks IO-013 reads.

The firing line is stated for every transition whose output spec has at most one Timeout node, not only for transitions that build: a transition with two or more Timeout nodes is rejected (IO-013) and has no single Timeout child, so no reading of 'the Timeout child' is claimed there, while a transition with a forward from a non-input place, rejected by the fourth line, is still covered, which is what keeps the fourth quote (no input consumed, nothing forwarded) checkable. A transition with one Timeout node has one Timeout child, the one Out.findTimeout finds.
'The `ForwardInput(from, to)` node of an output spec that, on the timeout outcome, deposits in `to` the tokens a firing consumed' (first quote) is the firing line, which says how many.

'Every ForwardInput(from, to) in the Timeout child' includes a ForwardInput nested under And or Xor. On a transition that builds the child holds no Xor node (IO-013), so it has one timeout deposit (glossary: timeoutOutcome_unique); the line is also stated for transitions that do not build, where an Xor child has several timeout deposits and which one a firing chose is visible only in the whole deposit, so the statement compares d place by place with one timeout deposit e of the child (glossary: Timeout outcome, TimeoutOutcome); deposits are compared per place, so the order of the deposit list does not matter (CORE-036). This also fixes the tokens the child's Place leaves put in, which is IO-013's subject (AC5); it is restated here only because it is what identifies the chosen alternative. Comparing only the place `to` would let a forward-first firing pass whenever another alternative of the child happens to put the same count in `to`.

'The count' (sixth quote) is the firing's consumption from `from`, the glossary term Consume (Consumes t m from), which is IO-007's consumption count of the input arc on `from` (bridge lemma consumes_eq) and 0 for a place with no input arc. The two bounds of the firing line together say d equals e place by place, with one existential e for both; they are split so that losing tokens and inventing tokens are refuted separately.

The seventh quote (no forward of fewer tokens, not only the first) is the first bound. The eighth quote (no input consumed, nothing forwarded) is the second bound, e having no forwarded token where Consumes t m from = 0.

The sentence '*When* a `ForwardInput` forwards a consumed token, the token it deposits in `to` *shall* carry the consumed token's `created_at` as well as its value.' is token metadata (a value and a creation stamp) below the count granularity of the firing semantics, which has no token values or stamps; it is not encoded, and neither is the paragraph around it (the TIME-015 exception, the NU-022 tie-break).

AC1 (from must be a declared input place, validated at build time) and AC3 (an invalid from reference is a build error) are the fourth line. Which forward AC3's existing message names when several are invalid is not said by the text; the reference builder names the first in pre-order, and the statement does not constrain the message.
AC2 (one token per consumed token, preserving values and consumption order) is the firing line for its count; values and consumption order are below the count granularity and are not encoded.
AC4 (All or Exactly(n) with N tokens consumed puts exactly N in `to`) is the two bounds together, with Consumes giving N for Exactly(n) and the whole place for All.

AC5 (a forwarded token's created_at equals the original's and is not re-stamped from the epoch clock, while a minted recovery token is, in every implementation) is token metadata below the count granularity and is not encoded.

AC6 (every analysis deposits what the executor deposits) is about the verifier's branch expansion (IO-016, VER-001), not about firings or building; Novel/ForwardDeposit.lean proves it for the flattened rows.

AC7 is the second, third and fifth lines: its three rejected specs (ForwardInput(a, b), Xor(c, ForwardInput(a, b)), And(c, Xor(e, ForwardInput(a, b)))) fail with the message naming a and b, and its two accepted specs (Timeout(d, ForwardInput(a, b)), Xor(c, Timeout(d, And(e, ForwardInput(a, b))))) build, under the reference builder with a an input place (IO_014_ac7_rejected, IO_014_ac7_builds).

Ruling D15: the premise PreOutputChecks t (glossary) is the checks the reference builder runs before the output-spec checks: distinct input places ([CORE-030]), input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]) and no input arc and read arc on one place ([EXEC-012]). A transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, so on it the build lines only require that building fails, as for CORE-030 before the ruling.

requirements.title: Output Validation
requirements.statement:
fun {N} V ↦
  (∀ (o : Out N) (d : List N) (i : ℕ),
      ExactAssignment o d i → (∀ (j : ℕ), ExactAssignment o d j → j = i) → V o d = true) ∧
    (∀ (o : Out N) (d : List N), (∀ (i : ℕ), ¬ExactAssignment o d i) → V o d = false) ∧
      ∀ (o : Out N) (d : List N) (i j : ℕ),
        i ≠ j → ExactAssignment o d i → ExactAssignment o d j → V o d = false
reading: For every declared output spec o and every deposit d, with assignment i of o claiming the i-th entry of Out.branches o:
if some assignment i claims exactly the produced set of d and every assignment that does is i, validation of d against o succeeds;
if no assignment claims exactly the produced set of d, validation fails;
if two different assignments i ≠ j both claim exactly the produced set of d, validation fails.
quotes: An *assignment* selects exactly one child at each `Xor` node it reaches; nodes beneath an unselected `Xor` child are never evaluated.
*If* exactly one assignment claims a set *equal* to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* succeed.
*If* no assignment claims a set equal to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* fail, because nothing explains what was written.
*If* two or more assignments claim a set equal to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* fail, because the write is genuinely ambiguous.
For a transition that builds, no two assignments claim the same set ([IO-012]), so on a firing this third case does not arise.
The comparison is over **sets of places**: a spec names places, not counts, so an action that deposits several tokens into one claimed place conforms.
assumes: A validator is the verdict function of one implementation: its inputs are the declared output spec and the tokens the completed action produced, as a deposit (a list of places with repetition); its output is success (true) or violation (false). The produced set is the places of the deposit (glossary: Produced set).

When an action completes, an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]), shall validate its produced set against the transition's output spec. This sentence is the trigger and is not encoded: the block fixes the verdict of the check, not when it runs. An executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled runs no check, so the verdict constrains nothing there (CONC-026's subject). A completion that fails validation deposits no outcome and is not a firing (glossary: Fire); a transition with no output spec has nothing to validate; the timeout outcome (IO-013) does not complete the action and is not validated.

Assignments are counted, not their claims: two assignments that claim the same set are two (Xor(A, A) with A produced has two exact assignments and fails). Out.branches enumerates one claim per assignment, in the claim rules of the bullet list; n-ary And and Xor are read as right-nested binary nodes, which changes neither the number of assignments, their claims nor their IO-016 order.

The verdict function is total: the three clauses range over every output spec, those IO-012 rejects at build included. The sentence 'For a transition that builds, no two assignments claim the same set' is a consequence, not a clause: the glossary's WellFormedOut is the build-time constraint on an output spec, and on a spec satisfying it no two different assignments are exact for any deposit (theorem IO_015_wf_noAmbiguous), so under IO-015 the verdict is success exactly when some assignment is exact (theorem IO_015_wf_iff). The theorems use only its IO-012 conjunct, pairwise distinct branch sets.

The set-of-places sentence is a consequence, not a clause: the three clauses fix the verdict from the number of exact assignments (theorem IO_015_determines), and that number reads only the produced set (theorem IO_015_setOnly). Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036): two deposits with the same count in every place, in any order, get the same verdict (theorem IO_015_perPlace).
AC1 (conforming output → success) is the first clause, 'conforming' read as 'exactly one exact assignment'.

AC2 (non-conforming output → failure event emitted) and AC3 (consumed input tokens are not restored on failure) are executor behaviour on a failed completion ('Validation failure is treated as a transition failure', EVT-007); the failure is not a firing of the reference semantics, which has no failed completion, so neither is encoded here.
AC4 (zero exact assignments → violation; two or more → violation) is the second and third clauses.
AC5 (Xor(And(A, B, C), And(A, B)) with A, B, C produced → success) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 (theorem IO_015_ac5).

AC6 (output spec declared, action produces nothing → validation failure on every firing) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 and every output spec (theorem IO_015_ac6): every claim names at least one place, so none equals the empty produced set. That the built-in passthrough is rejected before execution is CORE-043's subject.

AC7 (mid-action publication) fixes which tokens make up the deposit the validator sees (published places count) and that published tokens stay in the marking on a violation; both are executor behaviour outside the verdict function and are not encoded. With the published places in the deposit, the AC7 verdicts (And(A, B) with A, B produced → success; with A only → violation) are checked on the reference validator.

AC8 (And is unordered) is not a separate clause: a claim is compared as a set, and permuting the children of an And permutes the assignments and the order of places within a claim. It is checked for the AC8 pair And(A, Xor(D, E)) / And(Xor(D, E), A) on every produced set drawn from A, D, E and one foreign place, the empty one included (theorem IO_015_ac8).
AC9 (Xor(And(A, C), B) with B and C produced → violation) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 (theorem IO_015_ac9).
AC10 (Xor(And(A, Xor(D, E)), A) with only A produced → success) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 (theorem IO_015_ac10).

requirements.title: Output validation: a validated write is deposited
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),
    OutputSpec t = some o →
      ∀ (m : CountMarking N),
        Enabled t m →
          ∀ (d : List N),
            (∃ i, ExactAssignment o d i ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ), ExactAssignment o d j → j = i) →
              ∃ m', F t m d m'
requirements.scope: executors with output validation enabled (the default, CONC-026)
reading: For every transition t with output spec o, every marking m at which t is enabled and every deposit d such that exactly one assignment of o claims exactly the produced set of d:
some firing of t from m deposits d.
quotes: *If* exactly one assignment claims a set *equal* to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* succeed.
The comparison is over **sets of places**: a spec names places, not counts, so an action that deposits several tokens into one claimed place conforms.
assumes: The firing-level reading of the IO-015 sentences quoted: the block IO_015 fixes the validator's verdict; this one ties the verdict to firings. An action may write any tokens (glossary: Deposit), a completion that passes validation deposits what the action wrote, and one that fails is not a firing (glossary: Fire). So every write that validation accepts is the deposit of some firing. 'Conforms' is read as 'passes validation and is deposited', as IO-016 AC4 says of such a write ('the tokens are deposited regardless').
Timing and priority play no part: whether the action completes within a Timeout budget is nondeterministic (IO-013), so a validated write is always one way a firing can end.

CORE-036 compares deposits per place and asks only that the places a firing deposits in be the places of one output branch, each receiving one or more tokens, so it allows such a deposit: both blocks hold of the validated-write executor (theorem CORE_036_IO_015_firing_consistent).

requirements.title: Branch Enumeration
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] E ↦
  (∀ (p : N), E (Out.place p) = [{p}]) ∧
    (∀ (s d : N), E (Out.forward s d) = [{d}]) ∧
      (∀ (l r : Out N), E (l.and r) = branchCross (E l) (E r)) ∧
        (∀ (l r : Out N), E (l.xor r) = E l ++ E r) ∧ ∀ (c : Out N), E c.timeout = E c
reading: Place(p) enumerates exactly the one branch {p};
ForwardInput(from, to) enumerates exactly the one branch {to};
And(l, r) enumerates, for each branch x of l in order and, within it, each branch y of r in order, the branch x ∪ y, and nothing else;
Xor(l, r) enumerates the branches of l, in order, then the branches of r, in order, each as often as it occurs there, and nothing else;
Timeout(c) enumerates exactly the branches of c, in order.
quotes: The branch enumeration of a `Place` node *shall* be one output branch, holding that place.
The branch enumeration of a `ForwardInput(from, to)` node *shall* be one output branch, holding `to`.

The branch enumeration of an `And` node *shall* be the Cartesian product of its children's branch enumerations: one output branch for each choice of one output branch per child, holding the union of the chosen output branches, with the first child's choice varying slowest.
The branch enumeration of an `Xor` node *shall* be the union of its children's branch enumerations: one output branch for each output branch of each child, the first child's output branches first.
The branch enumeration of a `Timeout` node *shall* be its child's branch enumeration.
assumes: A branch enumeration is a function from an output spec alone to a list of output branches, so it is static by its type. A branch is a set of places (`Finset`), as the text says ("a set of places: it says which places receive a token when the branch is taken, not how many"). The list keeps multiplicity (`Xor(P, P)` has two branches) and its order: the lines compare lists with equality, so the enumeration is fixed exactly (`IO_016_unique`). The order is normative because the analyses expand a transition into its branches "in the order above" and name the virtual transitions `<t>_b<i>` in enumeration order ([VER-001]), which the byte-identical SMT scripts carry ([VER-013]).

An n-ary `And` or `Xor` is read as right-nested binary nodes, as `Reference.Out` writes it. List append and the lexicographic Cartesian product are associative and union is associative, so the nesting changes neither the branches nor their order: the n-ary product with the first child slowest is the right-nested product of binary ones.

A branch read as a set loses a repeated claim: `And(P, P)` enumerates {P}, while the reference `Out.branches` lists [P, P]. IO-011 rejects such a spec when it is built, so on every buildable spec the two agree (`IO_016_card_of_wf`: each set has as many places as the list it reads).

The list has one entry per assignment (IO-015), counted by position, so on a spec that builds no two entries are the same set: IO-012 rejects at build time any spec with two distinct assignments claiming one set, and its check enumerates per IO-016 and compares the entries as sets in index order (the numbering of VER-001's `<t>_b<i>`). The paragraph saying so is a consequence of IO-012's build check, not a further constraint on the enumeration; it is derived, not stated (`IO_016_nodup_of_wf`). The enumeration itself is defined on every spec, ambiguous ones included, because the build check is computed from it.

A spec that builds holds at most one `Timeout` node, and a `ForwardInput` only inside that node's child (IO-013, IO-014). The `Timeout` and `ForwardInput` lines still fix the enumeration on every spec: the enumeration is a total function on output specs, and the build checks read it before a spec is known to build.

AC1 (`And(P1, P2)` → {P1, P2}) follows from lines 1 and 3; AC2 (`Xor(P1, P2)` → {P1}, {P2}) from lines 1 and 4; AC3 (`Xor(And(P1, P2), P3)` → {P1, P2}, {P3}) from lines 1, 3 and 4. The non-vacuity theorem checks all three on the reference enumeration.

AC4 (the executor's WARN log-message event when a validated firing deposits more than one token in a place its matched branch names, at most once per transition per execution) is an [EVT-013] event of a running executor, and is skipped with the rest of validation by the CONC-026 option. Neither the branch enumeration nor the firing relation has an event store or an execution; it is not encoded here and needs a behaviour block over executions.

A branch fixes which places receive tokens, not how many: with output validation enabled, a firing that ends with its action deposits one or more tokens in each place of one output branch and none in any other (glossary: Output branch, IO-015, CORE-036). The paragraph on what the analyses deposit (one token per place of a branch: VER-010, VER-001, NU-051) describes those analyses, not the enumeration, and is their subject. The reference firing semantics deposits one token per claim of a branch, the case the analyses model; the non-vacuity theorem shows one such firing.

The paragraph on the timeout outcome says that it is not an output branch (glossary: Timeout outcome), which the `Timeout` line respects by enumerating the child's branches only; the `ForwardInput` line is the branch an action writes, `to` claimed once (glossary: Forward, IO-015), not the timeout outcome's per-consumed-token deposit (IO-014). How the analyses append the timeout outcome after the branches, when it differs place by place from every branch (deposits compared per place, CORE-036), is VER-001's subject.

The block fixes the enumeration function only. That executors and analyses use it (the executor's validation, the SCG virtual transitions, the flattener) is the subject of IO-015, VER-001 and VER-010.

requirements.title: allPlaces Flattening
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] A ↦
  (∀ (p : N), A (Out.place p) = {p}) ∧
    (∀ (s d : N), A (Out.forward s d) = {d}) ∧
      (∀ (l r : Out N), A (l.and r) = A l ∪ A r) ∧
        (∀ (l r : Out N), A (l.xor r) = A l ∪ A r) ∧ ∀ (c : Out N), A c.timeout = A c
reading: Place(p) gives exactly the set {p};
ForwardInput(from, to) gives exactly the set {to};
And(l, r) gives exactly the union of the sets of l and r;
Xor(l, r) gives exactly the union of the sets of l and r;
Timeout(c) gives exactly the set of c.
quotes: The `allPlaces` set of a `Place` node *shall* be the set holding only that place.
The `allPlaces` set of a `ForwardInput(from, to)` node *shall* be the set holding only `to`.
The `allPlaces` set of an `And` node *shall* be the union of its children's `allPlaces` sets.
The `allPlaces` set of an `Xor` node *shall* be the union of its children's `allPlaces` sets.
The `allPlaces` set of a `Timeout` node *shall* be its child's `allPlaces` set.
assumes: A place-set function is a function from an output spec alone to a finite set of places (`Finset`), so it is static by its type and has no order and no repetition: the text and every runtime return a set (Rust `HashSet<PlaceRef>`, Java `Set<Place<?>>`, TypeScript `Set<Place<any>>`). The lines compare sets with equality, so they fix the function exactly (`IO_017_unique`).

The lines say "be" and "holding only": the set equals the places the text names, so it is complete (every place, every `Xor` alternative, every `Timeout` child) and exact (nothing else). The markdown's prose ("collect all leaf places") and test derivation ("complete set") state completeness only; the block reads collecting the leaf places as returning them and nothing else, which is what all three runtimes do (Rust `rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs` `collect_places`, Java `Arc.java` `allPlaces`, TypeScript `out.ts` `collectPlaces`). The containment reading is strictly weaker (`IO_017_mutant_superset_killed`), and a `Place` leaf that also names another place is forbidden (`IO_017_forbids_placeExtra`).

The statement is generic in the place type `N` and its equality, so it fixes no place identity: it holds for whatever identity a runtime compares places by. Rust's set compares `PlaceRef` by name and Java's set compares `Place` records by name and token type (MOD-024). TypeScript's `Set` holds place objects by reference, so two distinct place objects with one name are two members there; on a net whose places have distinct names the three agree. The model writes places as names (CORE-002), and the glossary entry Same set of places, like the EARS lines, leaves place equality to the implementation (CORE-002, MOD-024).

An n-ary `And` or `Xor` is read as right-nested binary nodes, as `Reference.Out` writes it and IO-016 does. Union is associative, so the nesting does not change the set. An `And` with one child (the runtimes allow it; an `Xor` needs two) is that child, which the n-ary union also gives.

The second line strengthens AC2 (`ForwardInput(from, to)` contributes `to`), which does not say that `from` is left out: it reads AC2 as contributing `to` and nothing else. It says "only `to`" rather than "not `from`" because `from` and `to` may be one place, and then the set holds it. The reading follows the text: the prose collects the places the spec writes to, `from` is an input place (IO-014), and all three runtimes add only `to` (Rust `rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs` `collect_places`, Java `Arc.java` `allPlaces`, TypeScript `out.ts` `collectPlaces`). The glossary entries Forward ("In an output branch it claims `to`") and Output arc (a place the output spec names) say the same, so a forward makes `to`, not `from`, an output arc.

The function is defined on every output spec, ones that fail a build-time check included: the `Timeout` and `ForwardInput` lines fix it whether or not the spec has one `Timeout` node and its forwards inside that node's child (IO-013, IO-014), since the build checks and the glossary read it before a spec is known to build.

AC1 (`Xor(And(P1, P2), Timeout(5s, P3))` gives {P1, P2, P3}) follows from lines 1, 3, 4 and 5; the timeout's duration does not matter, since `Reference.Out` carries none and the fifth line reads only the child. AC2 is the second line. The non-vacuity theorem checks both on the reference function, and the test derivation (a nested spec gives the complete set) is AC1.

The relation to IO-016 is derived, not stated: the set is the union of the output branches of the branch enumeration (`IO_017_union_of_branches`, for every pair of functions that satisfy IO-016 and IO-017). So is the relation to the glossary's output arcs (`IO_017_outputArc`).

The block fixes the function only. That the output specification offers it as a method is an API fact of each runtime and is not encoded. That executors and analyses read output places through it (CORE-035, CORE-062, CORE-072, VER-001) is the subject of those requirements.

requirements.title: Name Identity
requirements.statement:
fun I ↦
  (∀ (a b : String), I.eq (I.ofValue a) (I.ofValue b) ↔ a = b) ∧
    (∀ (a b : String),
        I.lt (I.ofValue a) (I.ofValue b) → ¬I.lt (I.ofValue b) (I.ofValue a)) ∧
      (∀ (a b c : String),
          I.lt (I.ofValue a) (I.ofValue b) →
            I.lt (I.ofValue b) (I.ofValue c) → I.lt (I.ofValue a) (I.ofValue c)) ∧
        (∀ (a b : String),
            a ≠ b → I.lt (I.ofValue a) (I.ofValue b) ∨ I.lt (I.ofValue b) (I.ofValue a)) ∧
          ∀ (a b : String),
            (∀ c ∈ a.toList, c.toNat < 65536) →
              (∀ c ∈ b.toList, c.toNat < 65536) →
                (I.lt (I.ofValue a) (I.ofValue b) ↔ a < b)
requirements.scope: the names, the name equality and the name order of each implementation
reading: For all values a and b, the implementation's name equality holds between the name constructed from a and the name constructed from b exactly when a = b.
For all values a and b, if the name of a precedes the name of b, then the name of b does not precede the name of a (so no name precedes itself).
For all values a, b and c, if the name of a precedes the name of b and the name of b precedes the name of c, then the name of a precedes the name of c.
For all different values a and b, the name of a precedes the name of b or the name of b precedes the name of a.
For all values a and b whose characters all lie below U+10000, the name of a precedes the name of b exactly when a precedes b in the lexicographic order of code points.
quotes: The name constructor *shall* return equal names for equal underlying values and different names for different underlying values.

Each implementation *shall* order names by one fixed strict total order, the name order: if one name precedes another, the other does not precede it; if a first name precedes a second and the second precedes a third, the first precedes the third; and of two different names, one precedes the other.

Of two names whose underlying values hold only Basic Multilingual Plane characters, one *shall* precede the other exactly when its value precedes the other's in the lexicographic order of code points.
assumes: The model is one implementation's NameImpl: the carrier of names, the constructor from the underlying value, the name equality and the name order. A name is what the constructor returns; names minted by the executor (NU-010, NU-011) are constructed from their rendered string, so they are names in this sense. The underlying values are strings of Unicode scalar values (Lean's String), which covers every value Rust and Python accept; Java's rejection of a null value and JavaScript or Java strings holding an unpaired surrogate are outside the model.

The constructor is a function of the value, so two constructions of one value give one term of the carrier; the name equality is a field, so an implementation whose names compare by object identity, where two constructions of one value are not equal, is a model and breaks the first line (NU_001_mutant_identityEq). Rust derives PartialEq on the string, Java's NameId is a record and TypeScript's NameId is a branded string compared by value: each is the reference equality.

The fourth line ranges over different underlying values. By the first line these are exactly the pairs of different names, so it is the quote's 'of two different names'; stating it over values keeps it independent of the first line.

'Stable' and 'consistent across a single implementation' (AC2) are read as: the name order is one fixed relation of the implementation, a field of NameImpl, so it cannot differ between two comparisons. Whether it is the same relation in two processes of one implementation is not modelled; every runtime fixes it in code (Rust's derived Ord, Java's String.compareTo, TypeScript's string comparison).

Ruling D31 (a): outside the BMP the order is a parameter. The reference is code-point order (refNameImpl, the order of Rust and of Python, which runs on the Rust runtime); the UTF-16 code-unit order of Java and TypeScript satisfies the block too, agrees with code-point order on BMP names (NU_001_utf16_bmp_agree) and disagrees with it on U+FFFF against U+10000 (NU_001_allows_utf16). The fifth line is what NU-020's 'all languages fire identically' and its note 'byte-identical across implementations for BMP names' rest on for the name half of the tie-break; it rejects a reversed comparator (NU_001_mutant_reversed) and a shortlex order (NU_001_forbids_shortlex). That the oldest-token half of the tie-break agrees across languages is NU-020's and NU-022's, not a line here.

Ruling D96 (a): the sentence 'Whether a matched transition is enabled, and which tokens its firing consumes, shall depend on the names its keys project only through name equality and, for the tie-break of [NU-020], the name order.' is a behaviour line over the ν firing model and is stated in wave W9 together with NU-021, not in this block. It needs two clauses there: (i) under every injective renaming of projected names, whether a matched transition is enabled is unchanged and the names the tie-break chooses among are renamed, with the consumed tokens following the chosen name, so the order cannot decide enabledness or consumption outside the tie-break (a rule 'enabled only if the matched name is the least name in the marking' breaks it); (ii) a firing commutes with every injective renaming that also preserves the name order. Equivariance under order-preserving renamings alone is weaker than the sentence and does not discharge it. The sentences 'A name (NameId) is an opaque correlation identity, constructed from an underlying string value.' and 'The name order exists solely for that tie-break and carries no domain meaning.' are this line's design text and are traced by it. The verifier's name symmetry (Novel.RouteB.joinEnab_inv, joinStep_sym, mintStep_sym, CanonicalKey.canonicalKey_comp) is cited there.

'Identity is a projection of the token payload, not a field on the token' and 'the token model is unchanged' are design text: a match key reads the token value (NU-020), and no model in this development adds a name field to a token. AC3 (adding ν-matching does not change the token type or the on-the-wire shape of token-bearing events) and the test derivation's third check are API and wire shape (kind Q). No test in any language yet runs a net with and without the ν-net APIs and compares its token events, so AC3 has no traced Q evidence; it is recorded here as open, to be closed by a kind Q test beside the EVT-011 and EVT-012 tests.

AC1 (two names constructed from the same underlying value are equal; from different values, unequal) is the first line. AC2 (a stable total order on names, consistent across a single implementation) is the second, third and fourth lines: a strict total order on names, with stability read as above.

The test derivation's first two checks (NameId("a") constructed twice is equal; NameId("a") precedes NameId("b")) follow from the statement for every implementation (NU_001_testDerivation) and are NU_001_nonvacuous on the reference. At runtime the Rust unit tests equality_by_value and total_order_is_lexicographic in rust/libpetri-core/src/name.rs run them.
Implementations also hash names (Rust's derived Hash, Java's record hashCode, a JavaScript Map key); a hash consistent with the name equality adds no observation, and is not modelled.

requirements.title: EXTENDED Coloured-Consumer Fragment
requirements.statement:
fun C ↦
  (∀ (col : PlaceId → Bool) (declared : Bool) (tw : List (PlaceId × Novel.RouteB.TW))
      (T : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans),
      T.keys = none →
        ColouredInputs col T ≠ [] → C col Novel.RouteB.Mode.base declared tw T = none) ∧
    (∀ (col : PlaceId → Bool) (declared : Bool) (tw : List (PlaceId × Novel.RouteB.TW))
        (T : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans) (r : Novel.RouteB.Role),
        T.keys = none →
          ColouredInputs col T ≠ [] →
            C col Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended declared tw T = some r →
              SingleColouredWrites col T ∧
                ∃ s,
                  ColouredInputs col T = [s] ∧
                    UnitCount s ∧
                      r = Novel.RouteB.Role.consume s.place ∧
                        ForwardsOnly col tw s.place) ∧
      (∀ (col : PlaceId → Bool) (declared : Bool) (tw : List (PlaceId × Novel.RouteB.TW))
          (T : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans) (s : InSpec),
          T.keys = none →
            ¬ColouredTestArc col T →
              SingleColouredWrites col T →
                ColouredInputs col T = [s] →
                  UnitCount s →
                    ForwardsOnly col tw s.place →
                      C col Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended declared tw T =
                        some (Novel.RouteB.Role.consume s.place)) ∧
        (∀ (col : PlaceId → Bool) (mode : Novel.RouteB.Mode) (declared : Bool)
            (tw : List (PlaceId × Novel.RouteB.TW)) (T : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans),
            ColouredTestArc col T → C col mode declared tw T = none) ∧
          (∀ (col : PlaceId → Bool) (mode : Novel.RouteB.Mode) (declared : Bool)
              (tw : List (PlaceId × Novel.RouteB.TW)) (T : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans)
              (ks : List PlaceId),
              T.keys = some ks →
                (∃ s ∈ ColouredInputs col T, s.place ∉ ks) →
                  C col mode declared tw T = none) ∧
            ∀ (col : PlaceId → Bool) (mode : Novel.RouteB.Mode) (declared : Bool)
              (tw : List (PlaceId × Novel.RouteB.TW)) (T : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans)
              (p : PlaceId),
              C col mode declared tw T = some (Novel.RouteB.Role.consume p) →
                mode = Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended ∧
                  T.keys = none ∧ ColouredInputs col T ≠ []
requirements.scope: the fragment classifier of every ν verifier
reading: For every coloured set col, mint declaration, list of timeout writes tw and transition T:
under BASE, a transition with no match spec and a coloured input gets no role;

under EXTENDED, if a transition with no match spec and a coloured input gets a role, its branches deposit one token into each coloured place they write and drain none into one, its coloured inputs are a single input s, at count One or Exactly(1), the role is the coloured-consumer role of s's place, and every timeout write into a coloured place forwards s's place;

under EXTENDED, a transition with no match spec, no reset, read or inhibitor arc on a coloured place, whose branches deposit one token into each coloured place they write and drain none into one, whose coloured inputs are a single input s at count One or Exactly(1), and whose every timeout write into a coloured place forwards s's place, gets the coloured-consumer role of s's place;
in either mode, a transition with a reset, read or inhibitor arc on a coloured place gets no role;
in either mode, a transition with match keys ks that consumes a coloured place through an input whose place is not in ks gets no role;
in either mode, a transition that gets the coloured-consumer role of a place is classified under EXTENDED, has no match spec and has a coloured input.
quotes: *While* the fragment mode is BASE, the fragment classifier *shall* give no role to a transition without a match spec that consumes a coloured place.

*While* the fragment mode is EXTENDED, the fragment classifier *shall* give a transition without a match spec that consumes a coloured place no role other than the coloured-consumer role of its one coloured input, and that role only when it consumes exactly one coloured input, at count one, and puts on each branch exactly one token, and never a drained batch, into each coloured place the branch writes.

*If* a transition without a match spec consumes a coloured place and its timeout writes a coloured place other than by forwarding that consumed input, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give it no role.

*While* the fragment mode is EXTENDED, *if* a transition without a match spec consumes exactly one coloured input, at count one, has no reset, read or inhibitor arc on a coloured place, puts on each branch exactly one token, and never a drained batch, into each coloured place the branch writes, and on timeout writes a coloured place only by forwarding that input, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give it the coloured-consumer role of that input's place, whether or not it is declared a mint.
*If* a coloured place carries a reset, read or inhibitor arc of a transition, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give that transition no role, in both BASE and EXTENDED.
*If* a matched transition consumes a coloured place through an input that is not one of its match keys, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give it no role, in both BASE and EXTENDED.

The fragment classifier *shall* give the coloured-consumer role to no other transition: to none while the fragment mode is BASE, to no matched transition and to no transition that consumes no coloured place.
assumes: The classifier is per transition, as the glossary term Fragment classifier reads it: no role for one transition means the net falls back to the sound over-approximation ([NU-050]); the Rust `classify` (rust/libpetri-verification/src/name_fragment.rs) returns no fragment for the net as soon as one transition is refused. The coloured set is an argument. How a verifier builds it (the match keys, and under EXTENDED the declared carriers and the relay targets of [NU-054]) is the verifier pipeline's subject (W10), not a line here. So every line speaks of the places coloured in the mode at hand: a place coloured only by a declared carrier or a relay target is not coloured under BASE, where the coloured set is the match keys alone.

The first paragraph of the section is not a line. Its sentence 'Both are decided solely by the solver-free Route B quotient' conflicts with [NU-053], which lets Route A decide the EXTENDED fragment, and with AC7 and AC8, which speak of both routes (clash nu-c#1, ruling D20 open). The two-value knob, BASE as the default and its builder option names are configuration (kind N); the key format is [VER-012]'s subject.

Line 1 is the first quoted sentence. It is the BASE half of AC1 for a fixture whose consumed place is coloured under BASE, that is a match key of the net (the coloured place a mint feeds): a consumer of a place coloured only by an EXTENDED carrier or relay target consumes no coloured place under BASE, gets an ordinary role there, and the net is not refused on its account. Whether a given fixture's place is coloured in each mode is the coloured-set computation (W10). Line 2 is the second quoted sentence (the prose: 'The analyzer' takes such a transition 'only as a drain/relay role and only when it consumes exactly one coloured input at count exactly one'; 'A consumer that consumes more than one coloured place, or consumes at any count other than one (`Exactly(n≥2)`, `AtLeast`, `All`), is rejected') and AC2, and its last conjunct is the third quoted sentence and the Route B half of AC8: a timeout write into a coloured place that is a unit token or a forward of another input leaves the transition with no role. Its first conjunct (SingleColouredWrites: every branch puts exactly one token into each coloured place it writes, and no drained batch, a forward from an `All` or `AtLeast` input whose count is read off the marking ([IO-014]), into one) is the clause 'puts on each branch exactly one token, and never a drained batch' of the second quoted sentence. The markdown gives it only as the reason for refusing higher input counts ('the base marking adds exactly one token per output place, so re-emitting a higher input cardinality into the name layer would over-count'); the shipped classifier refuses on it (`classifyT`, the branch check), and so does the line.

Line 3 is the fourth quoted sentence and the EXTENDED half of AC1: the role is given, not only allowed (the markdown's 'MAY consume' is a permission to the net author; the classifier that the author relies on then has to give the role). Its premises are the sentence's conditions one for one: one coloured input at count one, no test arc on a coloured place (line 4), one token and no drained batch per coloured place a branch writes (SingleColouredWrites, as in line 2), and only forwards of that input on timeout (ForwardsOnly, as in line 2). A transition that builds has SingleColouredWrites whenever its coloured timeout writes forward its one coloured input: an output branch names a place at most once ([IO-011]), and that input is consumed at count one, so its forward deposits one token. The model takes the branches and the timeout writes as two separate arguments, so the line states the premise.

The mint declaration plays no part in lines 1 to 3 and 6, which hold for both values of declared; the role sentence says so ('whether or not it is declared a mint'). This agrees with [NU-010], whose mint writes a coloured place without consuming one: a declared transition that consumes a coloured place is a consumer here, and the mint rule (Novel.RouteB.classifyS_mint) is [NU-010]'s verifier line, not this block's.

'Because the consumed count is fixed at one, the role is identified by the input place name alone' is encoded by lines 2 and 3, which fix the role to `consume s.place`: Role.consume carries a place and nothing else.

Line 4 is the fifth quoted sentence and AC3. The prose says the analyzer rejects a net in which 'any coloured place carries' such an arc 'on any transition'; per transition that is line 4, and the net falls back because one of its transitions gets no role. Its reason ('it never turns a `Proven`/`Violated` into an unsound verdict') is [NU-050]'s soundness, not a line.

Line 5 is the sixth quoted sentence and the first half of AC7. 'A non-coloured non-key input (a budget or permit) is unaffected' is not a line: line 5 speaks only of coloured inputs, and NU_051_nonvacuous shows a join with an uncoloured budget input that gets its join role. The second half of AC7 ('a stranding such a net can reach is not reported `Proven`') is a verdict and waits for the verifier pipeline (W10).

Line 6 is the seventh quoted sentence, the converse of lines 1 to 3: the coloured-consumer role exists only under EXTENDED ('BASE reproduces the shipped mint → matched-join fragment exactly'), only for 'a transition with **no** match spec' (a matched transition takes a name by its match test, [NU-020], not by the consumer step), and only for a transition that consumes a coloured place (the relay step removes the name 'from its coloured input'). With line 2 it pins down every transition the role is given to.

The relay and drain semantics ('A coloured consumer relays the consumed name-symbol into each coloured output of the fired branch ... or drains it ... on a branch that produces no coloured output') is the block NU_051_relay. AC6 (MAY: one `Xor` consumer relays on one branch and drains on another) is permitted by lines 2 and 3, which do not depend on the branches: the fixture of NU_051_nonvacuous is such a consumer, and NU_051_relay_nonvacuous relays on one branch and drains on the other.

The relay/drain action precondition is an assumption on the net author (kind A), not a line: the action threads the consumed name into its coloured outputs, or into none, and never mints a fresh name while consuming a coloured token. No analysis can check it. It enters Route B as the consumer contract of the name step (`Novel.RouteB.Contract`, under which `name_step_simulates_exec` holds), the premise of [NU-050]'s soundness (W9). 'MUST be documented as such' is a documentation duty (kind Q). 'the report of a verdict names the consumers whose action writes it assumes' is a report line of the verifier pipeline (W10).

The carrier bullet is not a line yet. Where a declared carrier that is not a place of the net must fail is ruling D95 (clash nu-c#2: AC4 has no mode, the body ignores carriers under BASE, and Java and TypeScript reject at the builder while Rust refuses only on some Route B paths), so AC4 waits for it and for the verifier pipeline (W10). That the carriers join the coloured set before roles are given, and are ignored under BASE, is the coloured-set computation of the pipeline (W10).
The diagnosability bullet (an 'EXTENDED declined' note) is a report line (kind N) of the verifier pipeline (W10); whether every refusal must carry it is clash nu-c#10 (ruling D20 open).
AC5 (SHOULD: an end-to-end quiescence verdict on a carrier fixture, attributable to Route B) is a verdict and report line of the verifier pipeline (W10) and depends on the carrier line (D95).

AC8's executor half (with the minting forks m1, m2, the consumers r1, r2 and a join on KA and KB, the executor reaches done and `placeBound(done, 0)` is not `Proven`) is a verdict line (W10, with the reference ν firing of W9). Its Route A half is Novel.RouteA.shipped_consume, cited by NU_051_routeA_consume, and is not a line: the timeout sentence speaks of the fragment classifier, which is Route B's, and no Route A classifier is abstracted here, because whether Route A decides the EXTENDED fragment at all is clash nu-c#1 (ruling D20 open). Its last sentence ('A consumer whose timeout forwards its coloured input is still a relay') is line 3 with a forward of the consumed input, shown in NU_051_nonvacuous.
AC2's 'no false `Proven` from an over-counted name layer, no dropped base-enabled firing' is the soundness the refusal buys ([NU-050], W9); the block states the refusal.
Whether a transition is a mint (declared, and writing no coloured place on timeout) is [NU-010]'s verifier line (Novel.RouteB.classifyS_mint), not this block's.

requirements.title: EXTENDED Coloured-Consumer Fragment
requirements.statement:
fun S ↦
  ∀ (co : List PlaceId),
    co.Nodup →
      ∀ (inp : PlaceId) (outs : List PlaceId) (s : ℕ) (M : Novel.RouteB.NM co),
        outs.Nodup →
          1 ≤ Novel.RouteB.cnt co M s inp →
            ∀ (u : ℕ) (i : Fin co.length),
              (S co inp outs s M u i + if u = s ∧ co[↑i] = inp then 1 else 0) =
                M u i + if u = s ∧ co[↑i] ∈ outs then 1 else 0
requirements.scope: the name layer of Route B
reading: For every list co of distinct coloured places, consumed input inp, list outs of distinct coloured outputs of the fired branch, consumed name s resident in inp and name marking M, and for every name u and coloured place i: the step's count of u at i, plus one if u is s and i is inp, equals M's count of u at i, plus one if u is s and i is in outs.
quotes: *When* a coloured consumer fires on a branch with a name its coloured input holds, the name layer *shall* remove one token of that name from the input, add one token of that name to each coloured output of the branch and change no other count, so a branch with no coloured output drains the name.
assumes: The step is the name layer of Route B (`Novel.RouteB.NM`: the tokens of each name in each coloured place); which transition gets the coloured-consumer role is the block NU_051. The step is applied to a name resident in the consumed input (Route B's `will_fire` for a consumer), hence the premise that s has a token in inp, which the sentence states as 'with a name its coloured input holds'. Which resident name a consumer takes (any, on Route B; the oldest, FIFO, in the executor) is not this line's: it is the action contract and [NU-050]'s soundness; the outputs are the coloured places of the fired branch, without repetition (`colOut`), hence the premises on co and outs.

The line is the quoted sentence, which restates 'A coloured consumer relays the consumed name-symbol into each coloured output of the fired branch (threading the same name), or drains it (dead-letters the name) on a branch that produces no coloured output'. A relay back into the consumed input leaves its count as it was, which the equation allows. That the name the action writes is the consumed one is the action contract (kind A, see NU_051): this line says what the name layer does, the contract is why that matches the executor ([NU-050], W9).

AC6 (one `Xor` consumer relays on one branch and drains on another) is this line with outs the coloured outputs of each branch; NU_051_relay_nonvacuous applies it to one branch with a coloured output and one with none. The other acceptance criteria are the block NU_051's subject, which accounts for each.

requirements.title: Conflict-Only Priority for the Route B Name-SCG
requirements.statement:
fun {β} E C ↦
  (∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β) (κ : β → AMarking)
      (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans) (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role)
      (c : ℕ) (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),
      (∀ (b : β), base.compete b = C (κ b)) →
        (List.map (fun T ↦ T.base.name) net).Nodup →
          E co base net role true c S =
            List.filter
              (fun x ↦
                !decide
                    (∃ L ∈ net, L.base.name = x.1 ∧ ∃ H ∈ net, PreEmpts base role S H L))
              (E co base net role false c S)) ∧
    (∀ (a : AMarking) (H L : Transition),
        (∀ s ∈ H.inputs ++ L.inputs,
            (∃ sh ∈ H.inputs, sh.place = s.place) →
              (∃ sl ∈ L.inputs, sl.place = s.place) → fixedCard s.card = true) →
          (C a H L = true ↔
            ∃ sh ∈ H.inputs,
              (∃ sl ∈ L.inputs, sl.place = sh.place) ∧
                a sh.place <
                  Novel.RouteB.demandOn H sh.place + Novel.RouteB.demandOn L sh.place)) ∧
      (∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β)
          (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans)
          (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role) (c : ℕ)
          (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),
          List.Pairwise (fun T U ↦ T.base.name < U.base.name) net →
            E co base net role false c S =
              List.flatMap (fun T ↦ E co base [T] role false c S)
                (List.filter (fun T ↦ base.enabled S.b T.base) net)) ∧
        (∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base base' : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β)
            (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans)
            (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role) (c : ℕ)
            (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),
            base'.enabled = base.enabled →
              base'.fire = base.fire →
                E co base' net role false c S = E co base net role false c S) ∧
          ∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β)
            (T : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans) (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role)
            (c : ℕ) (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β) (d : Novel.RouteB.Row),
            base.enabled S.b T.base = true →
              d ∈ T.rows →
                (base.fire S.b T.base d).isSome = true →
                  Novel.RouteB.willFire co (role T) S.m S.bound = true →
                    ∃ x ∈ E co base [T] role false c S, x.1 = T.base.name
requirements.scope: the Route B successor step, under CONFLICT and NONE
reading: Let E be the Route B expansion and C the competition test.

For every net whose transition names are distinct, every base layer whose competition is C read on the count marking κ of the class, and every class: the CONFLICT successors of the class are its NONE successors, in order, without those labelled with the name of a transition L of the net that some transition H of the net pre-empts in the class (glossary: Pre-empt, read as PreEmpts over the base layer's enabled, readyLe, idle and compete and the will-fire test of H's role).

For every count marking a and transitions H and L whose input arcs on the places both consume from have cardinality One or Exactly: C a H L holds exactly when some input arc of H is on a place that is also the place of an input arc of L and holds fewer tokens in a than the sum of the tokens H and L consume from it on one firing.

For every base layer, every class and every net whose transitions are listed in the code-point order of their names: the NONE successors of the class are, in that order, the NONE successors each base-enabled transition T has when the step is given T alone (the net [T]), from the same class and the same base layer.
For every two base layers that agree on enablement and firing: the NONE successors of every class are the same under both.

For every base layer, class and transition T that is base-enabled, has a branch the base layer fires in the class, and whose role will fire on the class's name layer (willFire): the NONE successors of the class in the net [T] include one labelled with T's name.
quotes: *While* the mode is `CONFLICT`, the Route B graph *shall* leave a base-enabled transition `L` unexpanded from a class exactly when another transition `H` of the net pre-empts `L` in that class, and *shall* expand every other base-enabled transition of the class as under `NONE`, in the same order.

*While* the mode is `CONFLICT`, the Route B graph *shall* take two transitions `H` and `L` whose input arcs on the places both consume from have cardinality `One` or `Exactly` to compete in a class exactly when some place is a consumed input of both and its token count in the class marking is less than the sum of the tokens each of them consumes from it on one firing.

*While* the mode is `NONE`, the Route B graph *shall* expand each base-enabled transition of a class, in the class's clock order (the code-point order of the transitions' names, [VER-010] AC1), with the successors the transition has when it is expanded alone from the same class and the same base layer, *shall* expand no other transition, and *shall not* read the readiness, in-flight state or competition of any transition.

*While* the mode is `NONE`, the Route B graph *shall* give a base-enabled transition at least one successor labelled with its name when the base layer can fire one of its branches in the class and the transition will fire on the name layer (always for an ordinary or minting transition, with an enabling name for a join, with a resident name for a consumer).
assumes: The model is the pair (E, C). E is one expansion of a class of the name-aware state-class graph of Route B ([VER-012]): the coloured set, the base layer (Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer: enabled, fire, readyLe, compete and idle), the net with its roles, the mode (true for CONFLICT, false for NONE), the mint counter and the class give the labelled successors, each labelled with the name of the transition that fired. The witness is refExpand, the shipped step Novel.RouteB.succ (name_state_class_graph.rs build_until). C is the competition test on a class's count marking; the witness is refCompete, Novel.RouteB.sharesConsumed (shares_consumed_input). The step reads competition through the base layer (as in Graph.lean), so line 1 is stated for the base layers whose compete is C read on the class's count marking κ; that is what makes C the graph's competition and not a separate function. The untimed base is such a layer, with κ the identity (nu052_untimedBase_compete). The timed base, whose count marking is the marking of the timed class, comes with wave W10; a base layer whose compete is not of this form is a wrong base layer, not a wrong graph, and is not this requirement's subject. The pruning predicate itself is the glossary term Pre-empt; its shipped form is refPrune (GlossaryNuVer, refPrune_iff).

The first quoted sentence is line 1. 'Exactly when' restates the body's 'is not expanded from a class when' together with the soundness paragraph's 'The pruning removes only interleavings in which a lower-priority transition fires ahead of a ready, conflicting, strictly-higher-priority one': under CONFLICT the graph prunes and does nothing else. 'Another transition' is read as another name: the line is stated for nets whose transition names are distinct, because the shipped step labels successors with names and compares H and L by name (name_state_class_graph.rs:587, `h.name() != l.name()`). Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10, with D23 settling that distinct names are one shared assumption for every name-keyed requirement), so the premise is that assumption and the quoted sentence needs no narrowing. Outside it, on a net where two transitions share a name, the Rust prune never lets one pre-empt the other, while the Java and TypeScript prunes compare by identity (NameStateClassGraph.java:402, name-state-class-graph.ts:336) and do; D10 puts that net out of scope, so the case is not encoded.

Line 1 reads every bullet of the body through the glossary term Pre-empt: strictly higher priority, competition (the base layer's compete, line 2 on count markings), ready no later than L (the base layer's readyLe), no firing in flight (the base layer's idle) and 'actually fires in this class' (willFire of H's role: a join needs an enabling name, a consumer a resident one, so a name-disabled join pre-empts nothing). H ranges over the base-enabled transitions of the class, as the body's 'another enabled transition H in the same class'. 'Actually fires in this class' is read on the name layer, as the body's own gloss ('a name-disabled join, whose inputs carry no shared name, produces no name-successor') and the shipped prune (dominated reads will_fire and no firing of the base) do; whether H has a branch the base layer can fire is not part of it. On the untimed base every enabled transition fires. On a timed base, H ready no later than L (readyLe) makes H firable whenever L is, and when L is not firable pruning it removes no successor; that this holds of the timed readyLe is the timed base's subject (wave W10).

The second quoted sentence is line 2, stated for transitions whose input arcs on the places both consume from have cardinality One or Exactly (fixedCard). An All or AtLeast arc on a place only one of them consumes from plays no part in the demand on a shared place, so the premise leaves it free and line 2 still constrains such a pair (NU_052_forbids_wholePair). The body defines a demand as 'the tokens that transition consumes from p on one firing'; the runtimes and the Lean model use the required count (consumed_demand, Card.required), which is 1 for All and n for AtLeast(n), not the tokens consumed. For One and Exactly the two agree, so line 2 uses demandOn under that premise. Which reading holds for All and AtLeast on a shared place is ruling D97 (clash nu-c#3), and the widened line waits for it (wave W10); until then the quoted sentence names One and Exactly. 'Read and inhibitor arcs do not count' is line 2's 'consumed input of both': only input arcs occur in it.

The body's 'becomes ready no later than L by the class-relative residual earliest: the DBM lower bound of each enabled clock captured before time is let to pass (readyEarliest, parallel to the enabled set)', the comparison within a float epsilon, and the sentence '*While* the mode is `CONFLICT`, the Route B graph *shall* take `H` to be ready no later than `L` in a class exactly when `readyEarliest[H] <= readyEarliest[L]` within a float epsilon, where `readyEarliest` is the DBM lower bound of each enabled clock before time is let to pass.' are a timing line over a timed base layer, as are the body's claims that a static H.earliest() <= L.earliest() does not suffice, that the rule subsumes the immediate-H case and that it also prunes sound non-zero-earliest conflicts. The base layer here is abstract (readyLe); its timed instance needs the timed class of RefScg (VER-010), so this sentence is not encoded here and comes with wave W10. On the untimed base every transition is ready at once (untimedBase.readyLe is true).

The third quoted sentence is lines 3 and 4. It restates 'The default mode, NONE, MUST reproduce the prior Route B behaviour byte-for-byte' with the first paragraph's 'it expands every base-enabled transition': line 3 says no transition's NONE successors depend on another transition, that they come in the class's clock order and that a transition not base-enabled adds none, so NONE prunes nothing by priority; line 4 says NONE reads none of the base layer's readyLe, idle and compete, the inputs only the prune reads.

'In the class's clock order': the runtimes walk a class's enabled transitions in the class's canonical clock order, ascending transition name in code-point order ([VER-010] AC1; the Rust, Java and TypeScript name-state-class graphs walk the base class's enabled list, which the state-class graph permutes into canonical order when it builds a class). The model's step walks the net list it is given, so line 3 is stated for a net listed in that order (the Pairwise premise), and the model's list order is then the runtimes' order on every class. A net listed in another order is the same net handed to the step in another enumeration; line 1's 'in the same order' compares CONFLICT with NONE on one enumeration and needs no premise.

'Expanded alone from the same class and the same base layer' is the net [T] with the class and the base layer unchanged.
