The base layer is the class's own: the base successor of T is computed over the whole net (its clocks, enabled set and readyEarliest, state_class_graph.rs compute_successor_gated), and in the model that whole-net computation is inside base.fire, which line 3 does not vary, so [T] is not the net holding T alone. The minted symbols are compared up to the canonical key of the class ([VER-012] AC2): the runtimes thread one mint counter across the expansions of a class and across classes (name_state_class_graph.rs next_sym), while line 3 passes the same counter c to every transition, so the raw symbol numbers of the runtimes agree with the model only after interning.

The fourth quoted sentence is line 5. It is the least that 'expands' says of one transition: a transition that fires on both layers yields a successor labelled with its name, so an expansion that yields nothing is ruled out (NU_052_forbids_empty). The will-fire condition is the body's name-disabled join, which 'produces no name-successor', read the other way. Which successors one transition yields, all of them and byte for byte, is VER-012's subject, cited in wave W10, so 'the prior Route B behaviour' is not stated as a fixed function here.

Which mode the verifier hands the step is outside the step. On a net with a reapable transition Route B does not prune ([VER-002], 'It does not prune by priority ([NU-052]) on a net with a reapable transition.'; nu_scg_verifier.rs:195-200 turns CONFLICT into NONE). NU-052's body states the pruning without that exception; whether NU-052 gains the sentence is ruling D97 (clash nu-c#4). The lines here hold for whatever mode the step is given, so they need neither answer.

The paragraph 'In-flight actions' (the split rule: a verifier MUST split every pruner and every transition depositing into an input or read place of a pruner on a net with a ν-join, MUST NOT let H pre-empt while inflight:<H> is marked, falls back to the NONE verdict naming the transition when one cannot be split, keeps the pruning under assumeAtomicFiring and on a direct call to Route B) is a pipeline obligation over the split net. It needs RefSplit (VER-004) and the pipeline slice of RefVerifier, and its scope (a net with a ν-join) waits for ruling D97; it comes with wave W10. What this block keeps of it is the in-flight guard as the base layer's idle in line 1; that idle is the count of inflight:<H> being 0 is the split model's subject.

The paragraph 'Soundness' (the pruned firings are ones the eager, priority-ordered executor never performs; L is re-examined after H fires) relates the graph to the executor. It needs RefExec with a priority-ordered pass and actions in flight, and it must list EXEC-003 AC4 (a ν-join that received a same-pass deposit fires no earlier than the next cycle). Whether the Java and TypeScript wording of the in-flight case stays is ruling D8. It comes with wave W10; Libpetri.postFixPrune_agrees_with_executor (Priority.lean) is true by construction and is no evidence for it.
The option names prioritySemantics / priority_semantics, that CONFLICT is opt-in and that an implementation MAY omit it are configuration, not encoded.

AC1 (NONE is the default and the only mode an implementation MUST provide; NONE leaves every existing Route B verdict unchanged) is lines 3, 4 and 5 for the step: NONE expands each base-enabled transition on its own, reads nothing the prune reads and gives every transition that fires a successor. The default and the verdicts are configuration and VER-012's graph; not encoded beyond that.

AC2 (the fork-threaded co-mint plus immediate ν-join plus delayed lower-priority drain fixture: Violated under NONE, Proven under CONFLICT on Route B called directly and under assumeAtomicFiring; through verify() with the split on, the NONE verdict and a report note) needs the timed base (a delayed drain), the verdict and the pipeline; it comes with wave W10. Its step-level core, that under CONFLICT the join's competitor is pruned when the join pre-empts it, is line 1 (NU_052_nonvacuous on the untimed base).

AC3 (no over-pruning: a genuine orphan, whose join is name-disabled, still reaches its drain) is line 1's will-fire condition. The Route B retrodiction of commit c23cd9e (Novel.RouteB.WF: a priority-10 join whose keys hold two different names and a priority-0 drain competing for one token) is the evidence: the pre-fix prune without the will-fire guard stalls the class (NU_052_forbids_preFix), and the shipped step keeps the drain's edge (NU_052_orphan_not_pruned). The verdicts Violated without a drain and Proven with one are VER-012's graph and come with wave W10.
AC4 (only consumed-input conflicts prune; a read or inhibitor arc on the shared place creates no conflict) is line 2 (NU_052_forbids_reads, NU_052_nonvacuous).

AC5 (a delayed(100) ν-join still pre-empts a delayed(200) lower-priority drain, so DEADLETTER is unreachable under CONFLICT and reachable under NONE) is the residual-earliest comparison over a timed base and a verdict; it comes with wave W10. Line 1 keeps the readiness condition (NU_052_forbids_noReady).

AC6 (when the shared consumed place holds enough tokens for both transitions, CONFLICT does not prune the lower-priority one) is line 2 (NU_052_forbids_noCount) and, on the step, NU_052_nonvacuous (two tokens: both expanded).

AC7 (a pruner in flight pre-empts nothing: H with an asynchronous action, L, the refill g, Unreachable(bad) Violated under CONFLICT with L in the trace) needs the split net (inflight:<H>) and the verdict; it comes with wave W10. Line 1 keeps the in-flight condition as the base layer's idle (NU_052_forbids_noIdle); the count-level witness is Libpetri.inFlight_guard_is_necessary (Priority.lean).
The test derivation (the ν-join versus timed dead-letter drain fixture, the genuine orphan, every verdict attributed to Route B) is AC2 and AC3 and comes with wave W10.

requirements.title: EXTENDED-Coloured Quiescence in the Route A SMT Encoder
requirements.statement:
fun B K U V ↦
  (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : List PlaceId) (rows : List (Transition × Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit))
      (a0 : AMarking) (k : ℕ),
      B n C rows a0 = some k →
        Novel.RouteA.ScaledCover n C rows a0 k ∧
          ∀ j < k, ¬Novel.RouteA.ScaledCover n C rows a0 j) ∧
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : List PlaceId)
        (rows : List (Transition × Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit)) (a0 : AMarking) (k : ℕ),
        Nu053Fits n rows a0 →
          Novel.RouteA.ScaledCover n C rows a0 k →
            k ≤ Novel.RouteA.slotCap → ∃ j, B n C rows a0 = some j) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : List PlaceId)
          (rows : List (Transition × Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit)) (a0 : AMarking)
          (k : ℕ), B n C rows a0 = some k → ∃ D y, K n C rows a0 D y = some k) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : List PlaceId)
            (rows : List (Transition × Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit)) (a0 : AMarking)
            (D : ℕ) (y : Weight) (k : ℕ),
            K n C rows a0 D y = some k ↔
              0 < D ∧
                (∀ p < n, 0 ≤ y p) ∧
                  (∀ p ∈ C, ↑D ≤ y p) ∧
                    (∀ tr ∈ rows, Novel.LinearBound.dotIncD y tr n ≤ 0) ∧
                      k = (dot y a0 n).toNat / D ∧ k ≤ Novel.RouteA.slotCap) ∧
          (∀ (inp : PlaceId) (outs : List PlaceId) (k : ℕ) (s s' : PlaceId → ℕ → ℕ),
              U inp outs k s s' ↔
                ∃ c < k,
                  1 ≤ s inp c ∧
                    ∀ (p : PlaceId) (c' : ℕ),
                      s' p c' =
                        if c' = c then
                          if p = inp ∧ p ∉ outs then s p c' - 1
                          else if p ∈ outs ∧ p ≠ inp then s p c' + 1 else s p c'
                        else s p c') ∧
            ∀ (E : Novel.RouteA.Enc) (R : List String) (Q : AMarking → Prop)
              (e : Novel.RouteA.EState),
              V E R Q e ↔
                (∀ r ∈ E.rows,
                    Novel.RouteA.reapT R r.t = false →
                      Novel.RouteA.uDisabled E.C e r.t ∨
                        Novel.RouteA.colDisabled E.C E.k r.cls e.s) ∧
                  Q (Novel.RouteA.agg E.C E.k e)
requirements.scope: the colour-slot bound, its exact re-check and the coloured consumer and quiescence terms of the Route A coloured encoding, where offered
reading: For every colour-slot bound B, re-check K, consumer rule U and violation term V:

for every place count n, coloured places C, flat rows and initial marking a0: if B answers k, there is a scaled cover at k (some D > 0 and Y with Y ≥ 0 below n, Y ≥ D on every place of C, Y not increasing along any row and Y·a0 < D·(k + 1)), and there is none at any j < k;

if the flat net meets Nu053Fits (at most 4096 places and 16384 rows, C(n+m, n)·(2n+1)·(n+m+1) ≤ 4000000 and (n+1)!·E^(n+1) ≤ 2^63 − 1 with E = nu053Entry) and there is a scaled cover at some k ≤ slotCap, then B answers some bound;
if B answers k, K accepts some scaled weighting (D, Y) with the bound k;
K accepts (D, Y) with the bound k exactly when D > 0, Y ≥ 0 below n, Y ≥ D on every place of C, Y·C_r ≤ 0 on every row r, k = ⌊Y·a0 / D⌋ and k ≤ slotCap;

U relates the colour columns s and s' of the consumer with input inp, outputs outs and k slots exactly when some colour c < k has s(inp, c) ≥ 1 and s' is s with, on colour c, one less at inp when inp is not an output, one more at an output that is not inp, and every other place unchanged, and every column of another colour unchanged;

V marks an encoding state e of the encoding E with the reapable names R and the clause Q exactly when every row whose transition is not named in R is disabled at e for an uncoloured reason (uDisabled) or for every colour below k (colDisabled, which is False for a row of class untouched), and Q holds of the all-colour counts of e.
quotes: *If* the verifier sets the colour-slot bound to `k`, *then* some covering weighting `y` *shall* have `⌊y·M0⌋ = k`, and no covering weighting *shall* have `⌊y·M0⌋ < k`, a covering weighting being one with `y ≥ 0`, `y_p ≥ 1` on every coloured place and `y·C_t ≤ 0` on every flat transition.

*When* the verifier solves the colour-slot program of a flat net with `n` places and `m` transitions that has a covering weighting `y` with `⌊y·M0⌋ ≤ 2^31 − 1`, and `n ≤ 4096`, `m ≤ 16384`, `C(n+m, n)·(2n+1)·(n+m+1) ≤ 4000000` and `(n+1)!·E^(n+1) ≤ 2^63 − 1`, where `E` is the largest of 1, every initial count and `n` times every `pre + post` of a flat transition at a place, it *shall* set a colour-slot bound unless the solve is stopped ([VER-013]).
*If* the verifier sets the colour-slot bound to `k`, *then* the exact re-check *shall* have accepted a weighting and given it the bound `k`.

The exact re-check *shall* accept a weighting `y` exactly when `y ≥ 0`, `y_p ≥ 1` on every coloured place, `y·C_t ≤ 0` on every flat transition and `⌊y·M0⌋ ≤ 2^31 − 1`, and *shall* give an accepted weighting the bound `⌊y·M0⌋`.

*When* the coloured encoding emits the rule of a coloured consumer for a colour `c` below `k`, the rule *shall* be enabled only when colour `c` of the input holds a token, and *shall* subtract one from colour `c` of the input, add one to colour `c` of each coloured output, and leave unchanged colour `c` of a place that is both the input and an output and every other colour column.

*When* the coloured encoding decides a quiescence property, it *shall* treat an encoding state as violating exactly when every flat row (each XOR branch is its own row) whose transition is not reapable ([VER-002]) is disabled in the state for an uncoloured reason or, when the row touches a coloured place, for every colour below `k`, and the property's own clause holds of the state's all-colour token counts.
assumes: The model is the tuple (B, K, U, V). B is a function of the flat net as the shipped build_plan sees it: the place count, the coloured places (sorted, duplicate-free flat indices below the place count), the flat rows (Transition × Deposit, Novel.ForwardDeposit) and the initial count marking. A weighting is handled scaled to integers, a vector Y and a denominator D standing for y = Y / D, as check_cover takes it (slot_bound_lp.rs; Novel.RouteA.checkCover); 'y_p ≥ 1' is Y_p ≥ D and '⌊y·M0⌋' is ⌊Y·M0 / D⌋. A covering weighting at k is Novel.RouteA.ScaledCover at k. The column C_t of a flat transition is post − pre with pre the required count and a timeout outcome counting its deposit (dotIncD), and a reset or consume-all place may carry weight (no H1; SlotBound.lean, 'No H1'); the token-sum bound holds anyway (coloured_tokens_le). U is a relation between the colour columns before and after one rule, so it carries the rule's guard as well as its update; V is the violation term on one encoding state.

Line 1 is the first quoted sentence and the body's '`k` is `⌊opt⌋`, where `opt` is the least `y·M0` over all such weightings' (ruling D80 (d)): k is certified by a covering weighting and no smaller bound is. 'The optimum is unique, so every implementation computes the same `k`' is NU_053_unique: two bounds that meet NU-053 agree wherever both answer. 'When no weighting exists (the program is infeasible) ... the plan is refused' is NU_053_infeasible. The simplex itself is not modelled: the witness is the least certified bound by classical choice (refColourSlotBound), not an execution of the solve.

Line 2 is the second quoted sentence, which this migration adds so that a bound that never answers does not conform: on a net that meets Nu053Fits a bound is set whenever a covering weighting is within the cap, and by line 1 it is then the least one (NU_053_answers_least). The sentence after it in the markdown gives the reason the normative solve meets it: Bland's rule never returns to a basis, so it makes fewer than C(n+m, n) pivots of work at most (2n+1)·(n+m+1) each, and a tableau entry in lowest terms is a ratio of two minors of the initial tableau, each at most (n+1)!·E^(n+1) by the Leibniz expansion; the optimal weighting the solve reads off is an exact optimum, which passes the re-check below the cap. Every case of spec/verification-fixtures/slot-bound-lp.json that meets Nu053Fits is optimal or infeasible, and the coefficient-limit and work-limit cases do not meet it. Line 2 kills a bound that never answers (NU_053_forbids_never), one that treats k = 0 as a fallback (NU_053_forbids_zeroFallback), one with a narrower cap (NU_053_forbids_byteCap) and one that answers only integer optima (NU_053_forbids_integerOnly). On a net that does not meet Nu053Fits, whether the solve reaches a limit is the normative solve's, kind Q. A stopped solve ([VER-013]) ends the query with the stop, so B reads a solve that is not stopped.

Lines 3 and 4 are the third and fourth quoted sentences and the body's 'uses its weighting only after an exact re-check in arbitrary-precision arithmetic' with ruling D80 (a) (clash nu-c#6): the re-check also refuses a bound above 2^31 − 1 (slotCap), as every runtime does (slot_bound_lp.rs SLOT_CAP, SlotBoundLp.java, slot-bound-lp.ts). 'A weighting that fails the re-check is discarded and the plan is refused; it never sets `k`' is line 3 for the bound: no k is set without a weighting the re-check accepts with that bound. That the accepted weighting is the one the solve returned (the shipped colourSlotBoundLP binds the solve's answer to checkCover) is not stated, because B does not expose the weighting it read: a refusal of the solve's own weighting while another weighting would pass is the normative solve's and the fixture's (kind Q), and on a net that meets Nu053Fits line 2 already forbids refusing the plan. The re-check's shape guard on the length of Y (one entry per place) has no counterpart, Weight being total; it only refuses more. Each condition of line 4 is load-bearing: a re-check without the cap (NU_053_forbids_noCap), without the coloured condition (NU_053_forbids_noColouredCheck), without non-negativity (NU_053_forbids_noNegCheck), without the row condition (NU_053_forbids_noRowCheck), without D > 0 (NU_053_forbids_noPosDCheck) or with the ceiling for the floor (NU_053_forbids_ceilCheck) is killed.

Line 5 is the fifth quoted sentence and the paragraph on the update of a coloured consumer: the rule for colour c is enabled only with colour c resident in the input (its '>= 1' guard), emits '(- x 1)' for the input column and '(+ x 1)' for each coloured output column, and has no update term for a self-loop column, which keeps its guard and is carried over unchanged, as a join's key that is also a relay target is ([NU-054]). U ranges over the colour columns only: the uncoloured columns of the rule (AC7's tick and tock) are the uncoloured update uFire, not this line. Natural subtraction at a zero column does not arise under the guard. The shipped encoder emits exactly this rule (NU_053_consumer_shipped, Novel.RouteA.colourStep_consume_shipped). The old write order, in which the output's '+ 1' overwrote the input's '− 1' on a self-loop, is killed (NU_053_forbids_oldConsumer) and was a live wrong Proven (Novel.RouteA.self_loop_consume_false_proven); a rule without the guard is killed too (NU_053_forbids_noGuard).

Line 6 is the sixth quoted sentence and the quiescence bullet as reworded by ruling D80 (a) (clash nu-c#5): the quiescence of [VER-002], read colour-aware, for each quiescence property (DeadlockFree, TerminatesAtSink, JoinedOrDeadLettered, QuiescentCount), each conjoining its own clause Q over the all-colour counts (agg). Q is a parameter: NU-053 fixes the colour-aware quiescence term and that the clause is read over the all-colour counts, not which clause each property has. The clauses of DeadlockFree, TerminatesAtSink and QuiescentCount are VER-002's lines 1, 2 and 6 without their quiescence conjunct; JoinedOrDeadLettered and its clause, which has no sink clause ([NU-040] AC4), are NU-040's, and the NU-040 block (wave W9) adds the line that ties the coloured violation of each property to its clause. Until then 'so `JoinedOrDeadLettered` carries no sink clause' has no Lean line. A transition is reapable when its name is in R, the set the verifier hands the encoders (VER-002's reap-aware reading; empty under assumeNoReaping). Disabled 'for an uncoloured reason' is uDisabled: an uncoloured input below its demand, a marked inhibitor or an empty read place; 'for every colour' is colDisabled: a mint finds no globally-fresh colour, a join no colour on every key, a consumer no colour on its input. A row that touches no coloured place has no colour reason (colDisabled of class untouched is False), so it is disabled only for an uncoloured reason, also at k = 0. A strict quiescence that ignores R (NU_053_forbids_strict; Novel.RouteA.ReapW.reaping_breaks_routeA_quiescence) and a count-level quiescence that reads the all-colour counts instead of the colours (NU_053_forbids_countLevel) are killed.

The bullet on the EXTENDED fragment ([NU-051]: coloured consumers, relay or drain, and declared carrier places, each consuming exactly one coloured input at count one) is the fragment classifier of NU-051 (refClassify, the NU_051 block). The bullet 'classifies each XOR output branch independently by its own incidence' is build_plan's classification of each flat row (Novel.RouteA.ClassShape, buildPlan in Plan.lean), a pipeline line with the verifier slice of wave W10. 'The encoding has no environment-injection rule, so it does not answer when injection is modelled ([VER-006] AC7)' is the pipeline's decline under injection (wave W10).

The bullet on the structural bound restates line 1 and its soundness: 'every reachable marking has Σ_{coloured} M ≤ y·M ≤ y·M0' is NU_053_tokens_le (Novel.RouteA.coloured_tokens_le), and its dual reading (the largest coloured token count of the state equation M = M0 + C·σ over the reals) is LP duality, not encoded. The examples of the bullet (a budget place that gates minting yields a weighting, a refund to a non-minting place keeps the minting budget covering, a leaky co-mint fan-out yields none) are instances of line 1. 'A relay threads its colour onward and still MUST NOT refund' is not a check of its own: a relay that refunds the minting budget leaves the program infeasible, so by line 1 no plan is built (NU_053_relayRefund, mint: budget → a and relay: a → a2, budget), while a relay that refunds to a place that does not mint keeps the program feasible and the plan built (NU_053_otherRefund, k = 1). '`k = 0` is a bound like any other ... the zero-slot plan is exact rather than a fallback' is NU_053_zero_exact (Novel.RouteA.vacuous_colour_layer_lp) with line 2: a bound of 0 is set, not refused (NU_053_ac6).

The paragraph 'The solve is normative' (the presolve, the tableau, Bland's rule, the weighting read off the slacks, the limits of 4096 places and 16384 rows, the work limit 'it MUST NOT exceed 4000000', the coefficient limit 'MUST have numerator and denominator in lowest terms at most `2^63 − 1` in absolute value' and the order of each round) fixes which nets every implementation refuses and with which pivots. It is kind Q: the shared fixture spec/verification-fixtures/slot-bound-lp.json pins each case's status, pivots, work, presolved sizes, optimum, k and weighting for every implementation (ruling D80 (d)). Line 2 is the one consequence of it stated here. The six report lines, 'colour-slot bound k=<k>' and the stop that prints no line are report text (kind N).

The paragraph on the dispatch (Route B first, deferral to the coloured plan on a Route B Unknown, a verdict of the coloured plan not downgraded, its Proven sound while the declared mints and coloured consumers keep their contracts) and the paragraph on the [VER-015] linear bound running before the coloured query are verdict and pipeline lines. They need the reference ν executor and the verifier pipeline: the soundness line is stated over RefNuReach (design ruling S7 (a)) with wave W9, the dispatch order with wave W10. The current evidence for the soundness is Novel.RouteA.routeA_safety_sound_plan and routeA_quiescence_sound_reaping, relative to the Route A ν step (RouteA.NuStep).

AC1 (a budget-bounded EXTENDED ν-net whose only quiescent marking holds sink tokens is Proven deadlock-free via the coloured Route A encoding) and AC2 (removing the drain turns it Violated) are verdicts of the coloured plan: the quiescence term they read is line 6, the verdicts come with the soundness line (wave W9) and the test fixtures (kind Q).
AC3 (Route A and Route B agree on every small fixture both decide) is differential testing, kind Q.

AC4 (a net with no covering weighting falls back rather than a false Proven; a refund to a non-minting place stays bounded) and AC5 (a leaky co-mint fan-out falls back) are line 1: with no scaled cover at any k the bound answers nothing (NU_053_infeasible). The relay that refunds the minting budget is NU_053_relayRefund (no plan) and the refund to a place that does not mint is NU_053_otherRefund (lines 1 and 2: every bound that meets NU-053 answers 1). The fallback itself is the pipeline's (wave W10).

AC6 (an optimum below one yields the exact plan with k = 0) is lines 1 and 2: on the fork that consumes exactly(3) budget tokens from one budget token, optimum 2/3, every bound that meets NU-053 answers 0 (NU_053_ac6), and the zero-slot plan is exact (NU_053_zero_exact). That quiescence is then decided and the emitted encoding is well-formed with zero colour slots is the pipeline's and the scripts' (wave W10, kind Q). The remark that an exactly(2) fork refunded by a join has optimum 1 and that an infeasible program is still refused are instances of line 1.

AC7 (the self-loop consumer `spin: a, tick → a, tock` lets placeBound(tock, 0) be Violated) is line 5: the consumer's self-loop column is carried over under its guard, so `spin` can fire; the old update that kept only the '+ 1' is killed (NU_053_forbids_oldConsumer). The verdict itself comes with the soundness line (wave W9).

AC8 (k is the floor of the optimum, identical in every implementation, never larger than the bound of any covering non-negative P-semiflow) is lines 1 and 2 with NU_053_unique and NU_053_le_semiflow: on the exactly(3) fork with a budget of 7, optimum 14/3, every bound that meets NU-053 answers 4 (NU_053_ac8), where every integer cover gives at least 7 (NU_053_forbids_semiflow, NU_053_forbids_integerOnly). The scatter-gather numbers (k = 4 against 10) and that encodeScripts() emits k without a solver ([VER-013] AC1) are fixture checks, kind Q.

AC9 (a weighting is used only after the exact re-check; a negative weight, a weight below one on a coloured place, an increasing transition or a bound above 2^31 − 1 refuses the plan with the re-check report line; a reset or consume-all arc on an uncoloured place does not refuse the plan by itself) is lines 3 and 4 with their mutants. Its example (mint: budget → a, b, join: a, b → budget and cancel: r → r2 with a reset arc on budget, from {budget: 2, r: 1}) has k = 4 in every bound that meets NU-053 (NU_053_ac9_reset, lines 1 and 2; the reset place carries weight, no H1). The report line text is kind N.

The test derivation (a co-mint to join net Proven deadlock-free via Route A while its name-partition graph truncates; an EXTENDED drain-steal net Violated; the routes agreeing on the no-stall net) is AC1 to AC3 with the dispatch, wave W10; its scatter-gather k = 4 is a fixture check (kind Q), its exactly(3) fork with k = 0 is NU_053_ac6 and its reset arc that keeps the plan is NU_053_ac9_reset.

requirements.title: Name Alignment
requirements.statement:
fun A ↦
  ∀ (co : List PlaceId) (β : Type) (ps : List PlaceId) (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),
    ps ≠ [] →
      (A co β ps S = true ↔
        ∀ p ∈ ps,
          ∀ q ∈ ps,
            ∀ (s t : ℕ),
              Novel.RouteB.resident co p S.m s = true →
                Novel.RouteB.resident co q S.m t = true → s = t)
requirements.scope: every verifier that offers NameAligned or QuiescentNameAligned (MAY); the predicate on a class of the Route B graph
reading: For every coloured set co, base type β, non-empty list ps and class S of the graph, the check A answers true exactly when any name-symbol s resident in a place p of ps and any name-symbol t resident in a place q of ps, p = q allowed, are equal.
quotes: For places `p` and `q` of `S`, the same place included, and the name-symbols `s` and `t`: `s` resident in `p` and `t` resident in `q` imply `s = t`.
An empty place imposes nothing, but a place holding two names violates it whatever the others hold, so the singleton `NameAligned(p)` says that `p` never holds two names.

*Where* name alignment is offered, `NameAligned(S)` for a non-empty `S` *shall* hold on a class of the graph exactly when, for places `p` and `q` of `S`, the same place included, every name-symbol resident in `p` equals every name-symbol resident in `q`.
The predicate compares names only for equality, so it is invariant under any permutation of the name-symbols.
It is therefore a function of the canonical key of a class ([VER-012] AC2), and deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph.
Its places compare by name, and a place listed twice counts once, at its first occurrence, so `NameAligned(box, list, box)` is `NameAligned(box, list)`.
The order of `S` changes no verdict; it fixes the description and which place a reason names.
assumes: The model is a class of the Route B graph (NState co β, Graph.lean): a base b, a name layer m giving each name-symbol and each coloured place (a position of co) a count, and a bound above every live symbol. A name-symbol s is resident in p when its count there is not 0 (Name.lean resident). The NameAligned bullet speaks of a marking; its EARS restatement and the line speak of a class of the graph, which is where Route B evaluates the predicate. A marking's names are read on its coloured places through the one projection nameOf: its class is its name view (view co nameOf m), and on that view the line is the statement that all tokens in the places of S carry one name (alignedAll_view_iff, cited). Places are PlaceId, so 'its places compare by name' is equality of ids, and the check takes S as a list.

The line is the definition of the NameAligned bullet (its second and third sentences, restated by the EARS sentence): self pairs included, so a place holding two names fails whatever the others hold, and an empty place has no resident symbol and imposes nothing. The QuiescentNameAligned bullet reads 'the same predicate'; where it is read is NU_055_sound's subject. The first sentence of the NameAligned bullet ('in every reachable marking') is NU_055_sound's.

The permutation sentence, the first half of the canonical-key sentence and the S-order sentences ('a place listed twice counts once', 'The order of S changes no verdict', read on the predicate) are consequences of the line, not lines of their own: the line fixes A on every non-empty list, so A is the shipped check there (NU_055_eq_ref), and NU_055_perm, NU_055_key and NU_055_members derive the three invariances. The spec states them with 'so' and 'therefore', and they get no EARS sentence. The models that break one of them (nu055_symZero, nu055_headOnly) are killed by the line itself. The second half of the canonical-key sentence ('deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph') is also a claim about the verdict: the verdict on a closed graph is the predicate's answer over its classes, NU_055_truncation line 3.

An uncoloured place has no row in the name layer, so nothing is resident there (resident_of_not_mem) and the line holds vacuously for it (alignedAll_uncoloured, cited). That such a place is refused (refusal step 6, 'Coloured places only', AC2) is not a line of this block. It is the later refusal line of this ID, item (4) of the design row in design/nu.md and 'NU-055 line 4' in the plan's W0 Defers, a different thing from any line here: the refusal steps need the pipeline slice of the verifier model (wave W10) and the wording rulings under D20 (clashes nu-c#9, NC-7). The design's mutant 'proves on an uncoloured place' moves with that line.

'A place listed twice counts once, at its first occurrence' also fixes the description and which place a reason names, and 'The order of S changes no verdict' also covers the reason of an Unknown. The description (the Property: line) is N (an API note), and which place a reason names is the refusal order's (wave W10, D20). On the predicate, the only part of the verdict this block models, order and repeats change nothing (NU_055_members).

'An empty S MUST be rejected where it is constructed' and 'S is a non-empty list' are the language API (N): each constructor rejects an empty list (Java records, the TypeScript signature, the Rust panic, the Python ValueError). The line is stated for a non-empty S only, so the block fixes no answer for the empty list, which never reaches a verdict.

AC5 (invariance under name permutation, on a class and that class permuted, and under reordering S) is NU_055_perm and NU_055_members, theorems of the line; its run of the worked example with names minted in another scope ([NU-010]) is a test of the minter (NU-010, NU-011, wave W9) and of the verdict, not of the predicate, and is not encoded.

AC7 ('S is a list'; the cross pair of reply and staged without the self pairs would accept a marking with two stale replies in reply) is the line with self pairs: NU_055_forbids_crossOnly kills the check without self pairs. AC7's construction rules are the API (N, above) and NU_055_members; its descriptions are N; its verdicts and witness lengths on the worked example are tests on the fixtures (Q), as the Route B graph of that net is not computed in Lean.

requirements.title: Name Alignment: soundness
requirements.statement:
fun D Dq ↦
  (∀ (q : AlignQuery) (nameOf : Colour → ℕ) (m0 m : CMarking),
      q.co.Nodup →
        (∀ T ∈ q.net, Novel.RouteB.InFragment q.co T (q.role T)) →
          (∀ T ∈ q.net, Novel.RouteB.GuardFree T.base) →
            (∀ p ∈ q.ps, p ∈ q.co) →
              (∀ (i : Fin q.co.length), m0 q.co[↑i] = []) →
                q.a0 = alpha m0 →
                  D q = Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.proven →
                    Relation.ReflTransGen
                        (Novel.RouteB.NuStepC q.co nameOf q.net q.role q.conflict) m0 m →
                      ∀ p ∈ q.ps,
                        ∀ p' ∈ q.ps, ∀ c ∈ m p, ∀ d ∈ m p', nameOf c = nameOf d) ∧
    ∀ (q : QAlignQuery) (nameOf : Colour → ℕ) (m0 m : CMarking),
      q.co.Nodup →
        (∀ T ∈ q.net, Novel.RouteB.InFragment q.co T (q.role T)) →
          (∀ T ∈ q.net, Novel.RouteB.PosKeys (q.role T)) →
            (∀ T ∈ q.net, Novel.RouteB.GuardFree T.base) →
              (∀ p ∈ q.ps, p ∈ q.co) →
                (∀ (i : Fin q.co.length), m0 q.co[↑i] = []) →
                  q.a0 = alpha m0 →
                    Dq q = Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.proven →
                      Relation.ReflTransGen
                          (Novel.RouteB.NuStepC q.co nameOf q.net q.role q.conflict) m0
                          m →
                        Novel.RouteB.ExecRests q.reap m →
                          ∀ p ∈ q.ps,
                            ∀ p' ∈ q.ps, ∀ c ∈ m p, ∀ d ∈ m p', nameOf c = nameOf d
requirements.scope: every verifier that offers NameAligned or QuiescentNameAligned (MAY), judged against the untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings
reading: For every call q with a duplicate-free coloured set, every transition in the fragment for its role and without input guards, every place of S coloured, and an initial marking m0 whose coloured places are empty and whose counts are q's initial marking, and for every projection nameOf:
if D answers Proven for NameAligned(S), then in every marking m that NuStepC reaches from m0, any two tokens in places of S, the same place allowed, carry the same name;

if, in addition, every join key consumes at least one token (PosKeys), and Dq answers Proven for QuiescentNameAligned(S) with the reapable set reap, then the same holds in every marking m that NuStepC reaches from m0 and at which every transition the executor can fire is reapable (ExecRests reap, the call's own reapable set).
quotes: **NameAligned(S)**, for a non-empty list `S` of places: in every reachable marking, the places of `S` together hold at most one distinct name.
**QuiescentNameAligned(S)**: the same predicate, read only in the reachable quiescent markings.

Lean `Novel/RouteB/Aligned.lean` (`routeB_untimed_nameAligned_sound`, `routeB_untimed_quiescentNameAligned_sound`) proves: for the **untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings**, a `Proven` of either property holds in every marking that executor reaches (for the quiescent form, every marking at which it rests): the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name.

*If* the premises above hold, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `NameAligned(S)` only if the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name in every marking the untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings reaches.

*If* the premises above hold, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `QuiescentNameAligned(S)` only if the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name in every marking that the untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings reaches and rests at, resting being read with the reapable set of the call ([VER-002]).
assumes: The executor is Novel's NuStepC (Sim.lean): untimed, environment-free, one atomic firing per step, a coloured consumer taking any resident name (ruling D16 is why that differs from EXEC-010's FIFO). It is the executor the Soundness paragraph names. It is not the reference ν firing: RefNu and its reachability RefNuReach do not exist yet. Design correction S7 (a) states this line over RefNuReach once the bridge B1 (Reference/NuLink.lean, wave W9) exists; that changes the statement and its hash, so the block stays pending until then.

The premises are hypotheses (design correction S6), one per premise bullet of the Soundness paragraph: 'the coloured places start empty' (hempty); 'every place of S coloured' (ps ⊆ co; in the shipped verifier the refusal enforces it, which is the refusal line of wave W10); 'the conditions the classifier establishes (InFragment)', 'unguarded inputs' (GuardFree) and, for the quiescent form, PosKeys. The contracts of the mints and coloured consumers (NU-010, NU-051, NU-054), the projection contract of NU-050 (one projection nameOf, Exec.ProjCoherent) and one token per output place of the firing's branch (IO-016 AC4) are built into NuStepC, as the Soundness paragraph says. Conflict-only priority (NU-052) is the conflict flag of the call, read by NuStepC through the same prune.

Two hypotheses are not spec premises and get no premise bullet. q.co.Nodup says the list the call holds is a set: the spec's coloured set is a set, and the classifier's coloured order (Rust coloured_order, the co of the Lean theorems) lists each place once. q.a0 = alpha m0 says the call's initial counts are those of m0, the marking the runs start from. Neither narrows the claim about a call the shipped pipeline makes.

The lines ask soundness for every coloured set and role assignment that meets InFragment, not only for the classifier's. That is the premise bullet as written ('the conditions the classifier establishes (InFragment)', a condition, not the classifier), and Route B alone takes co and role as inputs; the classifier's own output meets InFragment (classifyS_inFragment, Novel/RouteB/Classify.lean, NU-051). That the coloured set is the one the classifier computes for the call, not one the caller names, is the pipeline's (wave W10).

The lines are soundness only: a decider that never answers Proven meets them. That a closed graph none of whose classes violates gives Proven is NU_055_truncation line 3, on the verdict function; whether a Proven or a Violated of the deciders is exact against the executor (VER-012's 'exact (sound and complete)', clash ver-d#1) waits for ruling D59.

The deciders are AlignDecider (glossary GlossaryNuVer.lean, witness refNameAligned) and QAlignDecider (here, witness refQuiescentNameAligned): Route B alone, from the initial class, with no refusal step and no routing. The quiescent line reads resting with the call's reapable set q.reap, the one the decider is given, as the reap-aware quiescence of VER-002 does on the graph. Every refusal of the refusal order (steps 1 to 7: cancellation and budget, an absent place, Bounded(k) outside its premises, in-flight state, the fragment declines of EXTENDED and BASE, an arrival into a coloured place, a modelled environment place, an uncoloured place of S, a marked coloured place), the 'Coloured places only' and 'Modelled injection' rules, 'Route B only' (no other route decides, no NU-053 fallback, no script) and the routing rule that sends these properties to Route B before a budget place, need the pipeline slice of the verifier model (wave W10) and the wording rulings of D20 (clashes nu-c#7, nu-c#9, NC-7, NC-8); they are not encoded here.

Not covered, as the spec itself says: the timed name × time graph the shipped Route B builds (gap R6 of Novel/RouteB/Sound.lean), the all-immediate worked example included; markings with actions in flight (the Lean model has none); faithfulness of a carrier's name to what its token is about, which rests on the unchecked contracts of NU-051.

AC1 (the worked example under EXTENDED: QuiescentNameAligned(box, list) and QuiescentCount Proven, NameAligned(box, list) Violated in 8 firings, the buggy variant Violated in 12, each attributed to Route B) is a fixture test (Q): the graph of that net is not computed in Lean. Its Proven verdicts are the kind lines 1 and 2 make sound; its Violated verdicts and witness lengths are graph facts.

AC2 (an uncoloured or absent place gives Unknown naming it, the first in S) and AC6 (an environment place under AlwaysAvailable gives Unknown naming it, a marked coloured place gives Unknown naming it) and AC8 (the refusal order on the worked example) are refusal steps 1, 5, 6 and 7, wave W10 after D20. AC3 (under BASE the net is outside the fragment, the reason names EXTENDED and the report names the ignored relay declarations) needs the classifier's BASE decline (NU-051, NU-054) on the pipeline, wave W10. AC4 (no other route decides; the script encoders return none) is the pipeline's 'Route B only' rule, wave W10; its last clause (a truncation stays Unknown unless the prefix rule finds a violation) is NU_055_truncation line 2.

requirements.title: Name Alignment: the verdict on a built graph
requirements.statement:
fun V ↦
  ∀ (co : List PlaceId) (β K L : Type) (E : Explorer (Novel.RouteB.NState co β) K L)
    (o : Novel.RouteB.Decide.Out (Novel.RouteB.NState co β)) (ps : List PlaceId)
    (p : Novel.RouteB.Decide.Prop' (Novel.RouteB.NState co β) L),
    ps ≠ [] →
      AlignProp ps p →
        (V (Novel.RouteB.NState co β) K L E o p = Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.proven →
            o.complete = true) ∧
          (o.complete = false →
              (∀ (i : ℕ), Novel.RouteB.Decide.violatesAt E o p i = false) →
                V (Novel.RouteB.NState co β) K L E o p =
                  Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.unknown) ∧
            (o.complete = true →
                o.stopped = false →
                  (V (Novel.RouteB.NState co β) K L E o p =
                      Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.proven ↔
                    ∀ (i : ℕ), Novel.RouteB.Decide.violatesAt E o p i = false)) ∧
              ∀ (i : ℕ),
                V (Novel.RouteB.NState co β) K L E o p =
                    Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.violated i →
                  Novel.RouteB.Decide.violatesAt E o p i = true
requirements.scope: every verifier that offers NameAligned or QuiescentNameAligned (MAY); the verdict Route B reads off a built graph
reading: For every explorer E over classes, every build outcome o, every non-empty list ps and every property p that is NameAligned(ps) or QuiescentNameAligned(ps) over some reapable set, where a class violates p as Decide.violatesAt reads it (for NameAligned a stored class that is not aligned, for QuiescentNameAligned an expanded class at which the net rests and that is not aligned):
if V answers Proven, the graph closed (o.complete);
if the graph did not close and no class violates p, V answers Unknown;
if the graph closed and the build was not stopped, V answers Proven exactly when no class violates p;
if V answers Violated at the class index i, class i violates p.
quotes: It is therefore a function of the canonical key of a class ([VER-012] AC2), and deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph.

*When* the graph closes, Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `NameAligned(S)` exactly when every class of the graph is name-aligned on `S`, and for `QuiescentNameAligned(S)` exactly when every class of the graph at which the net rests is.
A graph that does not close within the class bound never yields `Proven` (Lean `Decide.truncated_never_proven`).
*If* the graph does not close, because the build reaches the class bound, runs out of total budget or is cancelled ([VER-013]), *then* Route B *shall not* answer `Proven` for either property.
*If* the graph does not close and the prefix rule finds no violation, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Unknown`.
*If* Route B answers `Violated` for either property, *then* the class its counterexample ends at *shall* violate the property.
assumes: The model is a verdict function on a built graph (Decide.Out: the stored classes in discovery order, the number expanded, whether the build closed and whether it stopped) and a property (Decide.Prop'), restricted to the two name-alignment properties (AlignProp) on a non-empty S, the only S that reaches a verdict (NU_055's assumes). How the build stores and expands classes is Decide.build's, cited by NU_055_sound through the soundness theorems; it is not a line here.

'Does not close' is o.complete = false: in the shipped build that is the class bound reached, the total budget or a cancellation (cut), or the fuel of the Lean model run out. The quoted Truncation sentence names the class bound only; its EARS restatement names the budget and the cancellation as well, as VER-013 does for every route and refusal step 1 does for a call cancelled or out of budget before it starts. Lines 1 and 2 hold for each cause.

Line 3 is 'deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph', read on the verdict, and its EARS restatement: on a closed graph, Proven exactly when no class violates the property. It needs no open ruling. Ruling D59 asks whether a truncated graph may answer Violated and whether a closed graph's verdict is exact against the executor (VER-012's 'exact (sound and complete)', clash ver-d#1, VD-1); line 3 says only that a closed graph with a violating class does not answer Proven, not whether it answers Violated or Unknown, and that a closed graph with none answers Proven, which holds under either answer. Its premise o.stopped = false rules out only an outcome the build never makes (Decide.loop: a closed build is never stopped).

Line 4 is the EARS restatement of the Violated paragraph's 'to a violating class': the class a Violated names violates the property, for NameAligned a stored class and for QuiescentNameAligned an expanded resting class. The paragraph's first sentence is not quoted, because the line encodes only its 'to a violating class': the rest of it (the shortest path, the attribution to Route B, counterexampleConfirmed absent, counterexampleTiming) is VER-003's and VER-012's report shape and waits for ruling D40 (clash ver-a#11); a Violated is sound for the graph only, not for the executor.

The prefix rule's Violated on a truncated graph (a NameAligned violated by a stored class, a QuiescentNameAligned violated by an expanded class at which the net rests, with the shortest witness and a report line naming the truncation) is not a line: whether a truncated graph may answer Violated is open ruling D59 (NU-050 and VER-012). Lines 2 and 4 hold under either answer, as D59 (b) answers Unknown on every truncated graph. The witness lengths and the report line are Q and VER-003's.
AC4's last clause ('a Route B truncation stays Unknown unless the prefix rule finds a violation') is lines 1 and 2; the rest of AC4 is NU_055_sound's assumes (pipeline, wave W10).

requirements.title: Sparse Enablement Masks
requirements.statement:
fun w C ↦
  (∀ (m : Words), FitsIn w m → (C.compile m = SparseMask.empty ↔ nonZeroOf m = [])) ∧
    (∀ (m : Words) (i x : ℕ),
        FitsIn w m → nonZeroOf m = [(i, x)] → C.compile m = SparseMask.single i x) ∧
      (∀ (m : Words) (es : List (ℕ × ℕ)),
          FitsIn w m →
            C.compile m = SparseMask.multi es → ∀ p ∈ es, p.2 ≠ 0 ∧ wordAt m p.1 = p.2) ∧
        ∀ (needs inhib snap : Words),
          FitsIn w needs →
            FitsIn w inhib →
              FitsIn w snap →
                List.length needs = List.length snap →
                  List.length inhib = List.length snap →
                    C.check (C.compile needs) (C.compile inhib) snap =
                      denseEnable needs inhib snap
requirements.scope: executors that use sparse enablement masks (the precompiled executors)
reading: At word size w, for every mask m whose words are below 2^w:
C compiles m to the empty sentinel exactly when m has no non-zero word;
when m has exactly one non-zero word, x at index i, C compiles m to the single-word form (i, x);
when C compiles m to a multi-word form, every entry (i, x) of it has x non-zero and x the word of m at index i.

For every needs-mask, inhibitor-mask and presence bitmap of the same number of words, each below 2^w, C's presence check on the compiled forms of the two masks returns what the full-width presence check returns: every word of the needs-mask is contained in the bitmap's word of the same index, and no word of the inhibitor-mask shares a bit with it.
quotes: *Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, it *shall* compile a needs-mask or an inhibitor-mask to the empty sentinel exactly when all its words are zero and a mask with exactly one non-zero word to the single-word form holding that word's index and value, and it *shall* put only non-zero words of the mask, each with its index, into a multi-word form.

*Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, its presence check on the sparse forms compiled from a transition's needs-mask and inhibitor-mask *shall* return, for every presence bitmap, the result of the presence check of [CONC-004] computed over every word of both masks.
These two sentences hold for masks and presence bitmaps of the same number of words, each word within the executor's word size.
Enablement results are identical to full-width bitmap checks.
assumes: A bitmap is a list of words, each a natural number, and a word past the end of a bitmap reads as zero (glossary: Word). Every line is stated at a word size w for masks whose words are below 2^w (FitsIn), and line 4 for a needs-mask, an inhibitor-mask and a presence bitmap of the same number of words, as the runtimes build them (W words of 64 bits in Rust and Java, of 32 bits in TypeScript). So a check that reads its words at its own word size meets the line at that size (PERF_042_accepts_trunc); the reference reads unbounded naturals and meets it at every size.

The model is a sparse check (SparseCheck): a compile step from a full-width mask to one of the body's three forms (SparseMask: the empty sentinel, one word with its index, a list of words with their indices) and a presence check on the sparse forms of the needs-mask and the inhibitor-mask. The runtimes compile the forms when the precompiled net is built (Rust from_arc and compile_sparse in precompiled_net.rs, Java PrecompiledNet, TypeScript precompiled-net.ts); a runtime's own encoding of the three cases is read through SparseMask. Line 4 constrains compile and check together, since the check only ever sees compiled forms; a compile slip (the signed 8-bit word index) breaks it as much as a check slip.

Which place sits at which bit of which word is the compiled net's business ([CONC-007]); the join lemma denseEnable_maskCheck shows that, for any injective placement, the full-width check passes exactly when the glossary presence check (MaskCheck, [CONC-004]) passes, so the block needs no placement. [CONC-020] (a dependency) puts the sparse masks into the precompiled net's flat arrays; it bears on the scope only (the precompiled executors), so no line refers to it.

The priority SHOULD is about whether an executor uses a sparse representation at all; the lines bind an executor that does (the Where clause of both sentences, and the spec sentence that says so in words), so for such an executor they are mandatory.

The body sentence 'Enablement masks SHOULD use a sparse representation to avoid scanning zero words in large nets.', the cost halves of its three cases ('skip the check entirely', 'one AND + one compare operation', 'iterate only non-zero entries') and 'This avoids scanning W words when most are zero (common in large, sparse nets).' are about how the check is computed and what it costs, which a pure function cannot show; they are quality properties (kind Q) and are not encoded. The representation halves of the three cases ('Empty (sentinel value)', 'store word index + mask value', 'store only non-zero word indices and their mask values') are lines 1 to 3.

AC1 (empty masks are detected and skipped with no computation) is line 1 for 'detected' (the sentinel stands for exactly the masks with no non-zero word; PERF_042_mutant_listOnly kills a compile step that never emits it) and line 4 for its result (an empty needs form passes and an empty inhibitor form blocks nothing; PERF_042_forbids_emptyBlocks kills a check that reads an empty inhibitor form as blocked). 'Skipped with no computation' is cost (kind Q), not encoded.

AC2 (a single-word mask uses one AND and one compare, no loop) is line 2 for the form (a mask with one non-zero word compiles to its index and value; PERF_042_mutant_noSingle kills, through line 2 alone, a compile step that keeps the sentinel and puts such a mask in a one-entry list). 'One AND and one compare, no loop' is cost (kind Q), not encoded; PERF_042_forbids_signed kills the shipped slip in that compare.

AC3 (a multi-word sparse mask iterates only non-zero words) is line 3 for the form (the multi-word form lists non-zero words of the mask only; PERF_042_mutant_allWords kills a compile step that keeps the zero words) and line 4 for its result (every non-zero word is checked; PERF_042_forbids_firstWord kills a check that reads the first only). That the check's loop walks the listed entries and nothing else is cost (kind Q), not encoded: a check that scans every word of the bitmap on correct forms meets the line.

AC4 (enablement results identical to full-width bitmap checks) is line 4. The test derivation's net with 200 places whose transitions touch 2 or 3 places is line 4 on one net, exercised by the reference in PERF_042_twoHundredPlaces; its 'is faster' is a cost criterion (kind Q).

The check is the presence phase only. The cardinality check and the ν-match check ([CONC-008]) are later phases and are not part of it; reset arcs and output arcs play no part (glossary: Presence check).

requirements.title: Timing Specification
requirements.statement:
fun K ↦
  (∀ (tm : Novel.TimedScg.Timing),
      K.earliest tm =
        match tm with
        | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.immediate => 0
        | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.deadline byMs => 0
        | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.delayed a => a
        | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.window e latestMs => e
        | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.exact a => a) ∧
    (∀ (tm : Novel.TimedScg.Timing),
        K.latest tm =
          match tm with
          | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.immediate => 3153600000000
          | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.deadline b => b
          | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.delayed afterMs => 3153600000000
          | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.window earliestMs l => l
          | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.exact a => a) ∧
      (∀ (tm : Novel.TimedScg.Timing),
          K.hasDeadline tm =
            match tm with
            | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.immediate => false
            | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.deadline byMs => true
            | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.delayed afterMs => false
            | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.window earliestMs latestMs => true
            | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.exact atMs => true) ∧
        (∀ (tm : Novel.TimedScg.Timing),
            (match tm with
              | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.immediate => True
              | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.deadline b => 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 3153600000000
              | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.delayed a => a ≤ 3153600000000
              | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.window e l => e ≤ l ∧ l ≤ 3153600000000
              | Novel.TimedScg.Timing.exact a => a ≤ 3153600000000) →
              K.factory tm = Except.ok tm) ∧
          (∀ (b : ℕ),
              b = 0 →
                K.factory (Novel.TimedScg.Timing.deadline b) =
                  Except.error ("Deadline must be positive: " ++ toString b)) ∧
            (∀ (b : ℕ),
                3153600000000 < b →
                  K.factory (Novel.TimedScg.Timing.deadline b) =
                    Except.error
                      ("Deadline must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): " ++
                        toString b)) ∧
              (∀ (a : ℕ),
                  3153600000000 < a →
                    K.factory (Novel.TimedScg.Timing.delayed a) =
                      Except.error
                        ("Delay must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): " ++
                          toString a)) ∧
                (∀ (e l : ℕ),
                    3153600000000 < e →
                      K.factory (Novel.TimedScg.Timing.window e l) =
                        Except.error
                          ("Earliest must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): " ++
                            toString e)) ∧
                  (∀ (e l : ℕ),
                      e ≤ 3153600000000 →
                        l < e →
                          K.factory (Novel.TimedScg.Timing.window e l) =
                            Except.error
                              ("Latest (" ++ toString l ++ ") must be >= earliest (" ++
                                  toString e ++
                                ")")) ∧
                    (∀ (e l : ℕ),
                        e ≤ 3153600000000 →
                          e ≤ l →
                            3153600000000 < l →
                              K.factory (Novel.TimedScg.Timing.window e l) =
                                Except.error
                                  ("Latest must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): " ++
                                    toString l)) ∧
                      (∀ (a : ℕ),
                          3153600000000 < a →
                            K.factory (Novel.TimedScg.Timing.exact a) =
                              Except.error
                                ("Exact time must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): " ++
                                  toString a)) ∧
                        (∀ (tm : Novel.TimedScg.Timing), K.build tm = K.factory tm) ∧
                          K.defaultTiming = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.immediate
reading: For every timing contract K:
earliest() is 0 for Immediate and Deadline(by), after for Delayed(after), earliest for Window(earliest, latest) and at for Exact(at);
latest() is the maximum duration (3153600000000 ms) for Immediate and Delayed(after), by for Deadline(by), latest for Window(earliest, latest) and at for Exact(at);
hasDeadline() is true for every Deadline, Window and Exact and false for every Immediate and Delayed, whatever the bounds;
a factory called with bounds that satisfy the validity table (Immediate always, 0 < by <= maximum, after <= maximum, earliest <= latest <= maximum, at <= maximum) returns the timing as written;
deadline(0) fails with 'Deadline must be positive: 0';
deadline(by) with by above the maximum (so by is positive) fails with 'Deadline must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): {by}';
delayed(after) with after above the maximum fails with 'Delay must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): {after}';
window(earliest, latest) with earliest above the maximum fails with 'Earliest must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): {earliest}', whatever latest is;
window(earliest, latest) with earliest at most the maximum and latest below earliest fails with 'Latest ({latest}) must be >= earliest ({earliest})';
window(earliest, latest) with earliest at most the maximum, latest at least earliest and latest above the maximum fails with 'Latest must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): {latest}';
exact(at) with at above the maximum fails with 'Exact time must be at most MAX_DURATION_MS (3153600000000): {at}';
building a transition with a timing written out without a factory gives what the factory gives for its bounds: the same message for an invalid timing, the timing unchanged for a valid one;
a transition built without a timing has the timing Immediate ({x} above is the argument in decimal milliseconds).
quotes: `earliest()` *shall* return 0 for `Immediate` and `Deadline`, `after` for `Delayed(after)`, `earliest` for `Window(earliest, latest)` and `at` for `Exact(at)`.
`latest()` *shall* return the maximum duration for `Immediate` and `Delayed`, `by` for `Deadline(by)`, `latest` for `Window(earliest, latest)` and `at` for `Exact(at)`.
`hasDeadline()` *shall* return true for `Deadline`, `Window` and `Exact`, and false for `Immediate` and `Delayed`.
A timing is **valid** exactly when its bounds satisfy these rules, which are canonical for every variant ([TIME-002]–[TIME-006] restate them):

*If* a factory is called with bounds that make the timing invalid, *then* the factory *shall* fail with the message the table below gives for the first rule the bounds break (Rust panics; Python raises `ValueError` with the Rust message; Java throws `IllegalArgumentException`; TypeScript throws `Error`).
The checks run in the order of the table.
*If* a transition is built with a timing written out without a factory and that timing is invalid, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with the factory's message.
Each transition has a timing specification (defaults to Immediate).
assumes: A contract is the accessors, the factories and the transition builder of one implementation over the five variants of the Rust enum (Novel.TimedScg.Timing), with bounds in milliseconds; a call that fails is read as `.error msg` with its message, a call that returns as `.ok`. `factory tm` is the factory of tm's variant called with tm's bounds; `build tm` builds a transition with tm written out directly (a Rust enum variant, a TypeScript object literal, a Java record constructor).

Bounds are naturals, as Rust's `u64` arguments are, so the rows of the message table that check for a negative bound (TypeScript and Java only) and the `0 <=` halves of the validity table are not encoded. The messages are the Rust, TypeScript and Python form, with the argument printed in decimal milliseconds; Java's form (`MAX_DURATION (PT876000H)`, `Duration.toString()`) is the same table in another notation and is not encoded.

'The first rule the bounds break' together with 'The checks run in the order of the table' is encoded by the premises of lines 5 to 11: each line assumes the bounds pass every earlier rule of the variant (only `window` has rules the same bounds can break together; `deadline(0)` and `deadline(by > maximum)` exclude each other). Lines 4 to 11 fix the factory on every timing: a valid one is returned as written, an invalid one fails with exactly one message.

AC1 (each transition has a timing, Immediate by default) is line 13: `defaultTiming` is the timing the builder gives a transition built without one. The default Delayed(0), which has the same interval [0, maximum] as Immediate, is killed as TIME_001_mutant_sameInterval.
AC2 (earliest() and latest() are queryable) is lines 1 and 2; the value table of the accessors is the first two shall sentences.

AC3 (hasDeadline() by variant whatever the bounds, so a Window whose latest bound equals the maximum still has a deadline) is line 3 (ruling D2). The older literal reading 'hasDeadline() is latest below the maximum' is killed as TIME_001_mutant_latestBelowMax, on window(0, maximum). That a transition SHOULD be disabled after its latest bound is keyed on Reapable (Deadline, Window), not on hasDeadline: Exact has a deadline but is enforced softly (TIME-006, TIME-013).
The validity table of line 4 is Timing.Valid, the predicate the timed step, the state-class graph and the TIME-002 to TIME-006 blocks read (time001_valid_iff, cited).

AC4 (the validity table is canonical; the boundary at the maximum duration for every bound, including deadline's by and window's latest, with the table's messages) is lines 4 to 11 (ruling D11). The nonvacuous example TIME_001_nonvacuous checks each boundary named in AC4 and in the test derivation, window(maximum + 1, maximum + 2) included. The old checks (Timing.ValidPre: deadline only 0 < by, window only earliest <= latest, delayed and exact nothing) are killed as TIME_001_mutant_validPre.

AC5 (a timing written out without a factory is held to AC4 and to the factories' other checks, and a valid one builds unchanged) is line 12; TIME_001_forbids_uncheckedBuild is the builder that skips the check and passes delayed(maximum + 1) on to the verifier. Java's records check in their constructors, which the contract reads as a factory and a builder that agree.
A factory returns the timing as written (line 4): a valid window(earliest, maximum) stays a Window and keeps its deadline (AC3); it is not normalised to delayed(earliest).

The two body bullets are the rules of other blocks and are not encoded again: no firing before the earliest bound since the transition was armed is TIME-010 (cited by time001_fire_after_earliest), and reaping a reapable transition once its elapsed time exceeds latest plus the deadline tolerance is TIME-013 (cited by time001_reap_past_latest). That Immediate and Delayed have no finite latest bound and their latest() reports the maximum duration is line 2; reading the maximum as no bound at all is not proven (Novel.TimedScg.Timing, module docstring).

The maximum-duration constant is maxDurationMs = 3153600000000 (time001_maxDuration); Java's MAX_DURATION is Duration.ofDays(36500), the same duration. Java's sixth variant `Unconstrained` is not in the spec and not modelled.

requirements.title: Immediate Timing
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (X : TimedNet N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
    InNet X u →
      TimingOf X u = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.immediate →
        (∀ (s : TSt N) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
            Armed s u → RefFire u s.m d m' → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s' ∧ s'.m = m') ∧
          StaysArmed R X u ∧ ∀ (s s' : TSt N), ¬R X s (TLbl.reap u) s'
reading: For every timed net X and every transition u the net holds under its name, with timing Immediate:
while u is armed, the step relation has every firing of u that the reference semantics has, with the same successor marking;

no step disarms u while it stays enabled (StaysArmed): when the net's names are distinct, every step other than a reap of u, a firing of u itself included, leaves u armed if u was armed before it and is enabled after it;
the step relation has no reap of u.
quotes: *While* a transition with `Immediate` timing is armed, its timing *shall not* stop it from being ready ([TIME-010]).
The executor *shall not* reap a transition with `Immediate` timing ([TIME-013]).
assumes: A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt); a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic, and the relation may be late: a delay may pass any bound. Armed, Elapsed time, Ready and Reapable are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean).

Line 1 is the first 'shall' sentence. Readiness is read through the step relation: a transition whose timing does not stop it is one the relation may fire. Immediate has earliest bound 0 and is not reapable, so it is ready whenever it is armed, at every elapsed time, also past its finite latest() (the maximum duration). The firing order among ready transitions (priority, FIFO) is EXEC-002 and is not part of an atomic step.

Line 2 is the same sentence for steps that would make u not ready by disarming it while it stays enabled, whatever the label of the step; TIME_002_forbids_drop shows a firing of another transition that drops u's stamp, and TIME_002_forbids_selfDrop a firing of u itself that leaves u enabled and unarmed. It is the frame StaysArmed shared with TIME-003 to TIME-006 (GlossaryTime.lean); its exception for the reap of u is empty here, by line 3. Distinct names (NamesDistinct, ruling D10) are needed because stamps are kept per name, so the reap of another transition of the same name would drop u's stamp. A firing that leaves u enabled re-arms it, possibly with a fresh stamp (TIME-012); this line says only that u stays armed.
Line 3 is the second 'shall' sentence: no reap step of u exists at all. Together with line 2 it excludes a reap under another label.

The interval [0, ∞), earliest() = 0, latest() = maximum duration and hasDeadline() = false are the Timing accessors (time002_interval, cited); the reading of the maximum duration as no bound (ruling D11) is what line 1 and line 3 state for the executor.

AC1 (fires immediately when enabled) is read as readiness, line 1, exercised in TIME_002_nonvacuous at elapsed time 0. Line 1 speaks of an armed transition; 'when enabled' becomes 'when armed' only through TIME-010 (a transition enabled in the initial marking or after a firing that writes one of its arc places is newly armed) and TIME-012, which ConsistencyTime conjoins: an executor that never arms a newly enabled Immediate transition meets this block on its own. That it fires on the next cycle, before any other ready transition, is the eager Phase 2 executor's and EXEC-002's, not an atomic step's (ruling D3). AC2 (no deadline enforcement) is lines 2 and 3, exercised in TIME_002_nonvacuous past the maximum duration plus the tolerance, where u is still armed, still fires and has no reap.

requirements.title: Deadline Timing
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (X : TimedNet N) (u : Reference.Trans N) (b : ℕ),
    InNet X u →
      TimingOf X u = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.deadline b →
        (∀ (s : TSt N) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
            Armed s u →
              ¬b + Tolerance X < Elapsed s u →
                RefFire u s.m d m' → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s' ∧ s'.m = m') ∧
          (while fun s ↦ Armed s u ∧ b + Tolerance X < Elapsed s u, never fun s s' ↦
              ∃ d, R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧
            (∀ (s : TSt N),
                Armed s u →
                  b + Tolerance X < Elapsed s u → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.reap u) s') ∧
              (on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.reap u) s', shall fun s s' ↦
                  Armed s u ∧ b + Tolerance X < Elapsed s u ∧ ¬Armed s' u) ∧
                ClockFrame R X u
reading: For every timed net X and every transition u the net holds under its name, with timing Deadline(by):
while u is armed and its elapsed time is not greater than by plus the tolerance, the step relation has every firing of u that the reference semantics has, with the same successor marking;
no firing of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is greater than by plus the tolerance;
from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is greater than by plus the tolerance, the step relation has a reap of u;
a reap of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is greater than by plus the tolerance, and leaves u not armed;

u's clock is framed (ClockFrame): when the net's names are distinct, no step but the reap of u disarms u while it stays enabled, and a delay, the reap of a transition of another name, and a firing of a transition of another name that leaves u enabled in its intermediate marking and after it keep u's stamp.
quotes: *While* a transition with `Deadline(by)` timing is armed, its timing *shall not* stop it from being ready until it is expired.
*If* a transition with `Deadline(by)` timing is armed and its elapsed time exceeds `by` plus the deadline tolerance, *then* the executor *shall* reap it ([TIME-013]).
assumes: A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt); a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic, and the relation may be late: a delay may pass any bound. Armed, Elapsed time, Expired, Reaped and Deadline tolerance are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean). For a Deadline(by) transition, expired is exactly armed with an elapsed time strictly greater than by plus the tolerance, since Deadline is reapable and its latest bound is by.

Line 1 is the first 'shall' sentence. Readiness is read through the step relation: a transition whose timing does not stop it is one the relation may fire. Its earliest bound is 0, so the only timing obstacle is expiry, and line 1 asks for every reference firing up to and including the bound, so an executor that refuses to fire at the bound is excluded; one that reaps early is excluded by line 4. The firing order among ready transitions (priority, FIFO) is EXEC-002 and is not part of an atomic step.

Lines 2 to 4 are the second 'shall' sentence (ruling D4: strictly past by plus the tolerance, and the tolerance is MUST). An atomic relation cannot say that a reap happens, only that it is available and is the only way out: line 3 is the reap step being available (TIME-013 states the same for every expired transition, its last line), line 2 that the expired transition does not fire instead, and line 4 that a reap happens only when it is expired and disarms it. That the reap happens in the deadline step of the very cycle in which the bound is passed ([EXEC-001] step 4) and emits TransitionTimedOut ([EVT-009]) is the Phase 2 executor's, not this block's.

Line 5 is the frame ClockFrame shared with TIME-004 to TIME-006 (GlossaryTime.lean). Its first part is the first 'shall' sentence for steps that would make u not ready by disarming it: the only step that may take the clock from an enabled Deadline transition is its reap, and a firing of u itself that leaves u enabled re-arms it (TIME_003_forbids_selfDrop). Its other parts read 'elapsed time' in the second 'shall' sentence through the glossary (Elapsed: the clock reading minus the stamp taken when the transition was most recently newly armed): a delay, the reap of another transition and a firing of another transition that leaves u enabled throughout newly arm nothing, so they keep u's stamp. Without them an executor that restamps every armed transition on each delay (TIME_003_mutant_anyStamp_killed), or restarts every armed clock on every firing (TIME_003_mutant_restart_killed), keeps the elapsed time of u from growing in a busy net and never reaps it. That a delay advances the clock by its length is TIME-015 line 2, conjoined in ConsistencyTime. Distinct names (NamesDistinct, ruling D10) are needed because stamps are kept per name. Under ruling D6 an injected token also writes arc places, but injection is not a step of the Phase 1 relation.

The body sentence that the transition must fire within by (plus the tolerance) is not a property of the executor, which may be late (ruling D3): the executor reaps instead. The strongly urgent reading, under which time cannot pass beyond the latest bound of an enabled transition, is the verification semantics (Novel.TimedScg.TStep, timed_run_sound) and is not encoded here.

Construction (0 < by <= maximum duration) is TIME-001 AC4 (ruling D11), a property of Timing.Valid, not of the step relation (time003_construction, cited); the interval, earliest() = 0, latest() = by and hasDeadline() = true are the Timing accessors (time003_interval, cited).

AC1 (fires immediately after enablement) is line 1 at elapsed time 0, exercised in TIME_003_nonvacuous. AC2 (a transition still armed past by plus the deadline tolerance does not fire after that bound; if it is still armed on the first cycle whose elapsed time is strictly greater than the bound, it is reaped in that cycle) is lines 2 to 4, exercised in TIME_003_nonvacuous with Deadline(5000 ms) and tolerance 5 ms: u fires at elapsed 5005 and cannot be reaped there, and at 5006 it cannot fire, is reaped and is no longer armed. Its first sentence is the safety line 2 (no firing past the bound). Its second sentence is conditional on u still being armed, so a competitor that disables u before its bound does not falsify it ([TIME-011]); on the step relation it is lines 3 and 4, the reap offered in every state strictly past the bound and in no other. That the reap happens in the first such cycle is a property of the cycle loop ([EXEC-001] step 4), which the atomic Phase 1 relation does not have, and is deferred to Phase 2 (RefExec). The test derivation's 'verify transition disabled' after the reap is the reaped transition staying unarmed: across delays and other reaps by line 5, across a firing that writes none of its arc places by TIME-010 line 1 and TIME-013, so it is covered only jointly, in ConsistencyTime. The TransitionTimedOut event of AC2 is EVT-009, deferred to Phase 2.

requirements.title: Delayed Timing
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (X : TimedNet N) (u : Reference.Trans N) (a : ℕ),
    TimingOf X u = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.delayed a →
      (while fun s ↦ Armed s u ∧ Elapsed s u < a, never fun s s' ↦
          ∃ d, R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧
        (∀ (s : TSt N) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
            InNet X u →
              Armed s u →
                a ≤ Elapsed s u →
                  RefFire u s.m d m' → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s' ∧ s'.m = m') ∧
          (∀ (s s' : TSt N), ¬R X s (TLbl.reap u) s') ∧ (InNet X u → ClockFrame R X u)
reading: For every timed net X, every transition u and every bound a such that u's timing is Delayed(a):
no firing of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is below a (this restates [TIME-010] line 4 for this timing);
from every state in which u, the net's transition of its name, is armed and its elapsed time is at least a, every reference firing of u is a step, to the marking that firing gives;
no step reaps u;

when u is the net's transition of its name, its clock is framed (ClockFrame): when the net's names are distinct, no step but a reap of u disarms u while it stays enabled, a firing of u itself included, and a delay, the reap of a transition of another name, and a firing of a transition of another name that leaves u enabled in its intermediate marking and after it keep u's stamp.
quotes: *While* a transition with `Delayed(after)` timing is armed and its elapsed time is less than `after`, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* a transition with `Delayed(after)` timing is armed and its elapsed time is at least `after`, its timing *shall not* stop it from being ready.
The executor *shall not* reap a transition with `Delayed` timing ([TIME-013]).
assumes: A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic. Armed, Elapsed time, Reapable and Reaped are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean); bounds are in milliseconds.

Line 2 reads 'its timing shall not stop it from being ready' on the step relation: a Delayed transition that is armed and past its bound is ready (glossary: Ready; Delayed is not reapable, so it is never expired), and a ready transition can take every reference firing it has, as Covers says for all transitions. Line 2 is that coverage for this timing, so the step relation may not refuse such a firing for a timing reason. Choosing among several ready transitions (priority, FIFO) is [EXEC-002] and [TIME-014]; the atomic step relation of Phase 1 has no such choice.

Lines 3 and 4 read 'shall not reap' with the glossary meaning of reaping, to disarm without firing: no step labelled as a reap of u (line 3), and the frame ClockFrame shared with TIME-003, TIME-005 and TIME-006 (line 4, GlossaryTime.lean). Its first part, StaysArmed, says no step leaves u enabled and unarmed (reaped, in the glossary's state reading), a firing of u itself included: a firing of u that leaves u enabled re-arms it (TIME_004_forbids_selfDrop). Its other parts keep u's stamp across a delay, a reap of another name and a firing of another name that leaves u enabled throughout; the last is [TIME-012] line 2 specialised to u: without it a firing of an unrelated transition could drop u's clock, a reap hidden in a firing (TIME_004_mutant_dropClean_killed), or restart it, which pushes u's bound back so that its timing stops it from being ready (TIME_004_mutant_restart_killed). A firing that disables u in its intermediate marking or after it drops or restarts u's clock as [TIME-011] and [TIME-012] say, and which stamp a firing of u itself leaves (a fresh one) is [TIME-012] line 4; this block fixes neither. A reap labelled with a transition other than u that carries u's name is not constrained by line 3: it is excluded by [TIME-013] line 1 (only a transition of the net is reaped) together with NamesDistinct (ruling D10). That a delay advances the clock by its length is [TIME-015] line 2.
